# The ground rules

One line per rule, and the link to the rule that owns it. Generated from `docs/rules/` by `python tools/rules.py --render`.


## Programs

- **Novis is built for web applications of every kind, with command-line tooling second** — Novis is for web applications — not a segment, not a vertical, not a trust posture. ([`programs/audience`](rules/programs.md#programs-audience))
- **Novis claims three things, and "faster than PHP" is not one of them** — Novis claims exactly three things about itself, and each is a property no incumbent can add later:… ([`programs/three-claims`](rules/programs.md#programs-three-claims))
- **The PHP-shaped syntax is an on-ramp, and no document may promise compatibility** — The PHP-shaped syntax is an on-ramp. ([`programs/no-compatibility-promise`](rules/programs.md#programs-no-compatibility-promise))
- **When two slices compete, the one that gets a working application sooner wins** — When two slices compete for a session, the one that gets a working web application sooner wins. ([`programs/slice-ranking`](rules/programs.md#programs-slice-ranking))
- **Memory buys security, correctness, latency and simplicity — bounded, attributable and stated** — When a design trades memory footprint against security, semantics, latency or simplicity, Novis pays the memory. ([`programs/memory-priority`](rules/programs.md#programs-memory-priority))
- **`Core\Program::implementing<T>()` is the one enumeration, and it expands while compiling** — It expands, while compiling, to an array literal of `new` expressions — one per non-abstract class in the program implementing `T`, **sorted by fully-qualified name**, so the order never depends on filesystem enumeration. ([`programs/implementing`](rules/programs.md#programs-implementing))
- **A compile target changes the host context, never the language** *(designed)* — Every compile target shares one front end, one resolver, one type checker and one IR. ([`programs/compile-target`](rules/programs.md#programs-compile-target))
- **A name reaches its file while compiling; there is no runtime loader of any kind** — Nothing in Novis loads code in response to a name being referenced at run time. ([`programs/no-runtime-autoload`](rules/programs.md#programs-no-runtime-autoload))
- **`autoload` maps a prefix to roots, resolved relative to the file that declares it** — `autoload` is a top-level declaration in two forms, both taking **literal strings only**:… ([`programs/autoload`](rules/programs.md#programs-autoload))
- **A file reached by autoload declares exactly one thing, named for the file** — A file loaded through an autoload root contains exactly one top-level declaration — class, interface, enum or `type` alias — whose name matches the file's base name. ([`programs/one-declaration-per-autoloaded-file`](rules/programs.md#programs-one-declaration-per-autoloaded-file))
- **A `require` path is compared against the on-disk entry exactly, on every OS** — A `require` with a literal path resolves, and the resolved real path is then compared component-wise against the path as written. ([`programs/path-case`](rules/programs.md#programs-path-case))
- **`Core\Program::id()` is 64 hex characters naming this program's code and environment** — `BLAKE3(unit content hashes in program order ‖ env_hash)`, rendered as all 32 bytes in lowercase hex — 64 characters, never truncated by the runtime, because a caller that wants eight of them can take eight and one that… ([`programs/program-id`](rules/programs.md#programs-program-id))
- **A bundled executable is one trust domain: a program, never a service** — `nvs build --compile` ships a runnable *program*, not a deployable *service*. ([`programs/bundle-trust-domain`](rules/programs.md#programs-bundle-trust-domain))
- **Novis ships the framework, split by the standard-library placement tests** *(designed)* — Novis ships a working web framework. ([`programs/first-party-framework`](rules/programs.md#programs-first-party-framework))
- **The privileged half of the framework is `Core`, compiled into the binary** — The privileged half is compiled into the binary, and every entry is placed by a standard-library tier test rather than by convenience:… ([`programs/framework-core-half`](rules/programs.md#programs-framework-core-half))
- **The opinionated half is `nvs/web`, a first-party package providing the `Web` namespace** *(designed)* — The opinionated half is `nvs/web`, a first-party package fetched, locked, logged and granted exactly like any other, and bound by every package rule — including the one that makes a breaking release a new package name. ([`programs/framework-web-package`](rules/programs.md#programs-framework-web-package))
- **The framework has no ORM, no runtime container, and no second way to do anything** *(designed)* — becomes a declared class and nothing is lazy. ([`programs/framework-refusals`](rules/programs.md#programs-framework-refusals))
- **No migration runner ships until migration semantics are decided** *(designed)* — `Web\Migration` has a place in the package roster and **no semantics**. ([`programs/no-migration-runner`](rules/programs.md#programs-no-migration-runner))
- **`nvs new` writes an application that runs before it is edited** *(designed)* — `nvs new <name>` writes an application that **runs before it is edited**: a manifest depending on `nvs/web` alone with its generated lockfile, one `#[Route]` controller returning a view, one `#[Route]` returning JSON fr… ([`programs/nvs-new`](rules/programs.md#programs-nvs-new))

## Types

- **Every binding declares its type, and no binding's type ever changes** — Every binding site carries a written type. ([`types/declaration`](rules/types.md#types-declaration))
- **`var` takes a local's type from its initializer and fixes it there for good** — `var $name = expr;` declares a local without writing its type. ([`types/var-inference`](rules/types.md#types-var-inference))
- **The type grammar is a closed set of atoms under unions and intersections** — Unions are canonicalised — flattened, de-duplicated, order-insensitive — so `int|string` and `string|int|int` are one type. ([`types/grammar`](rules/types.md#types-grammar))
- **An integer literal is decimal, `0x`, `0o` or `0b`, and a leading zero is not a radix** — An integer literal is written decimal, `0x`, `0o` or `0b` — either case of the prefix letter, with `_` separators allowed between digits. ([`types/integer-literals`](rules/types.md#types-integer-literals))
- **A numeric literal is untyped until it is placed, and `as T` is a placing position** — A numeric literal is **untyped until it is placed**, and takes its type from the position it appears in. ([`types/numeric-literal-placement`](rules/types.md#types-numeric-literal-placement))
- **`uint` is a distinct unsigned 64-bit integer, and it costs no bytes a value did not already hold** — `uint` is an unsigned 64-bit integer, `0 … 2^64−1`. ([`types/uint`](rules/types.md#types-uint))
- **An arithmetic operator answers in its operands' own type, and overflow throws rather than wrapping or promoting** — The arithmetic rows are a **closed** list. ([`types/arithmetic`](rules/types.md#types-arithmetic))
- **An `int` or `uint` widening into a `float` position is the only implicit conversion in the language** — Implicit conversion happens in exactly one place: an `int` or `uint` **widening into a `float` position** — an argument, a return, an assignment, or the far side of an arithmetic operator. ([`types/implicit-widening`](rules/types.md#types-implicit-widening))
- **`decimal` is an exact scalar of 96 mantissa bits and a scale of 0 to 28** — `decimal` is a scalar: a sign, a 96-bit unsigned mantissa, and a scale of 0 to 28 giving the digits after the point. ([`types/decimal`](rules/types.md#types-decimal))
- **Only the types the table orders may be ordered, and two objects need `Comparable`** — `< <= > >= <=>` are defined on a **closed** list of operand pairs, and refused everywhere else:… ([`types/ordering`](rules/types.md#types-ordering))
- **A `string` is valid UTF-8 for its whole lifetime, and its unmarked unit is the grapheme cluster** — A `string` cannot hold invalid UTF-8 at any point in its lifetime. ([`types/string-is-utf8`](rules/types.md#types-string-is-utf8))
- **`bytes` is a primitive peer to `string` for data that carries no encoding** — `bytes` is a primitive scalar, peer to `string`, for data with no encoding at all — a file's contents, a socket read, a hash digest, a request body before anyone has claimed it is text. ([`types/bytes`](rules/types.md#types-bytes))
- **`1h30m` is a `Core\Time\Duration` constant, in one grammar shared by source, `parse` and `nvs.toml`** — errors naming this rule, so there is exactly one spelling of any given constant. ([`types/duration-literal`](rules/types.md#types-duration-literal))
- **A `string` or `int` literal is its own type, and a union of them is a closed set** — A `string` literal and an `int` literal are each their own type — the singleton type inhabited by that exact value — parsed only in type position, the way `array<T>` is. ([`types/literal-types`](rules/types.md#types-literal-types))
- **A scalar class constant used as a type folds to its own literal type** — `ClassName::CONST_NAME`, written where a type is expected, resolves at compile time to the constant's own value — exactly as long as that value is a `string` or `int` compile-time constant. ([`types/constant-in-type-position`](rules/types.md#types-constant-in-type-position))
- **An enum case used as a type is a narrowed subtype of its enum, never its backing integer** — `EnumName::CaseName`, written where a type is expected, does **not** resolve to its backing integer. ([`types/enum-case-type`](rules/types.md#types-enum-case-type))
- **An array is PHP's ordered hash with `string` keys and a declared element type** — The container is PHP's insertion-ordered hash with copy-on-write value semantics, unchanged. ([`types/arrays`](rules/types.md#types-arrays))
- **Three combining members treat every key alike, and `array + array` does not compile** — Three members combine arrays, and each walks its arguments left to right treating **every key the same way**:… ([`types/array-combination`](rules/types.md#types-array-combination))
- **`{preserveKeys: false}` discards every key, whatever shape the key has** — Wherever the `{preserveKeys: …}` option appears — `slice`, `chunk`, `reverse`, the sorts —… ([`types/preserve-keys`](rules/types.md#types-preserve-keys))
- **A subscript through a `mixed` is the tag's question; every other base answers it where it is written** — A base that declares an element type is checked where it is written. ([`types/mixed-subscript`](rules/types.md#types-mixed-subscript))
- **`property<T>` is a type whose values are `T`'s public property names, and `as` is its only source** — `property<T>` is a type atom, written in every position a type is written, whose **values** are the names of `T`'s public declared properties — its own and its ancestors' — and nothing else. ([`types/property-key`](rules/types.md#types-property-key))
- **`property<T>` widens as `T` narrows, because the argument bounds the receiver** — A subclass *adds* properties, so `property<Animal>`'s names are all valid on a `Dog` while `property<Dog>`'s are not all valid on an `Animal`. ([`types/property-key-variance`](rules/types.md#types-property-key-variance))
- **`$obj->$key` accepts a `property<T>` and nothing else; a read is the union and a write is checked** — `$obj->$key` and `$obj->{$expr}` are admitted, and **only** when the operand's type is a `property<T>` whose argument the receiver satisfies (`types/property-key-variance`). ([`types/property-key-access`](rules/types.md#types-property-key-access))
- **A union permits only what every member permits, and `mixed` is the one position checked nowhere** — A union permits only the operations valid for *every* member. ([`types/unions-and-mixed`](rules/types.md#types-unions-and-mixed))
- **`$x is T` tests whether a value holds a `T`, answers `bool`, and never refuses because the answer is knowable** — `$x is T` asks whether a value currently holds a `T` and answers `bool`, for any type a value can inhabit. ([`types/type-test`](rules/types.md#types-type-test))
- **Narrowing is flow-sensitive and branch-local, and there are exactly four spellings of it** — Narrowing is flow-sensitive and **branch-local**, and there are four spellings of it: `is`, a `== null` test, a comparison against a literal-typed value, and `match (true)`. ([`types/narrowing`](rules/types.md#types-narrowing))
- **`expr as T` is the only conversion, and it produces a `T` or throws** — There are exactly two ways to obtain a value of a different type: `expr as T`, and a second binding declared at the type you want. ([`types/conversion`](rules/types.md#types-conversion))
- **PHP's `(T)expr` cast does not parse, and the diagnostic names the `as` that replaces it** — `(int)expr`, `(uint)expr`, `(float)expr`, `(string)expr`, `(bool)expr`, `(array)expr` and `(object)expr` are all rejected at parse time. ([`types/no-legacy-cast`](rules/types.md#types-no-legacy-cast))
- **A `type` alias is a transparent, compile-time-only synonym for a type expression** — `type Name = TypeExpr;` declares a compile-time-only synonym for a type expression, written either at file and namespace scope alongside `use` and `namespace` or as a member of a class, interface or enum body (`types/cl… ([`types/type-alias`](rules/types.md#types-type-alias))
- **A `type` alias may not name a single bare class** — A `TypeExpr` that is nothing but one bare `ClassName`, `EnumName`, `self`, `static` or `parent` atom — with no union, intersection, array wrapper or `?` sugar around it — is refused (`E0307`). ([`types/alias-is-never-a-bare-class`](rules/types.md#types-alias-is-never-a-bare-class))
- **A `type` alias is also a member of a class, interface or enum, reached as `Owner::Name` and as a bare `Name` inside its owner** — A `type` alias is also a member of a class, interface or enum body, taking no visibility modifier, reached as `Owner::Name` from anywhere and as a bare `Name` inside its owner's own body, and never inherited. ([`types/class-scoped-alias`](rules/types.md#types-class-scoped-alias))
- **`callable` is satisfied by a closure and by nothing else, and no object is callable** — `callable` is satisfied by exactly one shape of value: a closure. ([`types/callable-is-a-closure`](rules/types.md#types-callable-is-a-closure))
- **`fn` is the only closure literal, with an expression body or a block body** — `fn` is the only closure literal, in two body shapes:… ([`types/closure-literal`](rules/types.md#types-closure-literal))
- **A `callable` type may name its parameters, and must then name its return type** — A `callable` type may name its parameters and its return type:… ([`types/callable-signature`](rules/types.md#types-callable-signature))
- **A closure satisfies a callable type when its arity is at most the type's, matched from the left** — A closure of arity *n* satisfies `callable(T₁..Tₘ): R` when **`n ≤ m`**, and only the first *n* parameter types are compared. ([`types/callable-arity`](rules/types.md#types-callable-arity))
- **A callable's parameters are contravariant and its return type covariant** — A callable type's **parameters are contravariant** and its **return type covariant**:… ([`types/callable-variance`](rules/types.md#types-callable-variance))
- **An unannotated `fn` parameter takes its type from the position the literal is written in** — Where a closure literal appears in a position whose expected type is a callable type, each parameter the literal does not annotate takes its type from the corresponding position of that type. ([`types/callable-literal-inference`](rules/types.md#types-callable-literal-inference))
- **`callable` is the only closure type name, and a callable value is invoked directly** — `callable` is the only type name for a closure value. ([`types/callable-absorbs-closure`](rules/types.md#types-callable-absorbs-closure))
- **A closure captures by value exactly the outer names its body reads, and there is no `use` clause** — A closure captures exactly the outer variables its body reads, snapshotted **by value** at the point the literal is evaluated. ([`types/implicit-capture`](rules/types.md#types-implicit-capture))
- **A closure may carry a self-name, visible only inside its own body** — A closure that needs to call itself may carry an optional name between `fn` and its parameter list:… ([`types/closure-self-name`](rules/types.md#types-closure-self-name))
- **`object` is the opaque top of every class type** — `object` is the opaque supertype of every class type — a named declared class, and the anonymous class an object literal synthesizes (`types/object-literal`). ([`types/object-top`](rules/types.md#types-object-top))
- **`{name: value}` builds an anonymous, methodless object and nothing more** — Each occurrence's precise type is a private, compiler-synthesized class with exactly the fields written, each field's type inferred from its initializer. ([`types/object-literal`](rules/types.md#types-object-literal))
- **`{name: T}` in type position is a structural shape checked by width subtyping, and `{name?: T}` marks a key that may be absent** — A shape type is **not** a class and **not** an interface. ([`types/shape-type`](rules/types.md#types-shape-type))
- **A member reached through an erased receiver is answered at run time, and a failure is a throw** — Three receivers are erased: plain `object`, a shape type asked for a name it does not list, and `mixed` — the widest, because it defers not only *which* class is behind the handle but *whether there is one*. ([`types/erased-member-access`](rules/types.md#types-erased-member-access))
- **`class<T>` is a type whose value is a class descriptor, and `as` is its only source** — `class<T>` is a type atom, written in every position a type is written, whose **value** is the run-time class descriptor — the same word a `new static(...)` already allocates from, carrying the class's name, parent chai… ([`types/class-reference`](rules/types.md#types-class-reference))
- **`class<T>` widens wherever `T` widens, and never narrows without an `as`** — `class<Dog>` widens to `class<Animal>` wherever `Dog` widens to `Animal` — a parameter, a return, an assignment to a wider binding — and **never back**. ([`types/class-reference-variance`](rules/types.md#types-class-reference-variance))
- **Three sites accept a `class<T>`, and every other operand is still refused there** — Three spellings accept a `class<T>` operand, and nothing else:… ([`types/class-reference-sites`](rules/types.md#types-class-reference-sites))
- **`::class` answers the class the value is, and folding is an optimization of that** — `::class` answers the class the value **is**. ([`types/class-constant`](rules/types.md#types-class-constant))

## Expressions

- **Six syntax positions test truthiness; every other `bool` position stays checked** — Exactly six syntax positions test a value's truthiness instead of requiring it to already be `bool`: `if`/`elseif`'s condition, `while`/`do…while`'s condition, `for`'s middle clause, the ternary and elvis condition, and… ([`expressions/truthy-positions`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-truthy-positions))
- **The truthy table is PHP's, and `bytes` is falsy only when it is empty** — A condition resolves PHP's own truthy table, over Novis's type set:… ([`expressions/truthy-table`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-truthy-table))
- **`and`, `or` and `xor` do not parse, and `&&`/`||` are the whole set** — `and`, `or` and `xor` are rejected at parse time, in every position, as `E0226`. ([`expressions/no-keyword-logical-operators`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-no-keyword-logical-operators))
- **A `?T` used directly as a condition is warned about, not refused** *(designed)* — `nvs check` warns when a `?T` is used directly as a condition, naming `!= null` as the fix. ([`expressions/nullable-condition-lint`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-nullable-condition-lint))
- **`==` and `!=` are the whole of equality, and `===`, `!==` and `<>` do not parse** — There is **one** equality operator, `==`, and its negation `!=`. ([`expressions/one-equality-operator`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-one-equality-operator))
- **Equality has one row per type, and every row is the strict reading** — Nothing converts. ([`expressions/equality-semantics`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-equality-semantics))
- **A `mixed` or union operand resolves at run time, and a mismatched pair answers `false`** — `$a == $b` where either side is `mixed` or a union compiles, dispatches on the runtime tags, and applies `expressions/equality-semantics`'s table to the row they land in. ([`expressions/mixed-equality`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-mixed-equality))
- **Two objects are equal only when they are the same object, and no class may change that** — `$a == $b` on two class instances asks whether they are the same object. ([`expressions/object-identity-equality`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-object-identity-equality))
- **Comparing two types that no single value inhabits is a compile error** — A comparison whose two static types are **disjoint** — no single value inhabits both — is a compile error (`E0466`), because the compiler already knows the answer and the author did not mean to write it. ([`expressions/disjoint-comparison-refused`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-disjoint-comparison-refused))
- **A `switch` label and a `match` arm compare by the equality rule and by nothing else** — A `switch` label and a `match` arm are compared against the subject by `expressions/equality-semantics`, and by nothing else. ([`expressions/switch-match-equality`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-switch-match-equality))
- **A literal argument to an intrinsic `Core` call is validated while checking and prepared into the artifact** — A short, closed roster of `Core` methods takes an argument that is really a small program — a regex pattern, a URI, a date format, a duration, a format string, a SQL placeholder list. ([`expressions/intrinsic-literals`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-intrinsic-literals))
- **The intrinsic roster is a closed set in the compiler's own source, and nothing declares itself into it** — The compiler recognises intrinsics by fully-qualified name from a **closed set in its own source** (`crates/nvs-types/src/intrinsics.rs`). ([`expressions/intrinsic-list-is-closed`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-intrinsic-list-is-closed))
- **`list(...)` does not parse; `[...]` is the only destructuring target** — `list(...)` as a destructuring target does not parse. ([`expressions/bracket-destructuring`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-bracket-destructuring))
- **`expr as ?T` yields the converted value or `null`, and never throws** — `expr as ?T` produces the value that `expr as T` would produce where that succeeds, and `null` where it would throw. ([`expressions/nullable-conversion`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-nullable-conversion))
- **`as ?T` is refused where the conversion cannot fail, where none exists, and at every class target** — `as ?T` is available for exactly the conversions the checked form already defines, and is a compile error everywhere else:… ([`expressions/nullable-conversion-availability`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-nullable-conversion-availability))
- **`as ?T` decides `tainted` and `secret` by exactly the rule `as T` uses, and launders nothing of its own** — Nullability and the security qualifiers are orthogonal axes. ([`expressions/conversion-keeps-qualifiers`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-conversion-keeps-qualifiers))
- **A failable single-`string` parse is spelled `tryParse`, and no separate validity predicate stands beside it** — A class whose `parse` takes **exactly one `string`** and can fail also carries `tryParse(string $s): ?T` — `Core\Uri::tryParse` and `Core\Uuid::tryParse` are it today. ([`expressions/try-parse`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-try-parse))
- **The prepared path and the runtime path are one implementation, so preparation is only earlier and never different** — The prepared path and the runtime path **share one implementation**. ([`expressions/preparation-preserves-behaviour`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-preparation-preserves-behaviour))
- **`|>` substitutes one hole at parse time, and has no run-time representation** *(designed)* — `|>` is a binary operator whose right side is an expression containing the hole `$_`. ([`expressions/pipeline-substitution`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-pipeline-substitution))
- **`|>` binds tighter than every binary operator and looser than unary** *(designed)* — `|>` binds **tighter than every binary operator and looser than unary**. ([`expressions/pipeline-precedence`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-pipeline-precedence))
- **The hole is `$_`, it appears exactly once on a right side, and nowhere else at all** *(designed)* — The hole is `$_`. ([`expressions/pipeline-hole-once`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-pipeline-hole-once))
- **An expression-level `catch` is a chain of typed arms guarding one expression** — A `catch` arm is a postfix on an expression. ([`expressions/catch-expression`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-catch-expression))
- **`catch` sits between assignment and the ternary, so one arm guards a whole `??` chain** — `catch` sits **between assignment and the ternary**. ([`expressions/catch-expression-precedence`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-catch-expression-precedence))
- **An arm body is an expression, which admits `throw` and refuses `return` by name** — The arm body is parsed as an expression, and that is the entire rule for what it may hold. ([`expressions/catch-arm-is-an-expression`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-catch-arm-is-an-expression))
- **The result type is the union of the guard and every arm, and an arm is checked from the pre-guard state** — The expression's type is the union of the guarded expression's type and every arm's, computed by the same union the `match` arms use. ([`expressions/catch-result-type`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-catch-result-type))
- **An unbound `catch (Throwable)` arm that supplies a value is warned about** — `W1006` warns on an expression-level arm that names `Throwable`, **binds no variable**, and whose body is not a `throw`. ([`expressions/bare-throwable-arm-warns`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-bare-throwable-arm-warns))
- **The expression form lowers to the block form's landing pad, with the value in a temporary** — There is no run-time representation of the expression form. ([`expressions/catch-lowers-to-block-form`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-catch-lowers-to-block-form))
- **`Name(...)` is the only spelling that takes a reference to a declared member** — `Name(...)` is the only way to take a reference to a declared method or function member: `Core\Str::length(...)`, `$user->getName(...)`, `self::helper(...)` (early-bound) and `static::helper(...)` (late-bound). ([`expressions/first-class-callable-syntax`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-first-class-callable-syntax))

## Statements

- **`<?nvs` is the only code-mode open tag; `<?php` is refused** — `<?nvs` is the only code-mode open tag. ([`statements/nvs-is-the-only-open-tag`](rules/statements.md#statements-nvs-is-the-only-open-tag))
- **A name containing a separator is read from the root, and one without it through the imports** — Given a name as written, and the namespace and import set active where it was written:… ([`statements/a-qualified-name-is-absolute`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-qualified-name-is-absolute))
- **A short name resolves through the imports and then the enclosing namespace, and stops** — A short name resolves through the imports and then the enclosing namespace, and stops. ([`statements/no-fallback-to-the-root-namespace`](rules/statements.md#statements-no-fallback-to-the-root-namespace))
- **A leading separator does not parse, in any of the three positions PHP writes one** — The leading separator is refused in all three positions PHP writes one, rather than stripped:… ([`statements/a-leading-separator-does-not-parse`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-leading-separator-does-not-parse))
- **One function decides what a name means, and there is no second place that does** — Name resolution is `nvs_hir::resolve_ref` and nowhere else. ([`statements/one-function-resolves-every-name`](rules/statements.md#statements-one-function-resolves-every-name))
- **A declaration is reachable under exactly the name it was declared with** — A class, interface, enum, method or constant is reachable under exactly the name it was declared with — its own short name, or a fully-qualified path to it — and under no other. ([`statements/nothing-gets-a-second-name`](rules/statements.md#statements-nothing-gets-a-second-name))
- **An enum's name is an ordinary type, usable at every binding site a class name is** — The `enum` keyword appears only at the *declaration*. ([`statements/an-enum-name-is-a-type-everywhere`](rules/statements.md#statements-an-enum-name-is-a-type-everywhere))
- **`require` is the only file-inclusion construct, and it runs every time it is reached** — `require 'path.nvs';` is the only same-frame inclusion construct. ([`statements/require-is-the-only-inclusion-construct`](rules/statements.md#statements-require-is-the-only-inclusion-construct))
- **Declarations cross a `require` and variables do not** — Every name a required file *declares* — a class, an interface, an enum, a `type` alias — is visible to the requiring file exactly as if it had been pasted in. ([`statements/a-required-file-shares-declarations-not-locals`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-required-file-shares-declarations-not-locals))
- **A `require` used for its value hands back `mixed`, and converts like any other boundary** — `require` is an expression, and `$config = require 'config.nvs';` is its value form. ([`statements/a-require-expression-is-mixed`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-require-expression-is-mixed))
- **`static` marks a class member and names a class-relative type, and nothing else** — `static` is a class-member modifier and a class-relative type. ([`statements/static-is-a-member-modifier`](rules/statements.md#statements-static-is-a-member-modifier))
- **A function holds no state of its own, and `global` does not exist** — Two spellings are refused, and each diagnostic names its replacement:… ([`statements/no-function-static-and-no-global`](rules/statements.md#statements-no-function-static-and-no-global))
- **A program holds state in five declared places, and the list is closed** — Exhaustive by construction. ([`statements/storage-that-outlives-a-call`](rules/statements.md#statements-storage-that-outlives-a-call))
- **An isolate's class statics are its own, and a child cannot reach its parent's** — An isolate's context is built with a **statics base of its own**, and that single word is the whole of "a child cannot read or write a parent static". ([`statements/an-isolate-has-its-own-statics`](rules/statements.md#statements-an-isolate-has-its-own-statics))
- **No variable is ever populated by the host; every superglobal is a `Core` class member** — No variable is ever populated by the host. ([`statements/no-host-populated-variables`](rules/statements.md#statements-no-host-populated-variables))
- **`$GLOBALS` and `$_REQUEST` have no replacement of any kind** — `$GLOBALS` and `$_REQUEST` are dropped with no replacement of any kind: no `Core` class, no method, no later addition under a different name. ([`statements/globals-and-request-are-dropped-outright`](rules/statements.md#statements-globals-and-request-are-dropped-outright))
- **A closure binds `$this` only when its body names it, so `static fn` has nothing left to assert** — A closure binds `$this` only when its body uses it, decided by the compiler. ([`statements/a-closure-binds-this-only-where-it-uses-it`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-closure-binds-this-only-where-it-uses-it))
- **A by-reference binding is written `inout`, in the modifier slot before the type** — `inout` is a reserved word, written **before the type**, in every position a by-reference binding is legal:… ([`statements/inout-is-the-by-reference-spelling`](rules/statements.md#statements-inout-is-the-by-reference-spelling))
- **An argument that binds an `inout` parameter says so at the call** — An argument bound to an `inout` parameter carries `inout` at the call, and an argument bound to a by-value parameter must not:… ([`statements/inout-is-written-at-the-call`](rules/statements.md#statements-inout-is-written-at-the-call))
- **An `inout` argument is a local, and never an element or a property** — `Adder::bump(inout $n)` binds a local. ([`statements/an-inout-argument-is-a-local`](rules/statements.md#statements-an-inout-argument-is-a-local))
- **There is no write-only `out` mode** — `inout` invites the question of a write-only `out` mode: assigned before return, unreadable on entry. ([`statements/there-is-no-out-mode`](rules/statements.md#statements-there-is-no-out-mode))
- **`&` in a by-reference position is refused at parse time** — `&` where a by-reference marker would go is still recognised, so the diagnostic can name the exact fix, and produces an error node — the AST keeps no variant for it. ([`statements/ampersand-is-not-a-by-reference-marker`](rules/statements.md#statements-ampersand-is-not-a-by-reference-marker))
- **`exit` is the only process-termination keyword; `die` is refused** — `exit` is the only process-termination keyword. ([`statements/exit-is-the-only-termination-keyword`](rules/statements.md#statements-exit-is-the-only-termination-keyword))

## Classes

- **No `function` and no `const` may be declared outside a class body** — A `function` declaration and a `const` declaration are legal inside a class body and nowhere else. ([`classes/no-free-functions-or-constants`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-free-functions-or-constants))
- **Every name is compared exactly, so `Foo` and `foo` are two names and never one** — Every name — class, interface, enum, enum case, namespace segment, method, property, parameter, local, class constant — is compared exactly, everywhere resolution happens. ([`classes/names-resolve-case-sensitively`](rules/classes.md#classes-names-resolve-case-sensitively))
- **Keywords, contextual keywords and the `<?nvs` tag are lower case and nothing else** — Keywords are matched exactly: `if` is a keyword, `IF` and `If` are not. ([`classes/reserved-spellings-are-lower-case`](rules/classes.md#classes-reserved-spellings-are-lower-case))
- **No property, parameter or local name may begin with `_`** — No property, parameter or local variable name may begin with `_`. ([`classes/no-leading-underscore-identifiers`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-leading-underscore-identifiers))
- **A constructor is an ordinary method named `constructor`, and `__construct` does not compile** — The constructor is a method named `constructor` — an ordinary lowercase-first name that needs no casing exception of its own. ([`classes/constructor-is-a-method-named-constructor`](rules/classes.md#classes-constructor-is-a-method-named-constructor))
- **A visibility keyword on a parameter promotes it to a property only in the `constructor`** — A `public`, `protected` or `private` keyword on a parameter promotes it to a property, and it does that only in the `constructor`. ([`classes/promotion-is-constructor-only`](rules/classes.md#classes-promotion-is-constructor-only))
- **A `new` through a class reference checks `T`'s constructor, and an implementor whose constructor diverges is refused there** — `new $cls(...)` over a `class<T>` types its arguments against **`T`'s** constructor, exactly as `new static(...)` types them against the current class's. ([`classes/constructor-compatibility`](rules/classes.md#classes-constructor-compatibility))
- **Every property a class declares is definitely assigned on every path out of every constructor** — Every property a class declares is assigned on every path out of every constructor the class exposes, checked by the same flow analysis that already proves definite assignment for locals. ([`classes/definite-property-initialization`](rules/classes.md#classes-definite-property-initialization))
- **There is no `undefined`: a property that may legitimately hold no value is `?T`** — There is no `undefined` type and no `undefined` value. ([`classes/no-undefined-value`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-undefined-value))
- **Reading a property that has never been written throws a catchable error and never yields a value** — Reading a property that has never been written throws an ordinary, catchable `Throwable`, propagated by checked return (`errors/propagation`) rather than routed through `errors/escalation-ladder`'s fatal ladder — it is… ([`classes/an-unwritten-property-read-throws`](rules/classes.md#classes-an-unwritten-property-read-throws))
- **A `lateinit` property is assigned after the constructor rather than inside it** — A property declared `lateinit` is exempt from the constructor-must-assign obligation, for the pattern that obligation cannot express: a container, an ORM, or any setter injection that populates a property after `new` re… ([`classes/lateinit`](rules/classes.md#classes-lateinit))
- **`lateinit` is admitted only on a non-nullable class- or interface-typed property that is neither promoted nor `readonly`** — `lateinit` is admitted only on a non-nullable property whose type is a class or an interface. ([`classes/lateinit-restrictions`](rules/classes.md#classes-lateinit-restrictions))
- **A `lateinit` read the enclosing method can prove is too early is a compile error, and nothing wider is attempted** — The definite-assignment pass runs inside every method, not only constructors, with a `lateinit` property entering in the "not yet proven written" state. ([`classes/lateinit-read-before-write`](rules/classes.md#classes-lateinit-read-before-write))
- **A property that the class does not declare cannot be read or written, and no user code runs for the attempt** — A class's declared properties are its whole property surface. ([`classes/no-dynamic-properties`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-dynamic-properties))
- **`unset` on a declared property is a compile error, and `isset` on one is an ordinary null test** — `unset($obj->prop)`, and `unset(Class::$prop)` with it, is a compile-time diagnostic for every declared property, static or instance, whatever its nullability. ([`classes/unset-is-refused-on-a-property`](rules/classes.md#classes-unset-is-refused-on-a-property))
- **A property's own `get`/`set` hook is PHP 8.4's, unchanged, and every read or write of that property is a call to it** — A property may declare `get` and `set` hooks, with PHP 8.4's syntax, per-property scoping, and its interaction with `readonly` and asymmetric visibility unchanged. ([`classes/property-hooks`](rules/classes.md#classes-property-hooks))
- **A class observes every read and write of its own properties by implementing `PropertyObserver`, never by declaring `__get`/`__set`** — A class observes its own properties by implementing the global interface `PropertyObserver`, whose members are `onPropertyGet(string $name, mixed $value): void` and `onPropertySet(string $name, mixed $value): void`. ([`classes/property-observer`](rules/classes.md#classes-property-observer))
- **A property access runs its hook or its storage first and the observer second, and the observer cannot change the answer** — Every read or write of a property on a class implementing `PropertyObserver` runs two steps in one fixed order. ([`classes/property-observer-pipeline`](rules/classes.md#classes-property-observer-pipeline))
- **A class that implements no `PropertyObserver` pays nothing for one** — Whether a class implements `PropertyObserver` is known at compile time from its declaration, so a property with no hook on a class that does not implement it compiles to a direct field load or store: no branch, no virtu… ([`classes/property-observer-costs-nothing-when-unused`](rules/classes.md#classes-property-observer-costs-nothing-when-unused))
- **A member reachable from two default or delegated sources with no override is a compile error** *(designed)* — A method name reachable from more than one source — a default from one implemented interface, a default from another, or a `by`-delegated interface — is a compile error when the class does not itself declare that method… ([`classes/member-conflict-is-an-error`](rules/classes.md#classes-member-conflict-is-an-error))
- **There is no `trait`: shared behaviour is an interface method with a body, shared state is `by` delegation** — `trait`, a class-body `use Trait, ...;` and `insteadof` are not in the grammar. ([`classes/no-traits`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-traits))
- **A `public` interface method with a body is a default method, and `$this` inside it is the interface** — An `interface` method may carry a body. ([`classes/interface-default-methods`](rules/classes.md#classes-interface-default-methods))
- **A `private` interface method is visible only to that interface's own bodies** — An `interface` method declared `private` and carrying a body is an internal helper for that interface's own method bodies. ([`classes/interface-private-methods`](rules/classes.md#classes-interface-private-methods))
- **`implements I by $field` forwards every member `I` requires to that property** — Each entry in a class's `implements` list may carry a `by $field;` suffix. ([`classes/delegation-by-field`](rules/classes.md#classes-delegation-by-field))
- **Two objects order only when their class implements `Comparable`, and there is no property-walk fallback** — Two objects may be compared with `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` or `<=>` only when their class implements the global interface `Comparable`, whose single member is `compareTo(self $other): int` returning negative, zero or positive. ([`classes/comparable`](rules/classes.md#classes-comparable))
- **`compareTo` fixes the other operand to `self`, so two different classes are never ordered against each other** — `compareTo(self $other)` fixes the other operand to the implementing class. ([`classes/comparable-is-same-class-only`](rules/classes.md#classes-comparable-is-same-class-only))
- **`<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` and `<=>` on two objects lower to one `compareTo` call** — All five relational spellings lower to one call: `$a < $b` is `$a->compareTo($b) < 0`, `$a >= $b` is `$a->compareTo($b) >= 0`, and `$a <=> $b` is the call itself. ([`classes/ordering-lowers-to-compare-to`](rules/classes.md#classes-ordering-lowers-to-compare-to))
- **An object becomes a string only through `Stringable::toString`, and everywhere else is a diagnostic** — An object reaches a string only through the global interface `Stringable`, whose single member is `toString(): string`. ([`classes/stringable`](rules/classes.md#classes-stringable))
- **No method name changes a class's behaviour by being present; every PHP magic method is replaced by a declared interface or gone** — No method name changes what a class does by being present. ([`classes/no-magic-methods`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-magic-methods))
- **There is no `__call` or `__callStatic`: a call to a method the class does not declare is a diagnostic** — Calling a method a class does not declare is a compile-time diagnostic, like any other unresolvable name. ([`classes/no-call-magic`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-call-magic))
- **There are no destructors: cleanup is an explicit method call the holder makes** — Novis has no destructors. ([`classes/no-destructors`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-destructors))
- **A debug dump shows a class's real declared properties and their real values, and no class can change that** — A debug dump shows a class's real declared properties and their real current values. ([`classes/no-debug-hook`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-debug-hook))
- **A copy is either `clone`'s one level or the graph copy, and no class customizes either** — Novis has two copy depths and no third. ([`classes/two-copy-depths`](rules/classes.md#classes-two-copy-depths))
- **`clone` copies an object's declared storage one level deep and shares every object it reaches** — `clone $x` produces a new instance of `$x`'s class and copies its declared storage one level deep, using PHP's own rule for what one level means. ([`classes/clone-is-shallow`](rules/classes.md#classes-clone-is-shallow))
- **The graph copy is one recursive, cycle-safe walk with two carriers, and it refuses what has no meaning on the other side** — The graph copy is a recursive, cycle-safe traversal of a value's reachable structure producing a result that shares no mutable heap state with its source. ([`classes/graph-copy`](rules/classes.md#classes-graph-copy))
- **`Core\Serialize::decode` accepts only bytes this build's `encode` produced, and refuses everything else outright** — `Core\Serialize::encode($x): bytes` runs the graph copy and encodes the result; `decode` runs it in reverse. ([`classes/serialize-is-a-closed-format`](rules/classes.md#classes-serialize-is-a-closed-format))
- **Every encoder that walks a value graph ends a cycle by identity and names the path, never by exhausting a depth cap** — Every encoder that walks a value graph carries the identity of the objects on the path from the root to the value it is writing, and the first value it meets twice ends the walk there — refused, naming the property chai… ([`classes/an-encoder-ends-a-cycle-by-identity`](rules/classes.md#classes-an-encoder-ends-a-cycle-by-identity))
- **A class is reachable under its declared name and nowhere else** — A class is reachable exactly where it is declared — under its own short name, in scope through an import, or by its fully-qualified path — and nowhere else. ([`classes/no-class-alias`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-class-alias))

## Enums

- **A case with no written value counts on from the one before it, starting at zero** — An enum body is a comma list of `Name` or `Name = <integer literal>`, and the optional `: int` or `: uint` before it names the backing type (`enums/one-backing-type`):… ([`enums/declaration`](rules/enums.md#enums-declaration))
- **PHP's `case` keyword does not parse, and each one is diagnosed where it is written** — There is no `case` keyword in an enum body. ([`enums/no-case-keyword`](rules/enums.md#enums-no-case-keyword))
- **An enum declares a new, closed, named integer type** — `enum Status { Active, Banned }` declares a new named integer type with a fixed set of cases, and the enum's name is then a type like any other — a property, a parameter, a return, a local, a class constant, an `array<T… ([`enums/closed-integer-type`](rules/enums.md#enums-closed-integer-type))
- **Every enum is backed by exactly one integer type, and nothing else backs one** — `enum E: int` and `enum E: uint` name the backing type; with no `: T` written it is `int`. ([`enums/one-backing-type`](rules/enums.md#enums-one-backing-type))
- **An enum value costs nothing beyond the integer it is** — An enum value is its backing integer and nothing more — zero additional bytes over what `int` or `uint` already costs, no allocation, no refcount, no descriptor. ([`enums/representation`](rules/enums.md#enums-representation))
- **An enum case is always truthy, whatever integer backs it** — An enum case in a condition is **always truthy**, whatever integer backs it. ([`enums/truthiness`](rules/enums.md#enums-truthiness))
- **A case is an integer constant, and an enum body declares nothing but cases** — `EnumName::CaseName` **is** an integer constant, inlined at every use site the way a literal `5` is: nothing is allocated, nothing is refcounted, there is no descriptor, and there is no per-isolate storage slot for an e… ([`enums/no-class-machinery`](rules/enums.md#enums-no-class-machinery))
- **Reflection describes an enum's shape and grants it nothing a class has** — `Core\Reflect\EnumInfo::of(Status::class)` reports an enum's shape as ordinary structural metadata — the type's name and its closed case list — the same way `ClassInfo` reports a class's shape. ([`enums/reflection`](rules/enums.md#enums-reflection))

## Iteration

- **A `for` init clause is one typed declaration or a list of expressions, never both** — A `for` header's init clause holds **one typed local declaration, or a list of expressions, and never a mix**:… ([`iteration/for-init-clause`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-for-init-clause))
- **A header-declared counter is function-scoped, and a second header declaring it again is refused** — A counter declared in a `for` header is **function-scoped**, exactly as every other binding is. ([`iteration/for-counter-scope`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-for-counter-scope))
- **A refused `for` header is one diagnostic, never a cascade** — Two grammatical refusals, each raised once and each naming the spelling that works:… ([`iteration/for-init-refusals`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-for-init-refusals))
- **`foreach` drives exactly three subjects, and a fourth is refused where it is written** — `foreach` accepts three subjects and refuses a fourth where it is written:… ([`iteration/foreach-subjects`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-foreach-subjects))
- **Two interfaces carry every iteration, and a cursor is `advance()` then `current()`** — Iteration has exactly two interfaces, both reserved names the compiler owns:… ([`iteration/two-interfaces`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-two-interfaces))
- **A class implements a compiler-owned generic interface at a concrete type, and declares no type variable of its own** — Type variables belong to declarations the compiler owns. ([`iteration/concrete-generic-implements`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-concrete-generic-implements))
- **A class cannot make `$obj[$k]` or a count into a method call** — `ArrayAccess` and `Countable` do not exist, and no other interface makes a syntactic form dispatch to a method. ([`iteration/no-magic-collection-interfaces`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-no-magic-collection-interfaces))
- **`current()` outside the protocol throws rather than answering** — `current()` throws a `LogicError` when it is called before the first `advance()`, and when it is called after an `advance()` returned `false`. ([`iteration/cursor-out-of-range`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-cursor-out-of-range))
- **A body that yields is a generator, and calling one returns a state object without running a line of it** — A function whose body contains `yield` is a **generator**. ([`iteration/generators`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-generators))
- **A generator is a lazy sequence and nothing more** — A generator is a lazy sequence in one direction. ([`iteration/one-way-only`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-one-way-only))
- **`yield` appears only in the generator's own body** — `yield` is confined to the generator's own body. ([`iteration/yield-lexical-confinement`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-yield-lexical-confinement))
- **A generator does not cross a boundary and does not clone** *(designed)* — A generator object is not serializable, does not cross a `spawn`, `spawn worker` or `spawn script` boundary, and does not `clone`. ([`iteration/generator-stays-in-one-isolate`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-generator-stays-in-one-isolate))

## Attributes

- **An attribute is a shape literal on a declaration, and nothing is ever declared or instantiated for it** — `#[Name(field: value, ...)]`, or the bare `#[{field: value, ...}]`, attaches an anonymous object literal to a declaration. ([`attributes/inert-metadata`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-inert-metadata))
- **An attribute attaches at four declaration sites, and a named one's name is a shape-typed `type` alias** — An attribute attaches to four things: a class or interface declaration, a method declaration, a property declaration, and a parameter. ([`attributes/attach-sites-and-forms`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-attach-sites-and-forms))
- **Every field value in an attribute payload is a compile-time constant** — Every field value inside a `#[...]` payload is a compile-time constant: a literal, a class constant, an enum case, or `Foo::class`. ([`attributes/payload-is-a-compile-time-constant`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-payload-is-a-compile-time-constant))
- **An attribute may be attached to one declaration any number of times, and attach time never counts them** — The same attribute — named or bare, with the same field values or different ones — may be attached to one declaration any number of times. ([`attributes/repeatable`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-repeatable))
- **An explicit `<T>` at a call site is written for compiler-owned members only** — `Core\Attributes::get<T>` needs `T` supplied at the call site: no argument has a type it could be inferred from. ([`attributes/call-site-type-argument`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-call-site-type-argument))
- **A retrieval matches a payload by the shape it satisfies, never by the name it was attached under** — `T` is a shape type — an inline `{...}`, or a `type` alias naming one. ([`attributes/structural-retrieval`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-structural-retrieval))
- **A retrieval is answered while checking and replaced by its answer, so ambiguity is a compile error** — A declaration's attached-attribute list is fixed by its source, so `Core\Attributes::get<T>` and `::all<T>` are answered by `nvs check` and the call is **replaced** with the answer:… ([`attributes/retrieval-folds-while-checking`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-retrieval-folds-while-checking))
- **`#[Api]` may add to the generated document and may not contradict the code** — `#[Api]` supplies what a handler's types cannot say — tags, error responses, a security scheme, an example — to the OpenAPI document `nvs build --openapi` writes. ([`attributes/api-adds-and-cannot-contradict`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-api-adds-and-cannot-contradict))
- **A method carrying `#[Route]` carries `#[Access]`, and an omission does not compile** — A method carrying `#[Route]` must also carry `#[Access]`. ([`attributes/access-is-a-required-sibling`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-access-is-a-required-sibling))
- **`#[Access]` names one resolvable decision in `allow`, and one of them covers a method** — `allow` is required, and its declared type is `mixed` because the compiler promises not to know what the value means. ([`attributes/access-payload`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-access-payload))

## Errors

- **A limit report is not a Throwable, and the type checker knows it** — The `Throwable` classes are global and are the ordinary `catch` target. ([`errors/throwable-hierarchy`](rules/errors.md#errors-throwable-hierarchy))
- **An error propagates as a checked return, never by unwinding** — Every compiled function and every runtime helper carries one signature, and errors travel in its return value:… ([`errors/propagation`](rules/errors.md#errors-propagation))
- **A throw costs no more than a return, and only its raise allocates** — The marginal cost of `errors/propagation`'s status check is **0.85 ns per frame**, measured as the slope between a 2-frame and an 18-frame chain so the harness's own call-out overhead cancels. ([`errors/throw-is-not-slower`](rules/errors.md#errors-throw-is-not-slower))
- **A runtime helper never unwinds, and a panic dies inside one request** — Because nothing may unwind through a JIT frame, a runtime helper is declared `extern "C"` — never `extern "C-unwind"` — and wraps its body in `catch_unwind`, turning a panic into `FATAL` with the message recorded in `Ct… ([`errors/helper-abi`](rules/errors.md#errors-helper-abi))
- **Recursion is bounded twice: a catchable error, then a fatal** — Novis compiles natively, so every user call is a real machine frame. ([`errors/stack-depth`](rules/errors.md#errors-stack-depth))
- **Tier 1 — a resource limit reaches the request that spent it** — `Core\Fatal::onLimit(closure(LimitReport): void $handler): void` fires only for a resource-limit `FATAL` — memory, CPU time, `max_output`, wall time, `max_script_depth` and call-stack depth. ([`errors/on-limit`](rules/errors.md#errors-on-limit))
- **An allocation past the memory ceiling is refused before it is made, and the refusal is a complete no-op** — An allocation that would carry a request past `[limits] memory` is refused **before** the block is taken, and the refusal is a complete no-op. ([`errors/an-allocation-past-the-ceiling-is-refused-in-front-of-itself`](rules/errors.md#errors-an-allocation-past-the-ceiling-is-refused-in-front-of-itself))
- **A failure escalates through four tiers, and no tier is retried** — Nothing Novis runs is silently dropped, but not everything is *caught* — those are different guarantees. ([`errors/escalation-ladder`](rules/errors.md#errors-escalation-ladder))
- **Tier 2 — an uncaught throw reaches the request root as itself** — `Core\Fatal::onUncaughtThrow(closure(Throwable): void $handler): void` fires when an ordinary `THROWN` propagates through every frame uncaught and reaches the isolate or request root. - **Tier 3 — the configured handler is an ordinary isolate on the engine's own budget** — `[log] handler = 'path/to/handler.nvs'` names a script invoked as an ordinary `spawn script` isolate — fresh arena, fresh globals, its own config overlay, sharing nothing but compiled code — receiving one explicit repor… ([`errors/handler-script`](rules/errors.md#errors-handler-script))
- **Tier 4 — the floor is native, bounded, and gives up rather than escalating** — Hardcoded in Rust, with no script execution — there is nothing left here that could throw, panic or need a further tier, because this is the floor. ([`errors/engine-floor`](rules/errors.md#errors-engine-floor))
- **An internal panic never runs the failing request's own code** — A resource-limit `FATAL` means the *script* asked for too much. ([`errors/panics-bypass-user-code`](rules/errors.md#errors-panics-bypass-user-code))
- **A compile failure is catchable mid-execution and reaches the ladder at entry** — the chance to register anything. ([`errors/compile-failure`](rules/errors.md#errors-compile-failure))
- **Every developer-facing output is one closed record** — Every developer-facing output in Novis is a **record**: an envelope plus a tree of **nodes**. ([`errors/diagnostic-record`](rules/errors.md#errors-diagnostic-record))
- **Five producers build the one record** *(designed)* — Five producers build `errors/diagnostic-record`, and none of them implements a format:… ([`errors/record-producers`](rules/errors.md#errors-record-producers))
- **A record names the file, line and member it was produced at, and a `Throwable`'s location is that same datum** — A record's envelope carries where it was produced — the file as the program named it, its one-based line, and the enclosing `Class::member` where there is one — filled by the producer from a constant the compiler alread… ([`errors/a-record-names-where-it-was-produced`](rules/errors.md#errors-a-record-names-where-it-was-produced))
- **Redaction, control bytes, bidi and elision are decided in the record** — Four transformations are properties of the **record**, applied when it is built, before any rendering sees it. ([`errors/record-transformations`](rules/errors.md#errors-record-transformations))
- **The sink in force picks the rendering, and no call site may name one** *(designed)* — A record is rendered as **plaintext**, **HTML** or **JSON**, and the sink already in force picks which. ([`errors/renderings`](rules/errors.md#errors-renderings))
- **A class cannot change how it is dumped** — There is **no customization hook**: no `DebugRepresentable`, no `__debugInfo`, no per-class renderer. ([`errors/no-render-hook`](rules/errors.md#errors-no-render-hook))
- **A dump goes to the log, and reaches a response body only in development** — CLI dumps go to stderr, not stdout, so piping and redirection keep working while debugging. ([`errors/debug-dump`](rules/errors.md#errors-debug-dump))
- **One write path, and the engine floor is its other caller** — Application code and `errors/handler-script` call this; it is a thin binding over the **same native record-and-write helper** `errors/engine-floor` calls directly when it has no script to run at all. ([`errors/log-write`](rules/errors.md#errors-log-write))
- **Five levels, and the mapping to syslog is fixed** — An ordinary enum, and the syslog mapping is fixed — 7, 6, 4, 3, 2 — because `syslog` is a `errors/engine-floor` target and a severity is not optional there. ([`errors/log-level`](rules/errors.md#errors-log-level))
- **A record's fields are named and typed, not a stringly bag** — `fields` is a **named, typed** structure inside `errors/diagnostic-record`, never `array<string, mixed>` at the core. ([`errors/log-fields`](rules/errors.md#errors-log-fields))
- **A repeat is bounded at the sink that suffers from it: a disk-bounded target coalesces before the write, and an indexed one groups at read time** — A run of identical records is bounded at the sink that would suffer from it, and each sink answers for what is scarce in it: a disk-bounded target coalesces before the write, and an indexed target stores every occurrenc… ([`errors/a-repeat-is-bounded-at-the-sink-that-suffers`](rules/errors.md#errors-a-repeat-is-bounded-at-the-sink-that-suffers))
- **Ambiguous input is refused whole, never repaired** — An input is **ambiguous** when two conforming readers can disagree about what it says. ([`errors/ambiguous-input-refused`](rules/errors.md#errors-ambiguous-input-refused))
- **The closed list of what makes an HTTP message ambiguous** — Refused on a request Novis receives **and on a response Novis's outbound client receives**:… ([`errors/http-message-defects`](rules/errors.md#errors-http-message-defects))
- **A cookie name is bytes, and a prefix is enforced once** — `Core\Request::cookie(name)` matches **byte for byte**. ([`errors/cookie-name-bytes`](rules/errors.md#errors-cookie-name-bytes))
- **A multipart body is capped by part count, not only by size** — `[limits] max_multipart_parts` defaults to **1000**, beside a per-part field-name length and a per-part size. ([`errors/multipart-part-count`](rules/errors.md#errors-multipart-part-count))
- **A path component that does not spell what it resolves to is refused, on every platform** — `Core\IO::within` — the launderer, and the one place the base directory is known — refuses a component that… ([`errors/path-component-refusals`](rules/errors.md#errors-path-component-refusals))

- **`Cli::displayWidth` measures the string the sink will write, in grapheme-cluster columns** — `Cli::displayWidth(string): uint` answers UAX #11 terminal columns for **the string the sink will write, not the one it was handed**. - **The tty belongs to the main task of a CLI program, so a `Core\Cli` member throws in a request and in a spawned isolate** *(designed)* — The tty belongs to the main task of a CLI program. ([`tooling/the-tty-belongs-to-the-main-task`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-the-tty-belongs-to-the-main-task))
- **In-place output is a scoped live region the runtime paints, never a cursor primitive** — `Cli::live<T>(callable(Cli\Live): T $body): T` hands its body a `Cli\Live` with `->set(array<Cli\Text> $lines)`; `Cli::progress<T>(uint $total, callable(Cli\Progress): T $body): T` hands it a `Cli\Progress` with `->adva… ([`tooling/in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region))

- **Raw mode, a hidden cursor and a live region are restored on a throw, a fatal, a panic and a signal** — Raw mode, a hidden cursor and a live region must be undone on a throw, on a fatal, on an internal panic and on a signal. ([`tooling/the-terminal-is-restored-on-every-exit-path`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-the-terminal-is-restored-on-every-exit-path))

([`tooling/commands-are-compiled`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-commands-are-compiled))

- **`nvs fmt` lower-cases a mis-cased reserved spelling only where that spelling has no other legal meaning — a duration unit and the open tag, never a keyword or an identifier** — `nvs fmt` normalizes a mis-cased reserved spelling to its lower-case form only where that mis-cased spelling has no other legal meaning. - **`nvs update-check` always reports the telemetry switch, the local and latest versions, and with telemetry on its upload history; `--json` is stable and the exit status is always 0** *(designed)* — `nvs update-check`'s output always carries whether telemetry is on or off, the local version and the latest released version. ([`tooling/update-check-states-the-whole-picture`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-update-check-states-the-whole-picture))

## The editor

- **The resilient parse is the one grammar's AST plus a trivia layer and an offset index, never a second tree** *(designed)* — There is one grammar and one tree. ([`ide/one-grammar-one-tree`](rules/ide.md#ide-one-grammar-one-tree))
- **Every token and every trivium, concatenated in offset order, reproduce the file byte for byte** *(designed)* — Concatenating every token's and every trivium's source text, in offset order, must equal the file byte for byte. ([`ide/tokens-plus-trivia-reproduce-the-file`](rules/ide.md#ide-tokens-plus-trivia-reproduce-the-file))
- **A node the parser invented says so — `MemberName::Missing` and a spanned `ExprKind::Error` — and an empty span is never the signal** *(designed)* — Where a production synthesises a node at the point of a failure, the node says so. ([`ide/recovery-is-explicit`](rules/ide.md#ide-recovery-is-explicit))
- **The parser always returns a tree, a node it invented says so, and an offset maps to the innermost node even inside a malformed region** *(designed)* — A live editor spends most of its time on a syntactically invalid document — mid-statement, an unclosed brace, a half-typed identifier — so completion and hover that go dark on the first error rarely work when they matter. ([`ide/the-tree-survives-a-syntax-error`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-tree-survives-a-syntax-error))
- **Position encoding is negotiated, every offset conversion lives in `nvs-diagnostics`, and a document's bytes are never normalised** *(designed)* — Position encoding is negotiated per LSP 3.17: the server offers `utf-8` and `utf-16`, takes `utf-8` when the client's `general.positionEncodings` offers it, and falls back to `utf-16`, which is what VS Code sends today. ([`ide/positions-have-one-home`](rules/ide.md#ide-positions-have-one-home))
- **`SyntaxIndex.at(offset)` answers the innermost node and its ancestors, and is rebuilt per analysis** *(designed)* — `SyntaxIndex` is built by one walk over the tree and answers `at(offset) -> NodePath`: the innermost node containing the offset plus its ancestors. ([`ide/the-index-answers-the-cursor`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-index-answers-the-cursor))
- **A full re-analysis of a ~1,000-line document stays under a named bound, and the guard is a test rather than an assumption** *(designed)* — A full re-analysis of a ~1,000-line document stays under a named bound, and the guard has the shape `benches/abi-probe/tests/perf_guards.rs` already uses. ([`ide/a-full-reanalysis-stays-under-a-bound`](rules/ide.md#ide-a-full-reanalysis-stays-under-a-bound))
- **`nvs ast --json` has a frozen node schema, is resilient by default, and its only type-dependent field is a `secret` literal's placeholder** *(designed)* — `nvs ast` gains `--json`, because the AST panel needs a stable shape and `{stmts:#?}` — Rust's derived `Debug` — has none: any field reordering in any AST struct changes it. ([`ide/ast-json-schema-is-frozen`](rules/ide.md#ide-ast-json-schema-is-frozen))
- **`nvs-lsp` and `editors/vscode` are one crate and one package that grow in place; no prototype is built to be discarded** *(designed)* — `crates/nvs-lsp` and `editors/vscode` are one crate and one package across every milestone that touches them. ([`ide/one-crate-and-one-extension-grow-in-place`](rules/ide.md#ide-one-crate-and-one-extension-grow-in-place))
- **`nvs-lsp` is synchronous on `lsp-server` and `lsp-types` — a reader thread, a writer thread, one analysis thread, and no async runtime** *(designed)* — `crates/nvs-lsp` is a library plus a thin `nvs lsp` subcommand speaking LSP over stdio, built on rust-analyzer's `lsp-server` and `lsp-types` — pure Rust, no build script — with `serde` and `serde_json` from the workspa… ([`ide/the-server-is-synchronous`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-server-is-synchronous))
- **Each open document is analysed as its own entry point, with open buffers overlaid on disk, and diagnostics are published only for open documents** *(designed)* — Document sync is `Full` at M4B: a whole-document push per keystroke over a pipe is not the cost that matters when the analysis behind it is a full reparse anyway. ([`ide/an-open-document-is-its-own-entry-point`](rules/ide.md#ide-an-open-document-is-its-own-entry-point))
- **M4B answers nine standard requests and exactly one of Novis's own, M10 adds eight more on the same test, and that test keeps the list from growing** *(designed)* — M4B answers nine standard requests plus one of Novis's own, and M10 adds eight more standard ones and a second of its own, each one admitted on the same test: the data structure the milestone already builds *is* the ans… ([`ide/the-request-set-is-closed`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-request-set-is-closed))
- **The first `nvs lsp` answers six requests and two code actions, and nothing else until the workspace index exists** *(designed)* — The first `nvs lsp` is built on `lsp-server` and `lsp-types`, synchronously, with no async runtime in the workspace. - **The VS Code client goes as deep as the editor allows, and each feature waits for the language or runtime piece it needs rather than shipping as a stub** *(designed)* — VS Code is the reference client and gets real depth, not an LSP passthrough with a grammar file: inspections and quick fixes, refactorings, signature help and workspace symbol search, inlay hints, a native Test Explorer… ([`ide/every-feature-is-staged-behind-its-dependency`](rules/ide.md#ide-every-feature-is-staged-behind-its-dependency))
- **A file with a lexer or parser diagnostic publishes those and its declaration diagnostics, and suppresses its own resolution and type diagnostics** *(designed)* — The front end runs parse → declarations → resolution → types with no gate between the phases, bailing only after the type check. - **The narrowing action answers from a literal in the same file, or it is not offered: no literal, a `mixed` element, or a no-op each hides it** *(designed)* — Three refusals, and each is a soundness question rather than a difficulty one. - **The synthesis is one function in `nvs-types` that no compile path calls, so an array literal stays checked against a target and `var` still refuses a bare one** *(designed)* — The synthesis is a single function in `nvs-types` — a sibling of `check_array_literal`, not a change to it — returning the type an array literal would have if it were synthesized bottom-up, or nothing where `ide/the-act… ([`ide/no-compile-path-calls-the-synthesis`](rules/ide.md#ide-no-compile-path-calls-the-synthesis))
- **The narrowing action is never registered under `source.fixAll.nvs` and never chases the call sites it affects, because it breaks writes it cannot see** *(designed)* — Narrowing a declaration is not a local edit, because `types/arrays`' element type is enforced on every **write**: a binding that was an `array<mixed>` and is now an `array<array<int>>` refuses the `$a[] = "x"` and the `… ([`ide/narrowing-is-a-diff-never-a-save-time-fix`](rules/ide.md#ide-narrowing-is-a-diff-never-a-save-time-fix))
- **Syntax highlighting is a TextMate grammar and a semantic-token provider, each with its own test, and each must cover what makes Novis not PHP** *(designed)* — "Colour" is two deliverables because the two layers fail differently: the grammar has to be right before the server has started, and the server has to be right about things a regex cannot see. - **Nothing Novis rejects is coloured as though it were valid** *(designed)* — Nothing Novis rejects may be coloured as though it were valid. ([`ide/rejected-syntax-gets-no-colour`](rules/ide.md#ide-rejected-syntax-gets-no-colour))

- **The editor completes a value only where the compiler already derives it for another reason, never from a convention scan, an annotation dialect or the network** *(designed)* — `nvs-lsp` contains no framework-specific module, no annotation dialect, no convention scan and no directory-layout knowledge. - **`--REQUEST--` is one line whose argument set is closed per request, and an unknown request or argument fails the case** *(designed)* — `--REQUEST--` is one line: the request name, then optional `key=value` arguments. ([`ide/a-request-line-is-closed`](rules/ide.md#ide-a-request-line-is-closed))
- **`--EXPECT--` is exact and frozen, and every response is rendered by `nvs_lsp::render` so no case invents a spelling** *(designed)* — `--EXPECT--` is exact and frozen, on the same terms as `.nvst`'s: the case's *source* may be corrected freely, its expectation may not be edited to make it pass. - **`.lspt` coverage is inferred from the node the cursor resolved to, never declared, and `every_request_answers_every_construct` names each empty cell** *(designed)* — Coverage is inferred, never declared. ([`ide/lspt-coverage-is-inferred`](rules/ide.md#ide-lspt-coverage-is-inferred))
- **Both tiers run on every acceptance sweep: the headless suites with no editor, and the extension-host run in a pinned build with a throwaway profile** — Both tiers of the extension's tests run on every acceptance sweep, and they answer different questions at costs two orders of magnitude apart. - **The redaction request is one server's to answer for both editors, but the drawing is per-editor and PhpStorm has none until its plugin lands** *(designed)* — `nvs/redactions` is a request on the one server both clients drive, so the PhpStorm plugin can answer it whenever it is built — the range computation is shared, per `ide/redaction-ranges-come-from-the-server`. ([`ide/phpstorm-draws-no-redaction-at-m4b`](rules/ide.md#ide-phpstorm-draws-no-redaction-at-m4b))
- **`tainted` ships no default editor decoration, and the marker is opt-in** *(designed)* — `tainted` gets a semantic-token modifier and **no default decoration**. ([`ide/tainted-has-no-default-decoration`](rules/ide.md#ide-tainted-has-no-default-decoration))

## Testing

- **A test is a method marked `#[Test]`, and its table is built while compiling** — A test is an ordinary `public` method carrying `#[Test]`, on an ordinary class. ([`testing/test-attribute`](rules/testing.md#testing-test-attribute))
- **`nvs run` and `nvs build` lower no test, and `nvs check` type-checks every one** *(designed)* — A `#[Test]` method may be declared in any file — beside the class it tests, or in a separate tree. ([`testing/tests-never-reach-a-build`](rules/testing.md#testing-tests-never-reach-a-build))
- **Every test runs in its own isolate and shares nothing but compiled code with its siblings** — Each test runs on an isolate of its own: it shares compiled code with its siblings and nothing else — not a static, not a cache entry, not an open handle. ([`testing/isolate-per-test`](rules/testing.md#testing-isolate-per-test))
- **A test reaches `private` members of classes declared in its own file, and nowhere else** *(designed)* — A test method may reach `private` and `protected` members of classes declared **in the same file**. ([`testing/private-in-the-same-file`](rules/testing.md#testing-private-in-the-same-file))
- **An assertion names its subject first and compares two values of one type** — The assertion surface is static members on `Core\Test`, each taking its **subject first**: `assertEquals($actual, $expected)`, with one trailing options shape, nothing mutating and failure throwing. ([`testing/assertions-are-typed`](rules/testing.md#testing-assertions-are-typed))
- **A failed assertion is a catchable `Throwable` and a ledger entry the test cannot erase** — `Core\Test\Failure` is an ordinary `Throwable`, and catching one is not merely allowed but necessary: a composite assertion, a retry wrapper, a soft-assert block and any test *of* an assertion all need to intercept one. ([`testing/failure-ledger`](rules/testing.md#testing-failure-ledger))
- **The constructor is the test's setup, and there is no second before-hook** — The constructor is the test's setup, and a stronger one than a `setUp` method can be: definite property initialization guarantees every property is assigned before any test body runs. ([`testing/constructor-is-setup`](rules/testing.md#testing-constructor-is-setup))
- **`#[After]` is for state that outlives the isolate, and nothing else needs teardown** *(designed)* — `#[After]` runs after a test and exists only for residue that outlives the isolate — a file, a row, a remote object. ([`testing/after-hook`](rules/testing.md#testing-after-hook))
- **`#[Fixture]` is built once per class and injected into a test by the type it returns** — `#[Fixture]` marks a `public static` method, and what it supplies is its declared return type. ([`testing/fixtures`](rules/testing.md#testing-fixtures))
- **`#[TestWith]` is matched against the parameters by name and by type, and each row is its own case** — `#[TestWith(...)]` carries a shape literal that the checker matches against the method's parameters… ([`testing/data-rows`](rules/testing.md#testing-data-rows))
- **A double is a shape of closures, structurally checked against an interface** *(designed)* — A double is a shape of closures, structurally checked against an interface: `Core\Test::double<Clock>({now: fn(): Instant => ...})` **is** a `Clock` and may be passed wherever one is taken. ([`testing/doubles`](rules/testing.md#testing-doubles))
- **A call to a double is asserted after the exercise, never expected before it** *(designed)* — A double records the calls made to it, and the test asserts on that record afterwards with ordinary assertions, in the order the test reads: `Core\Test::assertCalled($mailer, Mailer::send, {times: 1, with: [...]})` and… ([`testing/interaction-after-the-fact`](rules/testing.md#testing-interaction-after-the-fact))
- **`at:` and `seed:` fix the clock and the generator of the test's own isolate** — `#[Test(at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", seed: 42)]` fixes the clock and the random generator of that test's own isolate: `Core\Time::now()` answers exactly that instant, and the seeded generator and the identifier members d… ([`testing/determinism-declared-on-the-test`](rules/testing.md#testing-determinism-declared-on-the-test))
- **A task still running when a test returns fails that test** — The whole suite runs inside one task, so a test's isolate is a child of it and a `Core\Task::all` written in a test has a calling task to put its own children under. ([`testing/task-tree-and-virtual-clock`](rules/testing.md#testing-task-tree-and-virtual-clock))
- **`#[Test(db:)]` opens a transaction on the test's own context and rolls it back** — `#[Test(db: "test")]` opens a transaction against the named connection before the test and rolls it back after. ([`testing/db-transaction`](rules/testing.md#testing-db-transaction))
- **A test request is dispatched in-process through the compiled route table, and its input arrives `tainted`** — `Core\Test::request(...)` builds a request and runs it through the compiled route table and the real middleware chain — no socket, no port, microseconds per test. ([`testing/in-process-request`](rules/testing.md#testing-in-process-request))
