- **One registered answer makes every outbound call in that test come from the table, and an unmatched one throws rather than reaching the network** — Once a test registers one answer with `Core\Test::answerHttp(string $url, uint $status, {json?, body?, headers?})`, **every** outbound call that test makes is answered from the table, and an unmatched one throws a `Logi… ([`testing/an-outbound-call-is-answered-from-a-table`](rules/testing.md#testing-an-outbound-call-is-answered-from-a-table))
- **`Core\Test`'s table answers a WebSocket handshake, plays the frames it was given and records what the program sent, and an unmatched socket throws rather than connecting** — A test answers an outbound socket from `Core\Test`'s table, never from a listener. ([`testing/an-outbound-socket-is-answered-by-a-scripted-peer`](rules/testing.md#testing-an-outbound-socket-is-answered-by-a-scripted-peer))
- **`#[Property]` derives its generators from the parameters' declared types** *(designed)* — `#[Property]` runs a method against generated inputs, and the generators are **derived from the parameters' declared types** by the same declaration walk a codec is derived from, user classes included. ([`testing/property-testing`](rules/testing.md#testing-property-testing))
- **A snapshot is a literal in the test body, and the updater rewrites that literal and nothing else** — `Core\Test::assertMatchesInline($value, "...")` holds the expectation in the source file, and `nvs test --update` splices the produced value into that literal. ([`testing/inline-snapshots`](rules/testing.md#testing-inline-snapshots))
- **A mutation run asks whether any test would have noticed the code being wrong** *(designed)* — A mutation run makes a small, deliberate change to the code, re-runs the tests, and records whether anything failed. ([`testing/mutation-testing`](rules/testing.md#testing-mutation-testing))
- **A test that asserts nothing fails, a skip states a reason, and a retry is reported flaky rather than green** — A test that asserts nothing fails — the ledger already knows the count, and `Core\Test::assertDoesNotThrow(callable)` is how a test states "this must merely not throw", explicitly. ([`testing/runner-is-strict`](rules/testing.md#testing-runner-is-strict))
- **One verdict, three renderings, a machine format owns stdout alone, and the JSON one locates every test it reports** — Human output is the default and is written as the run goes, which is what keeps a long suite legible. ([`testing/report-formats`](rules/testing.md#testing-report-formats))
- **`.nvst` proves the language; `#[Test]` is how a program written in Novis tests itself** — `.nvst` is a whole-program, expected-stdout conformance case — a deliberate superset of PHP's `.phpt`, so importing PHP's corpus stays mechanical — and it is how **Novis's own conformance to its specification** is prove… ([`testing/nvst-is-separate`](rules/testing.md#testing-nvst-is-separate))
- **One slice writes all four of a feature's proofs together** — One slice takes one feature and writes **all four of its proofs together**. ([`testing/one-slice-is-one-feature`](rules/testing.md#testing-one-slice-is-one-feature))
- **`docs/examples/` is authoritative and the website mirrors it** — `docs/examples/` is authoritative, and the website's example tree is a mirror rebuilt from it. ([`testing/examples-live-in-the-repository`](rules/testing.md#testing-examples-live-in-the-repository))
- **A hostile case passes when nothing came apart, and a compile diagnostic is never a pass** — A hostile case is judged by a contract, never by frozen output. ([`testing/hostile-case-contract`](rules/testing.md#testing-hostile-case-contract))
- **A feature is finished when it has a test from both sides, three examples, a measured figure and an attack** — A feature is finished when five artefacts exist for it, not when it works. ([`testing/four-proofs`](rules/testing.md#testing-four-proofs))
- **The roster of features is read from the registry and the reference chapters, never kept as a list** — The roster of features is read from live sources and kept nowhere. ([`testing/roster-is-derived`](rules/testing.md#testing-roster-is-derived))
- **An example, an attack and a bench are attributed by path; a test is attributed by a marker** — An example, an attack and a bench are attributed by **where they sit**: the trees share one relative path per feature, so nothing has to be registered anywhere. ([`testing/proof-attribution`](rules/testing.md#testing-proof-attribution))
- **A proof that fails is fixed or recorded as a known gap, and never weakened** — An attack that breaks the member it was written against, and an example that disagrees with the binary, are the program working. ([`testing/a-failing-proof-is-fixed-or-recorded`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-failing-proof-is-fixed-or-recorded))
- **Every member of a capability-bearing class declares a capability or declares none, and there is no allowlist** — A class is **capability-bearing** when any of its members has a row in the capability table. ([`testing/capability-closure-test`](rules/testing.md#testing-capability-closure-test))
- **The third-party notice is committed, and a check fails when the lockfile moved without it** — `python tools/gen-attribution.py --check` regenerates the third-party notice and compares it, failing when the lockfile has moved and the notice has not. ([`testing/attribution-is-diffed-in-ci`](rules/testing.md#testing-attribution-is-diffed-in-ci))
- **`[debug] mode` is the ceiling as well as the default, and writing a trace or a profile is its own capability** — `[debug] mode` in `nvs.toml` states the default **and** the ceiling in one value: `[]` is off, and any subset of `coverage`, `branch`, `trace` and `profile` is a ceiling a request may narrow and can never widen. ([`testing/debug-mode-directive`](rules/testing.md#testing-debug-mode-directive))
- **Coverage, tracing and profiling are one per-request flag word checked at fixed probe sites, never a second compiled tier** — `Ctx` carries one small mutable bitset — coverage, branch, trace and profile — and codegen emits an unconditional load-and-branch against it at exactly two kinds of site, present in every compiled unit whether or not an… ([`testing/debug-probes`](rules/testing.md#testing-debug-probes))
- **Each probe starts and stops mid-request, and exports what existing tooling already reads** *(designed)* — `Core\Debug` starts and stops each probe from inside a request — coverage with an optional branch half, a trace to a named sink, a profile to another — and reads coverage back as a path-to-line-to- count map. ([`testing/debug-surface`](rules/testing.md#testing-debug-surface))
- **The conformance suite runs with the probes on, and once per optimisation level** *(designed)* — The conformance suite runs **at least once with coverage and tracing probes enabled**, and **once per Cranelift optimisation level**, so neither is a shape only production ever takes. ([`testing/probes-on-is-a-tested-configuration`](rules/testing.md#testing-probes-on-is-a-tested-configuration))
- **`[debug] store` is off by default and can only subtract, so no run mode or log level ever turns debug records on** *(designed)* — `[debug] store` decides whether debug records are persisted at all, is off by default, and can only subtract — no run mode, no log level and no other directive turns it on. ([`testing/writing-a-debug-record-to-disk-is-its-own-gate`](rules/testing.md#testing-writing-a-debug-record-to-disk-is-its-own-gate))
- **A debug record reaches the service through a sealed spool file that one writer owns, never over a socket** *(designed)* — A debug record reaches the service by being written to a file the writing core owns alone, never over a socket, and the service reads a spool file only once it has been sealed. ([`testing/the-debug-stream-reaches-the-service-through-the-disk`](rules/testing.md#testing-the-debug-stream-reaches-the-service-through-the-disk))
- **The ingester owns every write to the index and runs without a browser, and the viewer only ever reads** *(designed)* — The ingester owns every write to the index and runs from the moment the service starts, whether or not a browser has ever connected; the viewer is a reader that never opens a log file, parses a line or scans a directory. ([`testing/the-ingester-runs-whether-or-not-anyone-is-looking`](rules/testing.md#testing-the-ingester-runs-whether-or-not-anyone-is-looking))
- **A malformed line becomes a visible record and an unreadable file is quarantined under a backoff, so ingestion never stops** *(designed)* — A malformed line becomes a record that says so and an unreadable file is quarantined under a backoff, so nothing on disk can stop the ingester. ([`testing/a-bad-line-degrades-and-a-bad-file-is-quarantined`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-bad-line-degrades-and-a-bad-file-is-quarantined))
- **The viewer renders the correlated request stream and hands every artifact with an existing viewer to it** *(designed)* — The viewer renders the correlated request stream and the log, and every artifact that an existing tool already renders is handed to that tool rather than drawn. ([`testing/the-viewer-shows-the-stream-and-hands-off-every-artifact`](rules/testing.md#testing-the-viewer-shows-the-stream-and-hands-off-every-artifact))
- **`#[Bench]` reports counted semantic work, and CI may gate on the counts but never on wall-clock** *(designed)* — `#[Bench]` reports counted semantic work — statements executed, calls made, allocations, bytes attributed, GC cycles — read off the same probe sites coverage and tracing use, in a counting mode beside their timing one (… ([`testing/bench-counters`](rules/testing.md#testing-bench-counters))
- **A per-PR guard and the historical dashboard are separate measurements, and never one** — Two performance measurements exist and they are never one. ([`testing/perf-two-mechanisms`](rules/testing.md#testing-perf-two-mechanisms))
- **Wall-clock and the PHP ratio ride beside the instruction count as same-host figures only** — Each history entry carries that same run's wall-clock time and, where a runnable equivalent exists, the same-host same-run ratio against the pinned PHP oracle. ([`testing/perf-secondary-figures`](rules/testing.md#testing-perf-secondary-figures))
- **The performance history is an append-only NDJSON file in the repository** — A data point is one JSON object appended to `docs/perf/history.ndjson` — commit, date, workload, instruction count, wall clock, PHP ratio. ([`testing/perf-history-file`](rules/testing.md#testing-perf-history-file))
- **A member's record is four counts that compare on any machine and one clock that compares on its own, re-measured only when its implementing file's text moves** — A member's record is four counts and one clock, taken in one sweep over one bench program. ([`testing/member-perf-ledger`](rules/testing.md#testing-member-perf-ledger))
- **A cross-engine comparison is a `benches/userland/` case with one twin per engine** — `benches/userland/` holds ordinary web-and-CLI programs written once per engine — Novis, PHP and Python — and `python tools/bench.py` runs whichever engines a case has twins for and prints the same-host ratios. ([`testing/userland-benchmarks`](rules/testing.md#testing-userland-benchmarks))
- **The historical leg runs under callgrind on Linux or WSL, and nowhere else** — The historical leg runs under `valgrind --tool=callgrind`, which has no native Windows build, so it runs on Linux or WSL and nowhere else. ([`testing/valgrind-on-wsl`](rules/testing.md#testing-valgrind-on-wsl))
- **One workflow holds every job, and three lanes decide which of them a run needs** — One workflow file holds every CI job, and a schedule trigger plus a `full` flag decide which of them a given run needs. ([`testing/ci-lanes`](rules/testing.md#testing-ci-lanes))
- **One Python table decides what a diff runs, and the platform matrix is never one of the gates** — The first job compares the push's or the pull request's base against `HEAD` and emits one boolean per lane; every other job's `if:` is a single comparison against one of them. ([`testing/lane-table`](rules/testing.md#testing-lane-table))
- **A run with no base commit to diff against runs every lane** — A first push to a branch, a force-push and a shallow clone all leave the lane computation without a base commit it can diff against. ([`testing/unknown-base-runs-everything`](rules/testing.md#testing-unknown-base-runs-everything))
- **Miri, the fuzzers and the unsafe audit run nightly and at release, and the fuzz corpus persists** — The memory-safety and fuzzing evidence — the interpreter-under-Miri run, the fuzz smoke runs and the unsafe audit — runs in the nightly and at release, and not on a push. ([`testing/the-deep-lane`](rules/testing.md#testing-the-deep-lane))
- **A job a lane defers is skipped by its own `if:`, never filtered out of the workflow** — Every lane gate is a job-level `if:`, never a workflow-level path filter. ([`testing/a-deferred-job-is-skipped-never-absent`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-deferred-job-is-skipped-never-absent))
- **A run on the default branch is never cancelled by the next commit** — In-progress runs are cancelled for pull requests only. ([`testing/every-push-gets-a-verdict`](rules/testing.md#testing-every-push-gets-a-verdict))

## Security and isolation

- **Running another script is an in-process isolate that shares nothing with its parent but compiled code** — `spawn script` runs another `.nvs` file — or a static method — as an isolated unit of work inside this process. ([`security/isolate-shares-nothing`](rules/security.md#security-isolate-shares-nothing))
- **A value crosses an isolate boundary as one graph copy, and a closure, an alias or a host handle does not cross at all** — Arguments in and the result out are **deep-copied, or moved when the refcount is 1** — the identical mechanism and identical restrictions as `spawn worker`. ([`security/isolate-values-cross-by-copy`](rules/security.md#security-isolate-values-cross-by-copy))
- **A request and everything it spawns share one budget, accounted at the tree's root** — A request and everything it spawns form one tree, and limits are accounted against the tree's root. ([`security/isolate-budget-is-the-trees`](rules/security.md#security-isolate-budget-is-the-trees))
- **A child isolate's failure arrives as data on the result and never unwinds into its parent** — A child's failure arrives as **data on the result**, never as an exception unwinding into the parent. ([`security/isolate-failure-is-a-value`](rules/security.md#security-isolate-failure-is-a-value))
- **An isolate's output is captured by default and carries the parent's sink carrier** — `output: 'capture'` is the default: the child's output lands on the result and is charged to the tree's `max_output`. ([`security/isolate-output-is-captured`](rules/security.md#security-isolate-output-is-captured))
- **An isolate ends by draining its roots through the one release worklist and then sweeping what a cycle held up** — When an isolate ends — returning, throwing, breaching a limit, or being cancelled — its context's roots are released through one iterative worklist. ([`security/isolate-teardown-is-a-drain-then-a-sweep`](rules/security.md#security-isolate-teardown-is-a-drain-then-a-sweep))
- **An isolate's arena is an ownership root, not an address range** — An isolate's arena is its context together with the set of values reachable from that context's roots. ([`security/arena-is-an-ownership-root`](rules/security.md#security-arena-is-an-ownership-root))
- **An inbound request is the root isolate of its own tree, and there is one isolate implementation** — There is a single `Isolate` type, and **an inbound HTTP request is the root isolate of a request tree**. ([`security/one-isolation-implementation`](rules/security.md#security-one-isolation-implementation))
- **Executing code is its own capability, and the entry path is canonicalised and then prefix-checked** — Spawning an isolate requires `script.spawn`, a deny-by-default grant naming the roots that code may be executed *from*. ([`security/script-spawn-capability`](rules/security.md#security-script-spawn-capability))
- **Request, server and session state throws where there is no inbound request, rather than answering empty** — `Core\Request`, `Core\Server` and `Core\Session` **throw** where the context is answering no inbound request, rather than returning empty values. ([`security/request-state-throws-in-an-isolate`](rules/security.md#security-request-state-throws-in-an-isolate))
- **Nothing a request does is observable by another request except through an explicit, capability-gated store** — Nothing a request does is observable by another request except through an explicit, capability-gated store. ([`security/no-cross-request-state`](rules/security.md#security-no-cross-request-state))
- **Four doors are closed by construction, and no configuration reopens any of them** — Four mechanisms PHP has are absent from Novis by construction: native code loading (`security/no-ffi`), scheme dispatch on a path (`security/a-path-is-not-a-url`), cross-request state (`security/no-cross-request-state`)… ([`security/closed-doors`](rules/security.md#security-closed-doors))
- **No userland mechanism loads native code into the process** — There is no `FFI`-equivalent, no `com_dotnet`-equivalent, and no mechanism by which userland code causes native code to be loaded into the process. ([`security/no-ffi`](rules/security.md#security-no-ffi))
- **There is no `eval`, and no `Core` member compiles a string produced at run time** — There is no `eval`, no string-argument `assert`, and no `Core` member that compiles and runs a string produced at run time. ([`security/no-eval`](rules/security.md#security-no-eval))
- **A path is a filesystem path: no member dispatches on a scheme prefix, and nothing may register one** — No `Core` member that takes a path interprets a scheme prefix, and there is no registry by which userland or an extension adds one. ([`security/a-path-is-not-a-url`](rules/security.md#security-a-path-is-not-a-url))
- **A reflective call faces exactly the visibility check ordinary code at that site would, and there is no `setAccessible`** — Reading **metadata** — a member's existence, name, declared type, visibility, attributes, doc comment — is always available, because that is introspection of the program's *shape*. ([`security/reflection-enforces-visibility`](rules/security.md#security-reflection-enforces-visibility))
- **Reflection and AST parsing are capability-free, because neither reaches the world outside the process** — Reflection and source parsing are pure in-memory operations over a program's own compiled shape or its own supplied string. ([`security/reflection-needs-no-capability`](rules/security.md#security-reflection-needs-no-capability))
- **The capability check lives inside the function that performs the effect, and that door is the only way out of the process** — The check is **not** a line in a member's body that an author remembers to write, **not** at the call site in emitted code, and **not** in a dispatcher. ([`security/capability-check-at-the-door`](rules/security.md#security-capability-check-at-the-door))
- **A capability question is a grant and a scope, asked of the request's own configuration snapshot** — At the point of a call the question has exactly two parts: the **grant** — is this capability present at all in the effective configuration — and the **scope** — does *this argument* fall inside what was granted: a path… ([`security/capability-question-is-grant-and-scope`](rules/security.md#security-capability-question-is-grant-and-scope))
- **What each `Core` member needs is declared once in one table, and nothing at run time reads it** — What each `Core` member needs is declared once, in one table: a class, a member, and an optional capability. ([`security/capability-declaration-is-one-table`](rules/security.md#security-capability-declaration-is-one-table))
- **Every capability name that exists is on one roster, and a name outside it is refused where it is written** — Every capability name that exists is on one roster, in one place, with the reasoning for what it permits named beside it. ([`security/capability-roster-is-closed`](rules/security.md#security-capability-roster-is-closed))
- **Authority is a property of the namespace enclosing the code, never of the nesting depth or the name being called** *(designed)* — Authority is the namespace **enclosing the code**, not the nesting depth of the statement and not the name being called. ([`security/authority-is-the-enclosing-namespace`](rules/security.md#security-authority-is-the-enclosing-namespace))
- **The application's grant table is keyed on namespace prefixes, and a capability it names must be on the roster** *(designed)* — The application's grant table is keyed on namespace prefixes and lives in the application's own configuration rather than in a package manifest. ([`security/grants-are-keyed-on-a-namespace`](rules/security.md#security-grants-are-keyed-on-a-namespace))
- **The longest matching grant key wins, and a subtree is spelled out because it reaches code that does not exist yet** *(designed)* — Lookup reuses the resolution rule a developer already learned. ([`security/longest-prefix-wins`](rules/security.md#security-longest-prefix-wins))
- **A namespace matching no grant line holds the application's own authority, and a fetch leaves nothing unmatched** *(designed)* — A namespace matching no grant line holds what the application holds — the operator's ceiling. ([`security/an-unmatched-namespace-holds-the-application`](rules/security.md#security-an-unmatched-namespace-holds-the-application))
- **A path scope is canonicalise-then-prefix over whole components, and a path that does not exist yet is its deepest existing ancestor** — A path-bearing capability resolves by one comparison: **canonicalise both sides, then compare whole components.** A traversal through `..` does not reach a root it was not already under, a symlink planted under a grante… ([`security/path-scope-canonicalise-then-prefix`](rules/security.md#security-path-scope-canonicalise-then-prefix))
- **A denied capability is a catchable `RuntimeError` naming the capability, never a fatal** — A denied capability throws a `RuntimeError`, and a program may catch it and degrade. ([`security/denial-is-a-runtime-error`](rules/security.md#security-denial-is-a-runtime-error))
- **A capability is required or optional, and only a required one refuses to build** *(designed)* — A package's manifest splits what it asks for into `required` and `optional`. ([`security/optional-capability-degrades`](rules/security.md#security-optional-capability-degrades))
- **Two layers enforce a capability and only the static one grants; nothing anywhere widens** — Two layers enforce a capability. ([`security/no-runtime-grant`](rules/security.md#security-no-runtime-grant))
- **A member that needs no capability pays nothing, and one that does pays only beside a syscall** — A member that needs no capability pays nothing at all: no table lookup, no branch, no field on its row, no code emitted at its call sites. ([`security/capability-costs-nothing-unasked`](rules/security.md#security-capability-costs-nothing-unasked))
- **A dependency's authority is granted by the application one line at a time, and a declaration grants nothing** *(designed)* — A package **declares** what it requests, split into required and optional. ([`security/package-authority-is-granted-one-line-at-a-time`](rules/security.md#security-package-authority-is-granted-one-line-at-a-time))
- **Executing a program is deny-by-default under its own capability, and there is no shell to interpolate into** — Running another program is deny-by-default under `process.exec`, the same as every other syscall-touching entry point: a request may narrow it further and never widen it, and calling without the grant throws (`security/… ([`security/process-exec-capability`](rules/security.md#security-process-exec-capability))
- **`net.connect` carries an address policy that denies the private ranges, and an exception is one written IP address** — `net.connect` is not a boolean and not merely a host list. ([`security/net-address-policy`](rules/security.md#security-net-address-policy))
- **The grant follows what the program is doing rather than the transport: reaching out is `net.connect`, binding is `net.listen`, and neither widens the other** *(designed)* — Which network capability an opening asks is decided by **what the program is doing**, not by which transport it does it over. ([`security/net-listen-is-a-separate-grant-from-net-connect`](rules/security.md#security-net-listen-is-a-separate-grant-from-net-connect))
- **The address policy lives in the capability, so every client obeys it and none of them may hold its own** — Every client — the HTTP client, the raw socket layer, a program-supplied database target, and any socket a host import hands to an extension — is subject to the same policy, enforced at the point the connection is made… ([`security/the-policy-lives-in-the-capability`](rules/security.md#security-the-policy-lives-in-the-capability))
- **`tainted` is a compile-time qualifier on `string`, `bytes` and a shape of them, spellable in any declaration and erased before codegen** — `tainted string` and `tainted bytes` join the type grammar as a qualified form of the two scalar types, and `tainted {…}` writes the same fact over a whole shape of them. ([`security/tainted-qualifier`](rules/security.md#security-tainted-qualifier))
- **Every accessor that hands a program bytes from outside answers the `tainted` form, and the list of them is enumerable** — Every member of the request, server, session, environment and CLI accessors, and a script's own arguments, answers the `tainted` form of whatever it already returned. ([`security/tainted-sources`](rules/security.md#security-tainted-sources))
- **A tainted operand poisons every operation it takes part in, and only a checked conversion launders for free** — Any operation combining a tainted operand with an untainted one — concatenation, interpolation, a string member, an array of scalars — produces a tainted result. ([`security/taint-propagation`](rules/security.md#security-taint-propagation))
- **A `string` or `bytes` parameter is a sink when its content becomes an instruction a parser executes** — That one line derives every worked case, which is the test of it being the right predicate rather than a restatement. ([`security/sink-predicate`](rules/security.md#security-sink-predicate))
- **A `Core` parameter nobody classified refuses a tainted argument, and refuses to ship at all** — A `Core` member whose `string`/`bytes` parameter carries no classification **rejects a tainted argument**. ([`security/unclassified-parameter-refuses-tainted`](rules/security.md#security-unclassified-parameter-refuses-tainted))
- **Every grammar the library parses is a sink, and none of the four gets a launderer** — The library parses exactly four grammars — a regex pattern, a format template, a date pattern, and a byte-packing format — and every one of them is an instruction under `security/sink-predicate`. ([`security/every-grammar-is-a-sink`](rules/security.md#security-every-grammar-is-a-sink))
- **A regex pattern is a sink with no launderer; the subject is data and may be tainted** — A regex **pattern** requires the plain, unqualified `string`. ([`security/regex-pattern-is-a-sink`](rules/security.md#security-regex-pattern-is-a-sink))
- **An outbound URL or address is a sink, and a tainted one is refused where it is written** — The URL parameter of an HTTP client's request members, and the address parameter of a raw connect, are unqualified: a `tainted` value at either position is a compile-time diagnostic, exactly as at a query text parameter. ([`security/outbound-url-is-a-sink`](rules/security.md#security-outbound-url-is-a-sink))
- **A metric label value refuses `tainted`, and there is deliberately no launderer for one** *(designed)* — A metric label value is a sink: a query parameter, a header, a path segment or a database column cannot become a label. ([`security/metric-label-refuses-tainted`](rules/security.md#security-metric-label-refuses-tainted))
- **A log field is data, so it takes a tainted value and wants one** — A log field is data: the writer is a structured serializer, so a field is framed by the serializer and never by string concatenation into a line. ([`security/log-is-not-a-sink`](rules/security.md#security-log-is-not-a-sink))
- **The only way out of `tainted` is a `Core` member whose contract names the one sink it is safe for** — Short of a checked conversion, the only way to remove `tainted` is a `Core` member whose contract states which **one** sink it is safe for: an HTML escape for HTML text, an identifier quote for a dynamic table or column… ([`security/launderers-are-sink-named`](rules/security.md#security-launderers-are-sink-named))
- **A launderer answers its sink's carrier when that sink launders on its own and the transform is not idempotent, and a plain type otherwise** — A `Core` member that removes `tainted` answers its sink's **carrier type** rather than the plain type when **both** hold: its sink launders automatically — a value reaches that sink and is transformed with no call writt… ([`security/launderer-answers-a-carrier`](rules/security.md#security-launderer-answers-a-carrier))
- **Capturing a sink yields that sink's carrier, never a plain `string`** — Capturing output answers **the carrier of the sink in force**, not a plain `string`. ([`security/capture-answers-the-carrier`](rules/security.md#security-capture-answers-the-carrier))
- **A route capture is laundered by the parameter's own type, and a `string` capture stays tainted** — Every capture in a route path corresponds to a parameter of the same name, and the parameter's declared type is what the segment is converted to during matching. ([`security/route-capture-is-laundered-by-its-type`](rules/security.md#security-route-capture-is-laundered-by-its-type))
- **A derived codec adds no qualifier rule, and a `secret` field is refused at the declaration rather than silently omitted** — A derived codec introduces no qualifier rule of its own. ([`security/derived-codec-qualifiers`](rules/security.md#security-derived-codec-qualifiers))
- **`Core\Taint::assertTrusted` is the one generic way out, and it carries a written reason at the call site** — `Core\Taint::assertTrusted(tainted string, string $reason): string` is the one generic escape from the qualifier, for the case where the developer has validated the value themselves and needs to say so. ([`security/assert-trusted`](rules/security.md#security-assert-trusted))
- **A response body is written by one typed member, and mixing `echo` with one of them does not compile** — A response body is written by one of seven typed members, each owning a body shape and setting its own content type. ([`security/response-body-is-one-typed-member`](rules/security.md#security-response-body-is-one-typed-member))
- **A pooled database connection is proven clean before it is reused, and a failed reset destroys it** — A connection released at request teardown returns to a per-core pool, and **a released connection is reset before it is reusable**. ([`security/db-pool-reset-is-a-boundary`](rules/security.md#security-db-pool-reset-is-a-boundary))
- **`secret` is a second, independent compile-time qualifier, written before `tainted` and in that order alone** — `secret` is a second, independent compile-time qualifier on `string` and `bytes`. ([`security/secret-qualifier`](rules/security.md#security-secret-qualifier))
- **Nothing grants `secret` ambiently; it appears where a developer wrote it, and at one member that is its own contract** — Unlike `tainted`, **nothing in Novis grants `secret` ambiently.** The five host accessors are why `tainted` can attach itself automatically — every one is a named, enumerable place untrusted data enters (`security/taint… ([`security/secret-has-no-ambient-source`](rules/security.md#security-secret-has-no-ambient-source))
- **A `secret` operand poisons its own axis independently of `tainted`, and a checked conversion strips it** — Any operation combining a `secret` operand with a non-`secret` one produces a `secret` result — the poisoning shape `security/taint-propagation` defines, applied to this axis **independently**. ([`security/secret-propagation`](rules/security.md#security-secret-propagation))
- **Every output sink refuses a `secret` value outright, and no auto-escape or neutralisation bypasses one** — Every **output** sink refuses a `secret` value, and no neutralisation bypasses one: HTML and response output refuse outright with no auto-escape, terminal output refuses with no carrier bypass, a log field refuses, a se… ([`security/secret-sinks-refuse`](rules/security.md#security-secret-sinks-refuse))
- **A `secret` value is refused at the one graph copy, so it reaches neither `serialize` nor any spawn** — A `secret` value is refused at the one recursive graph-copy operation, for both of its callers alike — serialization to bytes and every crossing into a task, a worker or an isolate — rather than drawing a new distinctio… ([`security/secret-crosses-no-boundary`](rules/security.md#security-secret-crosses-no-boundary))
- **Comparing two `secret` values with `==` lowers to a constant-time helper, decided by the compiler** — `$provided == $expected`, where both operands are statically `secret`, lowers to a **constant-time** comparison helper rather than the short-circuiting one every other operand pair uses. ([`security/secret-comparison-is-constant-time`](rules/security.md#security-secret-comparison-is-constant-time))
- **A `secret` operand is compared but never rendered, and no flag lifts the redaction** — An assertion diff is simultaneously output, a log line, a dump and a `Throwable` message — all four of the things a `secret` value may not become (`security/secret-sinks-refuse`). ([`security/secret-in-a-test-report`](rules/security.md#security-secret-in-a-test-report))
- **No rendering the toolchain itself produces prints a `secret` in the clear, the AST dump included** *(designed)* — A `secret` value may not become output, a log line, a dump or a `Throwable` message (`security/secret-sinks-refuse`), and the toolchain is held to the bar it enforces on everyone else: no command this project ships prin… ([`security/redaction-reaches-the-tools-own-renderings`](rules/security.md#security-redaction-reaches-the-tools-own-renderings))
- **Everything an extension manifest may declare is a restriction, so a hostile manifest cannot make a calling program less safe** *(designed)* — Every declaration an extension manifest may carry is a **restriction**: it either rejects a call that would otherwise compile, or adds a qualifier the caller must discharge. ([`security/extension-manifest-only-tightens`](rules/security.md#security-extension-manifest-only-tightens))
- **An extension call is an ordinary operation for taint, so contagion is the default and needs no declaration** *(designed)* — An extension call is an ordinary operation for the purposes of taint. ([`security/extension-contagion`](rules/security.md#security-extension-contagion))
- **An extension manifest may declare exactly two things: a parameter that refuses `tainted`, and a return that is always `tainted`** *(designed)* — A manifest may say two things, and only these two. ([`security/extension-declares-sink-or-source`](rules/security.md#security-extension-declares-sink-or-source))
- **No extension may remove the `tainted` qualifier, in any manifest spelling** *(designed)* — There is **no manifest form** whose declared effect removes `tainted`. ([`security/extension-cannot-launder`](rules/security.md#security-extension-cannot-launder))
- **A `secret` value is refused at every extension boundary, in either direction** *(designed)* — A `secret` value passed to an extension is a compile-time diagnostic, and no manifest may declare a `secret` return. ([`security/secret-does-not-cross-an-extension`](rules/security.md#security-secret-does-not-cross-an-extension))
- **The image component declares no qualifier deviation and requests no capability** *(designed)* — The image component declares **no qualifier deviation**: ordinary contagion is exactly right, so a thumbnail of a `tainted` upload is `tainted` and reaches HTML output through the existing sinks like any other value, wh… ([`security/image-component-declares-nothing`](rules/security.md#security-image-component-declares-nothing))
- **There is one TLS client in the tree, and a driver reaches it over a generic transport rather than building a second** — There is one TLS client in the tree, with one answer to "whose certificates do you believe" and one place a configured anchor bundle plugs into. ([`security/one-tls-client`](rules/security.md#security-one-tls-client))
- **Verification is relaxed only where a `capabilities.tls` grant names the host and the call asks for it, and no such grant has a `true` spelling** — Certificate verification on an outbound call is strict by default and is relaxed only when two independent things agree: a `[capabilities.tls]` grant names the host, and the call itself asks. ([`security/tls-trust-is-relaxed-only-under-a-host-grant`](rules/security.md#security-tls-trust-is-relaxed-only-under-a-host-grant))
- **A closed roster of application-layer security protocols lives in `Core`, and nothing joins it without meeting the test** *(designed)* — A closed roster of application-layer security protocols lives in `Core`: signed and encrypted cookies (authenticated encryption only, with key rotation), CSRF tokens, TOTP, JWT — signed and verified under a shared key,… ([`security/protocol-roster`](rules/security.md#security-protocol-roster))
- **Three conditions and one boundary decide what may join the roster, and a flow never does** *(designed)* — Three conditions must all hold for a protocol to belong in `Core`. ([`security/protocol-admission-test`](rules/security.md#security-protocol-admission-test))
- **The algorithm comes from the key and never from the token** — The algorithm comes from the key, never from the token. ([`security/algorithm-comes-from-the-key`](rules/security.md#security-algorithm-comes-from-the-key))
- **A JWT without an expiry, or past one, fails verification, and no flag disables the check** — A JWT without an expiry, or past one, fails verification. ([`security/jwt-expiry-is-mandatory`](rules/security.md#security-jwt-expiry-is-mandatory))
- **Verification answers a value or throws, and no member exposes a raw comparison for the caller to get wrong** — Verification returns claims or throws. ([`security/verification-throws-and-compares-in-constant-time`](rules/security.md#security-verification-throws-and-compares-in-constant-time))
- **A verified signature proves origin, not safety: claims come back `tainted`** — Claims returned from token verification are **`tainted`**. ([`security/verification-does-not-launder`](rules/security.md#security-verification-does-not-launder))
- **`Core\Jwe` speaks compact JWE with `A256GCM` alone, and the static that built the key picks the algorithm** — `Core\Jwe` reads and writes compact JWE with `A256GCM` alone, and the static that built the key is what picks the key-management algorithm. ([`security/jwe-compact-subset`](rules/security.md#security-jwe-compact-subset))
- **A token another party issued verifies against a key found by `kid`, never one that is tried, and its claims come back as a `tainted` shape** — `Core\Jwt` verifies a token another party issued against a key it **finds** by `kid`, never one it tries, and answers the claims as a `tainted` shape. ([`security/jws-issued-subset`](rules/security.md#security-jws-issued-subset))
- **The server refuses an unsafe verb without a valid CSRF token, and the opt-out is written on the route itself** — The server refuses an unsafe verb — the four that change state — without a valid token, using the match it already made to know which handler is which. ([`security/csrf-is-on-by-default`](rules/security.md#security-csrf-is-on-by-default))
- **The compiler proves a route's access decision was written, never that it was honoured** — The compiler verifies that a route's access attribute is there and that the name inside it resolves. ([`security/access-is-checked-for-presence-not-meaning`](rules/security.md#security-access-is-checked-for-presence-not-meaning))
- **A span is rejected when it ends with a directional scope still open, decided by two counters** — Nine code points open or close a directional scope: four embedding and override forms closed by one terminator, and three isolate forms closed by another. ([`security/bidi-predicate`](rules/security.md#security-bidi-predicate))
- **The lexer refuses an unterminated control and the sinks substitute it, and nobody writes a second predicate** — The predicate has one implementation and several callers. ([`security/bidi-boundaries`](rules/security.md#security-bidi-boundaries))
- **Zero-width characters, homoglyphs and the full bidirectional algorithm are deliberately outside the check** — Three neighbouring hazards are deliberately outside the check, and saying so is what stops a future session from adding a fourth mechanism. ([`security/bidi-scope-is-the-whole-target`](rules/security.md#security-bidi-scope-is-the-whole-target))
- **`hash` writes Argon2id and nothing else, and no member takes an algorithm argument** — Hashing writes one algorithm and nothing else, and **no member gains an algorithm argument**. ([`security/hash-writes-argon2id-only`](rules/security.md#security-hash-writes-argon2id-only))
- **A stored password hash is read from a roster of exactly two shapes, and the roster grows only by amendment** — Verification accepts exactly two stored shapes: the modern hash this library writes, and a bcrypt hash under three prefixes — one algorithm under three tags, verified identically. ([`security/bcrypt-read-roster`](rules/security.md#security-bcrypt-read-roster))
- **`needsRehash` measures weaker rather than different, so every bcrypt hash asks to be rewritten** — `needsRehash` answers whether the stored hash is **weaker** than what hashing writes now, not whether its parameters differ. ([`security/needs-rehash-answers-weaker`](rules/security.md#security-needs-rehash-answers-weaker))
- **A stored bcrypt cost above 17 is refused before any work is done** — A stored bcrypt hash carries its own cost, and the cost is the base-2 logarithm of the round count — a CPU-time lever one `UPDATE` away from anyone who can write the table. ([`security/bcrypt-cost-ceiling`](rules/security.md#security-bcrypt-cost-ceiling))
- **bcrypt's 72-byte truncation is replicated exactly, because the stored row was written under it** — bcrypt hashes at most 72 bytes of a password and stops at a NUL byte. ([`security/bcrypt-truncation`](rules/security.md#security-bcrypt-truncation))
- **A stored value outside the read roster throws, and the message never quotes the bytes** — A stored value outside the read roster — garbage, a refused prefix, or a hash naming any other algorithm — **throws** rather than answering `false`, and the message never quotes the bytes (`security/secret-sinks-refuse`). ([`security/an-unreadable-stored-hash-throws`](rules/security.md#security-an-unreadable-stored-hash-throws))

## Concurrency

- **Concurrency is the `Core\Task` roster over the runtime's own single scheduler** — Concurrency is `Core\Task` and nothing else. ([`concurrency/one-scheduler`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-one-scheduler))
- **Every task is a child of the task that started it, shares that request's accounting, and dies with it** — Every task starts as a child of the task that started it. ([`concurrency/a-child-belongs-to-the-calling-task`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-child-belongs-to-the-calling-task))
- **A child spawned `on: "worker"` is started on another core, copies at every node in both directions, and is still its parent's child** — A child spawned `on: "worker"` is **started** on a core other than its parent's, and *started* is the whole of the placement: a task never migrates (`concurrency/a-wake-never-moves-a-task`), so which core runs it is dec… ([`concurrency/on-worker-runs-the-child-on-another-core`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-on-worker-runs-the-child-on-another-core))
- **`Core\Task::all` answers a shape with the argument's own field names, each field keeping its own type** — `Core\Task::all({...}, {limit?, deadline?}): S` takes a shape whose every field is a zero-argument callable, runs them concurrently, and answers **a shape with the same field names, each field carrying that field's own… ([`concurrency/all-answers-a-typed-shape`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-all-answers-a-typed-shape))
- **An `all` field answers its own callable's declared return type, and a callable declaring none answers `mixed`** — Each field of a `Core\Task::all` argument answers **its own callable's declared return type**. ([`concurrency/an-all-field-answers-what-its-callable-declares`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-an-all-field-answers-what-its-callable-declares))
- **`Core\Task::map` answers an array of the callback's own return type, in the input's keys and order** — `Core\Task::map(array<T> $items, callable $fn, {limit?, deadline?}): array<U>` runs one callback per element concurrently. ([`concurrency/map-preserves-keys-and-order`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-map-preserves-keys-and-order))
- **`{limit, deadline}` is the whole of what bounds a group, and there is no `timeout` member and no `race`** — `all` and `map` take one trailing options shape with the same two fields. ([`concurrency/limit-and-deadline-are-the-only-bounds`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-limit-and-deadline-are-the-only-bounds))
- **Control never leaves `all` or `map` with a child still running** — `all` and `map` do not return while a child is still running. ([`concurrency/nothing-is-still-running-when-a-call-returns`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-nothing-is-still-running-when-a-call-returns))
- **A cancelled task runs no `catch`, no cleanup and no handler, and cancellation is not a `Throwable`** — A cancelled task is torn down by the runtime where it parked. ([`concurrency/cancellation-runs-no-user-code`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-cancellation-runs-no-user-code))
- **A deadline bounds when cancellation is asked for, not when the call returns** *(designed)* — A `deadline` bounds when cancellation is **requested**, not when the call returns. ([`concurrency/a-deadline-bounds-the-cancel-not-the-return`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-deadline-bounds-the-cancel-not-the-return))
- **`Core\Task::afterResponse` runs after the request's own frame returns, still charged to the request tree** — `Core\Task::afterResponse(callable $fn, {deadline?}): void` registers work to run once the request is done with:… ([`concurrency/after-response-outlives-the-connection`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-after-response-outlives-the-connection))
- **Only the request's own task may defer work, and deferred work may not defer more** — Only the request's own task may register deferred work. ([`concurrency/only-the-request-registers-deferred-work`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-only-the-request-registers-deferred-work))
- **Deferred work may read the request but not write the response, and its uncaught throw reaches the log alone** *(designed)* — The response is on the wire before deferred work runs, so **the closure may not touch it**. ([`concurrency/deferred-work-cannot-write-the-response`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-deferred-work-cannot-write-the-response))
- **`[deferred]` carries two bounds: a `System` `max_concurrent` and a `Runtime` `deadline`** — which is a host-sizing decision and not a request-local one, so a request cannot raise it. ([`concurrency/deferred-is-bounded-by-two-directives`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-deferred-is-bounded-by-two-directives))
- **Past `[deferred] max_concurrent`, `afterResponse` throws at the call site rather than queueing** — Past `[deferred] max_concurrent`, `Core\Task::afterResponse` throws a `RuntimeError` **at the call site**. ([`concurrency/a-full-deferred-executor-throws`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-full-deferred-executor-throws))
- **A value outlives the request that made it only by being put into a named store** — A value outlives the request that made it only by being **put into a named store**. ([`concurrency/cross-request-state-is-explicit`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-cross-request-state-is-explicit))
- **`Core\Cache::process()` is one store per serving process, coherent across its cores and gone when it ends** — `Core\Cache::process()` hands back one store per **serving process** — coherent across every core of that process, held in memory only, and gone when the process ends. ([`concurrency/the-process-tier-is-one-store-per-process`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-process-tier-is-one-store-per-process))
- **The cache boundary is a copy in and a copy out, so nothing a program can reach is read-modify-write** — What crosses the cache boundary is a copy in and a copy out. ([`concurrency/put-and-get-are-the-whole-boundary`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-put-and-get-are-the-whole-boundary))
- **A value is copied into the cache and copied back out, by the same graph copy the isolate boundary uses** — `put` copies a value out of the request heap into the cache; `get` copies one back in. ([`concurrency/a-cached-value-is-copied-across-the-boundary`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-cached-value-is-copied-across-the-boundary))
- **The local tier's memory is charged to the core, capped in `nvs.toml`, and the cap evicts rather than failing a write** — Cache memory is **not attributable to a request**. ([`concurrency/cache-memory-is-charged-to-the-core`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-cache-memory-is-charged-to-the-core))
- **A cross-request store's bytes go on a balance of their own, and no request is charged or credited for them** — A request is measured against its own allocations, so the bytes of a store that outlives requests move a balance of their own and no request is charged or credited for them. ([`concurrency/a-cross-request-stores-bytes-are-its-own-balance`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-cross-request-stores-bytes-are-its-own-balance))
- **Anything a program relies on the value of goes to the shared tier, and a weaker tier is not offered for it** — The local tier is per-core with no coherence between cores: a write on one core is not visible on another, and any entry may be absent at any time. ([`concurrency/the-local-tier-cannot-hold-what-must-be-coherent`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-local-tier-cannot-hold-what-must-be-coherent))
- **A secret reaches a cache only as ciphertext, through `putSecret` and `getSecret` and a key ring** — A `secret` value meets a cache through exactly two members — `putSecret(string $key, secret string $value, Duration $ttl, array<secret bytes> $keys)` and `getSecret(string $key, array<secret bytes> $keys, {fill?, wait?}… ([`concurrency/a-secret-is-cached-only-sealed`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-secret-is-cached-only-sealed))
- **On a miss, one caller per process runs `fill` while the others wait, and a failure is never shared** — On a miss, `getSecret`'s `fill` runs in **exactly one caller per process**, in that caller's own request and under its own capabilities, while every other caller on every core waits for it — each for at most its `wait`,… ([`concurrency/a-secret-fill-runs-once-per-process`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-secret-fill-runs-once-per-process))
- **A persistent connection is a root isolate, and the request that upgraded it ends** — An upgraded connection is a **root isolate**, not a suspended request: its own arena, its own globals and statics, its own `[limits]` budget, its own capability grants, and its own entry in the timeline and the metric s… ([`concurrency/a-connection-is-a-root-isolate`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-connection-is-a-root-isolate))
- **An upgrade names compiled code — a file or a static method — and never a closure** — `Core\Socket::upgrade('sockets/chat.nvs', args: {room: $room})` takes a spawned script's operand and nothing else: a file path, resolved and root-checked exactly as that construct's is, or a static method written `Chat:… ([`concurrency/an-upgrade-is-spawn-shaped`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-an-upgrade-is-spawn-shaped))
- **An upgrade's `args`, `limits`, `grants` and `on` are a spawned script's options as ordinary named arguments** *(designed)* — An upgrade takes `args`, `limits`, `grants` and `on` — the same four options a spawned script spells after its operand, with identical meaning. ([`concurrency/an-upgrades-options-are-spawn-scripts`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-an-upgrades-options-are-spawn-scripts))
- **Inside a connection, code is an ordinary loop, and `receive()` answering `null` is what ends it** — Inside a connection, code is an ordinary loop — `while (var $msg = $conn->receive()) { … }` — with no handler interface, no event registration and no second control-flow style. ([`concurrency/a-connection-is-a-loop`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-connection-is-a-loop))
- **`receive()` is the one wait, and it answers the peer or a subscribed topic, whichever arrives first** *(designed)* — `receive()` is the **one** wait a connection takes, and it answers whichever of two sources arrives first: a frame from the peer, or a value published to a topic this connection subscribed to (`core-classes/topic`). ([`concurrency/receive-is-the-one-wait`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-receive-is-the-one-wait))
- **What a peer sent arrives `tainted`, and `Core\Validate` is the only way to launder it** — A received frame's payload arrives `tainted`. ([`concurrency/a-peer-frame-is-tainted`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-peer-frame-is-tainted))
- **A stream that ends with its response is a streaming response; one that outlives it is a connection isolate** — The line between a streaming response and a connection is **what the stream outlives**, and it is worth stating sharply because it is the one place two spellings could appear for one job. ([`concurrency/a-stream-that-outlives-its-request-is-a-connection`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-stream-that-outlives-its-request-is-a-connection))
- **`Core\Socket` and `Core\Sse` are two hand-overs onto one isolate, and each reports the one it is missing** — `Core\Socket::upgrade` and `Core\Sse::upgrade` open the same isolate through two different hand-overs, so a request carries **two cells and not one**. ([`concurrency/two-doors-one-isolate`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-two-doors-one-isolate))
- **Every bound on an open connection is finite with nothing configured** — Every bound on an open connection is finite before anything is configured: connections per process, maximum frame size, maximum message size, idle timeout, total lifetime, send timeout and subscriber queue depth. ([`concurrency/connection-bounds-are-finite`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-connection-bounds-are-finite))
- **An open connection runs to completion on the code it started with, and an edit reaches only the next one** — A connection isolate holds the compiled unit it started with. ([`concurrency/a-connection-keeps-its-compiled-unit`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-connection-keeps-its-compiled-unit))
- **A shutdown or a reload closes a connection with a defined code after a drain, never with a reset** — A graceful shutdown and a control-socket reload close connections with a defined code after a drain period, so a client's reconnect logic sees a clean close rather than a reset. ([`concurrency/a-drain-closes-a-connection-cleanly`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-drain-closes-a-connection-cleanly))
- **A `push` on the queue's connection commits with the write that caused it, or neither happens** — `Core\Queue::push` on the queue's own connection enlists in whatever transaction that connection already has open. ([`concurrency/enqueue-commits-with-your-write`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-enqueue-commits-with-your-write))
- **`Core\Queue`'s four request-path members are each asked about a job or about a queue, never about a row number** — `Core\Queue` is `push`, `status`, `cancel` and `stats` — the four members a request asks, and the four that take no capability. ([`concurrency/queue-four-members`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-queue-four-members))
- **A `tag` names a group of jobs and a `key` admits one pending job, and they are two columns because they are opposites** *(designed)* — `push`'s `tag` names a group of jobs and `key` admits at most one pending job, and they are two columns because they are opposites at the point they touch. ([`concurrency/a-tag-groups-jobs-and-a-key-dedupes-them`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-tag-groups-jobs-and-a-key-dedupes-them))
- **A job names a script file, and its payload crosses as a copied value** — A job names a script file — not a class, not a closure, not a static method. ([`concurrency/a-job-names-a-file`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-job-names-a-file))
- **A job's budget and grants are recorded when it is enqueued, and narrowed from that context rather than widened** *(designed)* — `push` takes the job's `limits` — the memory, CPU and time its isolate may spend — and its `grants`, and both are recorded with the row. ([`concurrency/a-jobs-budget-and-grants-are-recorded-at-enqueue`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-jobs-budget-and-grants-are-recorded-at-enqueue))
- **A worker claims a job with one statement the database arbitrates, so a fleet needs no lease protocol** — A worker claims a job with a single statement that selects the oldest due job in its queues and marks it in the same moment: `for update skip locked` on PostgreSQL and MySQL, `readpast` on SQL Server, and an immediate t… ([`concurrency/claiming-is-one-statement`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-claiming-is-one-statement))
- **A job between attempts is `Pending`, and there is no `Failed` state to ask about** — `Queue\State` is `Pending`, `Claimed`, `Succeeded`, `Dead` and `Cancelled`. ([`concurrency/a-job-between-attempts-is-pending`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-job-between-attempts-is-pending))
- **Delivery is at-least-once, and idempotency is the job's own obligation** — A job may run twice, and that is stated rather than implied. ([`concurrency/delivery-is-at-least-once`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-delivery-is-at-least-once))
- **Attempts are finite, backoff is exponential and jittered, and an exhausted job is kept rather than discarded** — A job's attempts are finite with nothing configured, because an unbounded retry is an unbounded wait wearing a different name. ([`concurrency/attempts-are-finite-and-a-dead-letter-is-kept`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-attempts-are-finite-and-a-dead-letter-is-kept))
- **A job that exceeds its budget is a failed attempt, reported as that and retried like any other** — A job that exceeds its memory, CPU or time budget has had a **failed attempt**. ([`concurrency/a-budget-overrun-is-a-failed-attempt`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-budget-overrun-is-a-failed-attempt))
- **`cancel` answers whether it won the race, and it changes the job's state rather than deleting the row** — `cancel` answers a `bool`, and the `bool` says whether *this* call is what took the job out of the queue. ([`concurrency/cancel-is-a-race-it-can-lose`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-cancel-is-a-race-it-can-lose))
- **A queue row is removed by `delete` or `purge`, never while claimed, and never dead-lettered or pending unless the call says so** *(designed)* — A queue row is removed by `delete`, which names one job by its receipt, or by `purge`, which names a queue and a filter — and neither ever removes a claimed job, a dead-lettered one, or a pending one unless the call say… ([`concurrency/queue-deletion-is-explicit-and-bounded`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-queue-deletion-is-explicit-and-bounded))
- **A job runs as a root isolate, and there is no second execution path** — A job runs as a **root isolate**: its own arena, its own budget, its own grants, sharing only compiled code. ([`concurrency/a-job-runs-as-a-root-isolate`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-job-runs-as-a-root-isolate))
- **Which process runs a job is configuration, and every spelling drives the identical isolate** *(designed)* — Whether jobs run inside the server process or in a worker of their own is configuration, not a different mechanism. ([`concurrency/who-runs-a-job-is-configuration`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-who-runs-a-job-is-configuration))
- **`nvs serve` runs the accept loop, the schedule ticker and the queue's workers in one process, and the drain stops all three** *(designed)* — `nvs serve` is one process running three things — the accept loop, the `[[schedule]]` ticker and the queue's workers — on the scheduler it already turns, and the drain stops all three. ([`concurrency/one-process-serves-requests-schedules-and-jobs`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-one-process-serves-requests-schedules-and-jobs))
- **A durable payload refuses `secret`, and a `tainted` value comes back `tainted`** *(designed)* — A durable row is an output, and an output refuses `secret` (`security/secret-qualifier`). ([`concurrency/a-payload-refuses-secret-and-keeps-its-qualifiers`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-payload-refuses-secret-and-keeps-its-qualifiers))
- **A `push` on a connection other than the queue's is not transactional, and is counted rather than assumed away** *(designed)* — A `push` issued while a transaction is open on a *different* connection than the queue's is not transactional. ([`concurrency/foreign-connection-enqueue-is-counted`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-foreign-connection-enqueue-is-counted))
- **Queued work is durable, retried and declared by the application; scheduled work is a clock tick and none of those** — Two things run outside a request, and they are not variants of one mechanism. ([`concurrency/queued-work-is-not-scheduled-work`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-queued-work-is-not-scheduled-work))
- **There is no broker backend and no pluggable driver, because a driver makes transactional enqueue optional** — There is no Redis, NATS, SQS or AMQP backend, and no pluggable driver interface. ([`concurrency/no-broker-and-no-driver-interface`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-no-broker-and-no-driver-interface))
- **A connection is one future, driven to completion by the coroutine that owns it** — A connection is one future, and the coroutine that accepted it drives that future to completion in a loop of *clear the flag, poll, park*. ([`concurrency/one-future-per-connection`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-one-future-per-connection))
- **A waker decides nothing; it is permission to make one more poll happen** — Waking sets an atomic flag and, if a permission is installed, delivers it. ([`concurrency/a-waker-is-one-permission-to-poll`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-waker-is-one-permission-to-poll))
- **One wake permission is installed per drive, and a fresh one is issued only after it fires** — A wake permission is taken per **drive**, not per park. ([`concurrency/one-permission-per-drive`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-one-permission-per-drive))
- **A wake from another core queues an id on the task's own core and never migrates it** — What crosses a thread boundary is a task id and a poke of one core's poller, and nothing else — no reference to a scheduler, a stack or an arena. ([`concurrency/a-wake-never-moves-a-task`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-wake-never-moves-a-task))
- **A cancellation ends the drive: torn down where it parked, or told once and answered** — A cancellation ends the drive. ([`concurrency/a-cancelled-drive-never-parks-again`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-cancelled-drive-never-parks-again))
- **Where a drive parks is decided once when it starts, and off a core it blocks the thread** — Where a drive parks is decided once, when it starts, because a task never migrates and so the answer cannot change underneath it. ([`concurrency/the-park-route-is-chosen-once`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-park-route-is-chosen-once))
- **A task registers before it suspends, treats a wake as a hint, and leaves the reactor holding nothing when it ends** — Five rules govern a task that waits on I/O, and the first two are ordering rules a reader will otherwise get backwards. ([`concurrency/the-parking-contract`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-parking-contract))
- **A stream issues the syscall first and parks only on `WouldBlock`, so a warm socket pays nothing** — A read is: issue the syscall; on success return; on `WouldBlock` register, suspend, and loop. ([`concurrency/try-the-syscall-then-park`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-try-the-syscall-then-park))
- **The reactor reports readiness on every platform, Windows included, so a stream is written once** — The reactor reports **readiness**, never completion, on every platform: epoll on Linux, kqueue on the BSDs and macOS, and on Windows a poll of `\Device\Afd` through the completion port, which turns it into a readiness s… ([`concurrency/the-reactor-reports-readiness`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-reactor-reports-readiness))
- **A parking stream is a plain `Read` and `Write`, so nothing up the call chain is coloured** — A parking socket implements nothing but `std::io::Read` and `std::io::Write`. ([`concurrency/a-stream-is-an-ordinary-io-stream`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-stream-is-an-ordinary-io-stream))
- **A task's stack is 1 MiB of reserved address space, resident only where it is touched, and pooled per worker** — A task's stack is 1 MiB of **reserved** address space with a guard page. ([`concurrency/a-task-stack-is-reserved-wide-and-pooled`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-task-stack-is-reserved-wide-and-pooled))
- **A task's recursion limit is armed from the real bounds of the stack it was handed** — A task's recursion limit is armed from the base and length of the stack it was actually handed, not asserted from a compiled-in ceiling. ([`concurrency/a-tasks-recursion-limit-comes-from-its-own-stack`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-tasks-recursion-limit-comes-from-its-own-stack))

## The Core API

- **`Core` means always present, so nothing outside Tier 0 may register a name under it** — Nothing outside Tier 0 may register a class under the `Core` namespace, and nothing whose presence a build flag can remove is registered there at all. ([`core-api/core-means-always-present`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-core-means-always-present))
- **A library candidate is placed by six ordered tests, not by PHP's extension list** — A candidate for the standard library is placed by six tests, applied in order, rather than by which PHP extension it happened to live in:… ([`core-api/tier-placement`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-tier-placement))
- **A candidate lands in exactly one of five placements: Core, Native, Ext, Dropped or answered** — The six tests (`core-api/tier-placement`) put a candidate in exactly one of five places:… ([`core-api/five-placements`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-five-placements))
- **Every subsystem's tier is recorded once in the roster, including the ones no milestone has built** *(designed)* — Every subsystem has a recorded placement, including the ones no milestone has scheduled, because an entry nobody will build is more useful named than pending. ([`core-api/tier-roster`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-tier-roster))
- **The `Core` namespace is the compiler's: nothing may declare under it and its rosters are closed while compiling** — `Core` and everything nested under it is reserved. ([`core-api/reserved-namespace`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-reserved-namespace))
- **A domain class is a singular noun and its object types nest under it** — A domain class is named with a singular noun, and the object types it constructs nest under it: `Core\Time`, `Core\Time\Instant`, `Core\Time\Duration`. ([`core-api/a-domain-class-is-a-singular-noun`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-a-domain-class-is-a-singular-noun))
- **Every `Core` member obeys the same twenty shape rules, R1–R20** — Every member of every `Core` class obeys all twenty shape rules below. ([`core-api/shape-rules`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-shape-rules))
- **The subject is parameter 1 of every `Core` member, with no exceptions** — The thing a member operates on is its first parameter, including where the member also takes a callback or a needle: `Arr::map($array, $fn)`, `Str::replace($subject, $search, $replacement)`, `Arr::contains($haystack, $n… ([`core-api/subject-first`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-subject-first))
- **A member's verb predicts its return type, and `…OrNull`, `…Safe`, `…Ex` and every `try…` but `tryParse` are banned** — One verb means one thing, so a member's name predicts its return type. ([`core-api/verb-lexicon`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-verb-lexicon))
- **A symmetric operation gets a symmetric name, and which pair to reach for is a rule rather than taste** — A symmetric operation gets a symmetric name: `encode`/`decode`, `split`/`join`, `pack`/`unpack`, `escape`/`unescape`, `trimStart`/`trimEnd`, `startsWith`/`endsWith`, `indexOf`/`lastIndexOf`, `first`/`last`. ([`core-api/symmetric-names`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-symmetric-names))
- **One name has one signature, and two behaviours need two names** — One name has one signature. ([`core-api/one-name-one-signature`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-one-name-one-signature))
- **A member name is a full word; only a class name may abbreviate, and only from a closed list** — A member name is a full word. ([`core-api/members-are-full-words`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-members-are-full-words))
- **An identifier's casing is fixed by its category and a mismatch is a hard compile error** — Every user-written identifier is checked against exactly one pattern for its category, and a mismatch is a hard compile error — not a lint, not a warning. ([`core-api/identifier-casing`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-identifier-casing))
- **Only the leading character's case is checked, so `HTTPClient` and `HttpClient` both pass** — Only the first character's case is checked. ([`core-api/casing-checks-the-leading-character`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-casing-checks-the-leading-character))
- **There is no suppression mechanism for a casing error, in any category** — There is no configuration, no per-project override and no suppression annotation for a casing error. ([`core-api/casing-has-no-suppression`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-casing-has-no-suppression))
- **Every member declaration writes exactly one visibility keyword, and there is no implicit `public`** — Every member declaration in a class, interface or anonymous-class body writes exactly one of `public`, `protected` or `private` — properties, class constants and methods alike, including a property carrying only `readon… ([`core-api/written-visibility`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-written-visibility))
- **An asymmetric property writes both halves, so a bare `private(set)` does not compile** — An asymmetric property writes both halves: `public private(set) string $name;`. ([`core-api/asymmetric-visibility-is-a-pair`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-asymmetric-visibility-is-a-pair))
- **`var $x;` and a bare `int $x;` in a class body report the missing visibility, not a statement error** — A class body containing `var $x;`, a bare `int $x;` or a bare `static int $x;` reports the missing visibility and names what to write, rather than falling through to the local-declaration grammar and reporting something… ([`core-api/legacy-property-shapes-name-the-visibility`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-legacy-property-shapes-name-the-visibility))
- **A constructor parameter is not a member, because visibility is what promotes one** — A constructor parameter carrying no visibility is a plain parameter, complete and correct, and the missing-visibility error does not fire on it. ([`core-api/a-parameter-is-not-a-member`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-a-parameter-is-not-a-member))
- **A class participates in a wire format only where it writes so, never structurally** — A class takes part in a wire format only where it says so. ([`core-api/written-participation`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-written-participation))
- **Every `Core` member declares whether it is a sink, a launderer, contagious or neutral** — Every `Core` member states, as a column of its signature rather than as a footnote, whether it is a… ([`core-api/qualifier-behaviour-is-declared`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-qualifier-behaviour-is-declared))
- **No `Core` member mutates its argument and none takes a reference** — No `Core` member mutates an argument and none takes a reference. ([`core-api/nothing-mutates`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-nothing-mutates))
- **Every `Core` value type is immutable, so no mutable twin exists to choose between** — Every `Core` value type is immutable, so there is no mutable twin to choose between. ([`core-api/no-mutable-immutable-twins`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-no-mutable-immutable-twins))
- **No `Core` member reads ambient state: there is no default timezone, locale, array pointer or error global** — No `Core` member reads state the call site did not give it. ([`core-api/no-ambient-state`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-no-ambient-state))
- **A `Core` member throws on failure and returns `?T` for absence; `false` is never an answer** — A `Core` member signals failure by throwing. ([`core-api/failure-throws`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-failure-throws))
- **No operation is reachable two ways, and a domain class's statics never mirror an object's own methods** — One operation is reachable exactly one way. ([`core-api/one-paradigm-per-operation`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-one-paradigm-per-operation))
- **A scalar and an `array<T>` never gain methods** — A scalar and an `array<T>` never gain methods. ([`core-api/no-methods-on-scalars-or-arrays`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-no-methods-on-scalars-or-arrays))
- **A mode is an enum, never a string or an integer constant, and only four grammars are exempt** — A member never takes a mode as a string or as an integer constant. ([`core-api/no-mode-strings`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-no-mode-strings))
- **A unit is a type: a duration is a `Duration` and a size is `uint` bytes** — A quantity carrying a unit is a type, not a number with a convention attached. ([`core-api/units-are-types`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-units-are-types))
- **A `string` member never takes an encoding argument** — No member taking a `string` takes an encoding argument. ([`core-api/no-encoding-argument`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-no-encoding-argument))
- **Every range is `(offset, ?length)`, and a negative counts from the end** — Every member taking a range takes `(offset, ?length)`, and `Core\Str` and `Core\Arr` share the convention exactly. ([`core-api/one-range-convention`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-one-range-convention))
- **A callback always receives `($value, $key)`, and may declare fewer parameters than the call site passes** — A callback a `Core` member invokes always receives `($value, $key)`, in that order, and a closure may declare fewer parameters than the call site passes (`types/callable-arity`). ([`core-api/callback-receives-value-and-key`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-callback-receives-value-and-key))
- **Every `Core` parameter is callable by the name the spec writes, and that name is compatibility surface** — Every parameter of every `Core` member may be written by name at the call site — the `$name` the spec's signature column writes, and the trailing bag under the one name `options` — under exactly the rules a user-declare… ([`core-api/parameters-are-callable-by-name`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-parameters-are-callable-by-name))
- **A member's optional knobs are one trailing shape literal, never a flag or a bitmask** — After the subject come the required arguments in dataflow order, and then **at most one** trailing optional shape literal — an object literal (`types/object-top`) declared as a `type` alias. ([`core-api/options-bag`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-options-bag))
- **Required, optional and nullable are three separate questions: nullability belongs to the type and optionality to the default** *(designed)* — "Does `?T` mean the key may be absent, or that `null` is a legal value?" has a better answer than choosing: they are separate questions, and both already have a spelling. ([`core-api/required-optional-and-nullable`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-required-optional-and-nullable))
- **An options bag tells an omitted key from a written `null`** — A call site's two ways of not giving an options-bag field a value are two different requests. ([`core-api/omission-is-not-a-written-null`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-omission-is-not-a-written-null))
- **A bag or shape field is nullable exactly when its omission fills the never-written marker** — A field of an options bag or of a shape arm carries a default, and that default is what an omitting call site materializes. ([`core-api/a-nullable-field-omits-as-the-never-written-marker`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-a-nullable-field-omits-as-the-never-written-marker))
- **Wherever a `Core` member admits a written `null` it means remove, and `""` is never a removal spelling** — Wherever a `Core` member admits a written `null` — a bag field or an ordinary argument — it means… ([`core-api/a-written-null-removes`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-a-written-null-removes))
- **The never-written marker is not in the type system and is never handed to user code** — The never-written marker is not a value a program can hold, observe or name. ([`core-api/the-marker-never-reaches-a-program`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-the-marker-never-reaches-a-program))
- **The three-state bag changes which constant fills a slot and nothing else about the ABI** — The three-state bag changes *which constant fills one slot, for one kind of field*, and nothing else. ([`core-api/the-bag-abi-is-unchanged`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-the-bag-abi-is-unchanged))
- **Where the registry and the spec both describe an implemented member, precedence is field by field** — For an implemented member, a documentation field the registry carries is authoritative and a field it lacks falls back to the spec-derived default. ([`core-api/field-wise-precedence`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-field-wise-precedence))
- **A fixed-key shape parameter is one type carrying its arms, and it is only ever a whole parameter** — A required, positional, fixed-key shape parameter is declared as **one type carrying a non-empty list of arms**, each arm an ordered field list: one arm for the ordinary case, two or more for a discriminated union. ([`core-api/shape-parameter`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-shape-parameter))
- **A shape's arms are pairwise disjoint, so exactly one accepts a written literal and no field is declared a discriminant** — A written shape literal is checked by asking which arm accepts it, where an arm accepts when the literal's keys are exactly that arm's required keys plus any subset of its optional ones, each value assignable to its fie… ([`core-api/shape-arms-are-disjoint`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-shape-arms-are-disjoint))
