- **The options bag and the shape parameter are two registry spellings of one checked type** — The trailing options bag and the fixed-key shape parameter are two registry spellings that intern into… ([`core-api/one-checked-shape-type`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-one-checked-shape-type))

- **Cross-request state is reached through a member per tier, each with its own contract, never one API with a flag** — Cross-request state is reached through **a member per tier, each with its own contract**, not one member with a flag. - **`Core\Cli::arguments` is how a program reads the words it was started with, at every depth** — `Core\Cli::arguments()` answers the words the program was started with, as an `array<tainted string>`. ([`core-classes/cli-arguments`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-cli-arguments))

- **`open` orients and converts to sRGB, and `encode` strips metadata unless the plan kept it** *(designed)* — Three defaults make the common result the correct one. ([`core-classes/image-correct-by-default`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-image-correct-by-default))
- **Comparison, hashing, placeholders, text, QR codes and SVG are one entry point each, because each is one job** *(designed)* — Beyond the pipeline, each remaining job is exactly one entry point. ([`core-classes/image-one-entry-point-per-job`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-image-one-entry-point-per-job))
- **PDF generation is a first-party extension that performs no I/O, and an unresolved asset throws** *(designed)* — PDF generation is a first-party Tier 1 extension package, sandboxed, with everything a program names under one namespace and one registered class. ([`core-classes/pdf-render-has-no-io`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-render-has-no-io))
- **The only input language is HTML plus a CSS subset, and every backend answers that one interface** *(designed)* — The sole input language is **HTML plus the CSS subset plus inline SVG**. ([`core-classes/pdf-one-engine`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-one-engine))
- **The CSS subset is documented, and the render result lists every declaration it dropped** *(designed)* — The engine implements a **documented subset** of CSS — block and inline flow, tables, flex, fonts, images, inline SVG and the page family are the working floor — and handles everything outside it by CSS's own forward-co… ([`core-classes/pdf-css-subset`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-css-subset))
- **The writer emits nothing a reader would execute, and equal input gives byte-equal output** *(designed)* — The writer never emits JavaScript, launch actions, embedded files, or any construct that makes a reader fetch or execute on open. ([`core-classes/pdf-output-is-inert`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-output-is-inert))
- **A PDF page is a decode-only format of the image component: one page per `open`, priced by the pixel cap** *(designed)* — A PDF is a **decode-only format of the image component**, not a member of the PDF generation package: a writer and an interpreter share no code, and a raster produced there would have to recross the boundary to enter th… ([`core-classes/pdf-page-is-an-image-source`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-page-is-an-image-source))
- **An encrypted document and a detectable omission both throw, and everything past rasterising is somebody else's job** *(designed)* — An **encrypted document throws** naming the encryption. ([`core-classes/pdf-decode-refusals`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-decode-refusals))
- **The spreadsheet component is a first-party extension that fetches nothing and executes nothing it reads** *(designed)* — Spreadsheet reading and generation are one first-party Tier 1 extension package, sandboxed, with one registered class and everything else Novis source that calls it. ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-has-no-io`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-has-no-io))
- **Only an explicit `Formula` value writes a formula cell, so an export built from user data is inert** *(designed)* — Only an explicit `Formula` value produces a formula cell. ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value))
- **A workbook crosses the boundary in whole blocks, and a bomb is refused before a sheet buffer exists** *(designed)* — The builder assembles the whole document — sheets, cells, styles, charts — as Novis values, and… ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-bulk-boundary`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-bulk-boundary))
- **The roster is read-wide and write-narrow, a macro is never written, and evaluation is an explicit call** *(designed)* — The roster is **read-wide and write-narrow**. ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-evaluation-and-roster`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-evaluation-and-roster))
- **The writer embeds no executable content and no entropy, so equal input gives byte-equal output** *(designed)* — The writer emits no macros, no embedded executables and no launch-shaped content; hyperlinks exist only where the document wrote them. ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-output-is-inert`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-output-is-inert))
- **`Core\Net` is one class over TCP, UDP and Unix sockets, reached through five entry points that park on the runtime's own reactor** — `Core\Net` is the whole socket surface, replacing PHP's `socket_*`, `stream_socket_*` and `fsockopen` with one class over three transports: TCP, UDP and Unix-domain sockets. ([`core-classes/net-one-api-three-transports`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-net-one-api-three-transports))
- **A `Core\Net` socket closes with the request that opened it, so there is no persistent connection and no pool across requests** *(designed)* — A socket opened through `Core\Net` closes with the request that opened it. ([`core-classes/net-a-socket-does-not-outlive-its-request`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-net-a-socket-does-not-outlive-its-request))
- **A datagram socket sends and receives messages and offers no ordering, retransmission or acknowledgement above them** *(designed)* — A `Core\Net` datagram socket sends and receives messages, reports what it sent and what arrived, and offers nothing above that: no ordering, no retransmission, no fragmentation and no acknowledgement. ([`core-classes/net-udp-carries-no-reliability-layer`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-net-udp-carries-no-reliability-layer))

## Observability

- **Production telemetry is read from the instrumentation that already exists, and adds no probe site to the measured path** — Production telemetry — the default metric series, the spans, the trace ids on a log line — is read from instrumentation the runtime already has: the per-statement and per-call probes of `testing/debug-probes`, and the `… ([`observability/the-runtime-exports-what-it-already-measures`](rules/observability.md#observability-the-runtime-exports-what-it-already-measures))
- **A trace id exists for every request whatever the sampling decision, and it is the only request identifier** — A trace id is drawn for every request when its context is built, whatever the sampling decision. ([`observability/a-trace-id-exists-for-every-request`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-trace-id-exists-for-every-request))
- **A log record inside an active trace carries `trace_id` and `span_id`, and outside one omits both rather than writing them empty** — The JSON-Lines record `errors/log-write` defines gains `trace_id` and `span_id` whenever a trace is active. ([`observability/a-log-record-carries-trace-ids-when-a-trace-is-active`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-log-record-carries-trace-ids-when-a-trace-is-active))
- **`Core\Metrics` is three verbs for three kinds, always present, and accumulates whether or not an exporter is built** — `increment` for a counter, `observe` for a histogram, `gauge` for a point-in-time value — three verbs for three kinds, rather than one `record` with a kind enum, because the kind is a property of the series and not of t… ([`observability/metrics-three-members`](rules/observability.md#observability-metrics-three-members))
- **Ten series exist the moment an exporter is configured, with no application code written** *(designed)* — Ten series are present the moment an exporter is configured, with no application code written:… ([`observability/default-series`](rules/observability.md#observability-default-series))
- **A metric name is fixed to one kind and one label set on first use, and a second kind throws naming both sites** *(designed)* — A metric name is fixed to one kind — counter, histogram or gauge — on its first use within a process, and its label *names* are fixed with it. ([`observability/a-name-is-fixed-to-one-kind`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-name-is-fixed-to-one-kind))
- **The `route` label carries the route's declared name, never the request path, and a route without one has no label** — The `route` label on the request series carries the route's **declared name** from the compile-time table of `routing/routes-are-compiled-not-registered` — a closed set known when the program is built — and never the re… ([`observability/route-label-is-the-declared-name`](rules/observability.md#observability-route-label-is-the-declared-name))
- **A metrics registry is per core, merged at scrape, and no program reads a metric** — Each core holds its own metrics registry, and a scrape merges them. ([`observability/a-registry-is-per-core-and-nothing-reads-it`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-registry-is-per-core-and-nothing-reads-it))
- **Past `max_series` a new series is refused and an existing one is never evicted** — `[metrics] max_series` bounds the number of distinct label combinations one **core** holds. ([`observability/past-max-series-a-new-series-is-refused`](rules/observability.md#observability-past-max-series-a-new-series-is-refused))
- **`[metrics]` and `[trace]` are `System` blocks, and a value neither exporter accepts is refused at boot** — Both blocks are **`System`** (`config/system-means-a-request-may-not-set-it`): where a process ships telemetry, and how much it costs to do so, is a deployment decision, and a request able to turn tracing on for itself… ([`observability/metrics-and-trace-blocks-are-system`](rules/observability.md#observability-metrics-and-trace-blocks-are-system))
- **Exactly four things become a span, and a `call` event never does** — A distributed trace is not the per-call trace `testing/debug-probes` produces, and conflating them would give a trace one span per function call, which no backend can store and no human can read. ([`observability/four-kinds-become-a-span`](rules/observability.md#observability-four-kinds-become-a-span))
- **A `call` event never becomes a span; the root, a `query`, an outbound HTTP call and a `spawn` do, and `gc` becomes a metric** *(designed)* — Production telemetry reads the same four event kinds the trace records and adds no instrumentation of its own — and it is bound by one rule the taxonomy owns: **a `call`-kind event never becomes a distributed-tracing sp… ([`observability/a-call-never-becomes-a-span`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-call-never-becomes-a-span))
- **A trace event carries one of five kinds — `call`, `gc`, `spawn`, `query`, `http` — and a `call` keeps its probe shape** — Every trace event carries a `kind` tag, and the tag is one of exactly five: `call`, `gc`, `spawn`, `query`, `http`. ([`observability/trace-events-carry-a-kind`](rules/observability.md#observability-trace-events-carry-a-kind))
- **A statement is a `query` trace event that carries its duration, driver, connection, truncated SQL and row counts, and never a bound parameter** — A statement is a `query` trace event, beside `call`, `gc` and `spawn`, instrumented in the driver's own statement routine and off the hot path exactly as those two are. ([`observability/a-query-is-a-trace-event`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-query-is-a-trace-event))
- **A `[db.<name>] slow_query` threshold writes a statement's span facts to `Core\Log`, and is off until a block writes one** — A `[db.<name>]` block may write `slow_query`, a duration such as `"200ms"` or `"1s"`; a statement on that connection that runs longer writes the same facts its trace event carries — duration, driver, connection, truncat… ([`observability/a-slow-query-is-logged-past-a-threshold`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-slow-query-is-logged-past-a-threshold))
- **A collector pause is a `gc` event recorded from the collector's run routine, never from the safepoint poll** — A stop-the-world collection run is a trace event of its own, `kind: gc`, recorded from **inside the cycle collector's run routine** and gated by the same `TRACE`/`PROFILE` bits `Ctx` already carries. ([`observability/gc-pause-is-its-own-event`](rules/observability.md#observability-gc-pause-is-its-own-event))
- **A spawn and its join are one `spawn` event naming the form it was, with an overhead split where the child reports its own time, and a child's own stream never crosses live** — Each spawn construct — `spawn`, `spawn worker`, `spawn script`, and `Core\Process::spawn`, whose child is the operating system's rather than an isolate — emits a `kind: spawn` event from its own runtime routine, and its… ([`observability/spawn-is-its-own-event`](rules/observability.md#observability-spawn-is-its-own-event))
- **An inbound `traceparent` is continued, and one the process cannot read starts a new trace rather than failing the request** — An inbound W3C `traceparent` header continues the trace: its trace id and parent span id are adopted, and its sampled flag is honoured. ([`observability/an-inbound-traceparent-is-continued`](rules/observability.md#observability-an-inbound-traceparent-is-continued))
- **`Core\Http\Client` sends `traceparent` while `[trace] propagate` is on, and the id it sends is the request's own** — `Core\Http\Client` sends `traceparent` on every outbound call while `[trace] propagate` is on, which is what makes a trace cross a service boundary at all. ([`observability/an-outbound-call-propagates-traceparent`](rules/observability.md#observability-an-outbound-call-propagates-traceparent))
- **Sampling is decided once at the root by `[trace] sample`, and an inbound trace that is already sampled is always continued** — Sampling is **head-based at the root**: `[trace] sample` is the probability, from `0.0` to `1.0`, that a *new* trace is recorded. ([`observability/sampling-is-head-based`](rules/observability.md#observability-sampling-is-head-based))
- **The exporter is a feature-gated Native subsystem, and `Core\Metrics` is Tier 0 in every build** — The exporter — the Prometheus scrape endpoint and the OTLP client — is a **Native, feature-gated** subsystem (`core-api/five-placements`), on by default in the server distribution, so a CLI binary or a single-file execu… ([`observability/the-exporter-is-a-feature-and-core-metrics-is-not`](rules/observability.md#observability-the-exporter-is-a-feature-and-core-metrics-is-not))
- **The OTLP and Prometheus paths are somebody else's specification, implemented here; the wiring and the registry are ours** — The OTLP path, including the W3C TraceContext propagator, and the Prometheus scrape path are somebody else's specification, and they are implemented against it behind the feature `observability/the-exporter-is-a-feature… ([`observability/the-exporters-are-crates`](rules/observability.md#observability-the-exporters-are-crates))
- **An exporter brings no second registry, no second scheduler and no second client, and a crate is taken only for an encoder** — An exporter brings no second registry, no second scheduler and no second client: a crate is taken for a half that needs none of those — an encoder — and never for a half that carries its own execution or its own socket. ([`observability/an-exporter-brings-no-second-scheduler-and-no-second-client`](rules/observability.md#observability-an-exporter-brings-no-second-scheduler-and-no-second-client))
- **The four event kinds export as one speedscope evented timeline, beside Callgrind, Clover/lcov and NDJSON** *(designed)* — A `TRACE`-flagged run exports its `call`, `gc`, `spawn` and `query` events as speedscope's evented-profile JSON — open/close pairs at a timestamp, which is exactly what the trace already holds. ([`observability/speedscope-timeline-export`](rules/observability.md#observability-speedscope-timeline-export))
- **A request reads its own memory as `memoryHeld`, `memoryPeak` and `memoryLimit` on `Core\Budget`, and the process's resident bytes are `Core\Os`'s** — A request reads its own memory as three members on `Core\Budget` — `memoryHeld()` is the bytes it holds right now, `memoryPeak()` the high-water mark of that figure for this request, and `memoryLimit()` the ceiling both… ([`observability/memory-is-three-numbers-on-core-budget`](rules/observability.md#observability-memory-is-three-numbers-on-core-budget))
- **The runtime records a request's memory high-water mark in every build, and a nested isolate restores the enclosing mark rather than clobbering it** — The runtime keeps a request's memory high-water mark in every build, updated where the live-byte balance is updated, and a nested `Ctx` restores the larger of its own mark and the one it displaced rather than clobbering… ([`observability/a-memory-peak-is-recorded-not-asked-for`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-memory-peak-is-recorded-not-asked-for))
- **A `[limits] memory_high_water` fraction writes one `Warn` when a request's memory peak crosses that share of its ceiling, and is off until a block writes one** *(designed)* — A `[limits]` block may write `memory_high_water`, a fraction between `0.0` and `1.0`; a request whose memory peak crosses that share of its effective ceiling writes one `Warn` to `Core\Log` at the end of the request, na… ([`observability/memory-high-water-writes-a-warn`](rules/observability.md#observability-memory-high-water-writes-a-warn))
- **`Core\Script::onExit` registers a request-local hook that runs FIFO as the last user code, and each hook receives one readonly `ExitReport`** — `Core\Script::onExit(callable $hook): void` registers a hook that runs as the **last user code of the script**. ([`observability/script-on-exit`](rules/observability.md#observability-script-on-exit))
- **The exit queue drains once — at a normal end, at `exit` and at an uncaught throw — and the report says which ending it was** — Three endings fire the exit queue, and the report each hook receives says which:… ([`observability/three-endings-fire-the-exit-queue`](rules/observability.md#observability-three-endings-fire-the-exit-queue))
- **Exit hooks run after every `finally` and after the failure hooks, and before native teardown, with the heap alive and output where it was** — On the throw path the order is fixed: the unwind's `finally` blocks, innermost first; then `errors/on-uncaught-throw`'s handler; then this queue; then native teardown. ([`observability/exit-hooks-run-after-the-ladder-before-teardown`](rules/observability.md#observability-exit-hooks-run-after-the-ladder-before-teardown))
- **A `FATAL` and a cancellation run no exit hook — `Core\Fatal::onLimit` is the one observer of a limit breach** — Two terminations never fire the exit queue. ([`observability/a-fatal-and-a-cancellation-run-no-exit-hook`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-fatal-and-a-cancellation-run-no-exit-hook))
- **A hook observes the ending and never steers it: the report is fixed first, a throw is logged and abandoned, `exit` inside a hook throws, and the drain continues** — The report — reason and status — is fixed before the first hook runs, and nothing a hook does changes it. ([`observability/a-hook-observes-and-never-steers`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-hook-observes-and-never-steers))

## The HTTP server

- **The server is a development server or a proxied production origin, and nothing a proxy does earlier is in it** — The built-in server has exactly two deployments. ([`http-server/two-deployments-and-nothing-a-proxy-owns`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-two-deployments-and-nothing-a-proxy-owns))
- **The `[server]` block is `Boot`-class, `listen` is one flat array defaulting to `127.0.0.1:8000` in both modes, and the flag is the last word** — The whole block is `Boot`-class (`config/three-changeability-classes`): `header_timeout` and `keepalive_timeout` apply before any Novis code exists on a connection, so a `Runtime` class would be a promise the block coul… ([`http-server/the-server-block-is-boot-class`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-server-block-is-boot-class))
- **A mount matches on `prefix` or `host`, names one `entry` or one `scan`, and a scan expands against the disk at boot** — A mount matches on `prefix`, on `host`, or on both, and names **either** `entry` (one literal file) **or** `scan` (a glob); both or neither is a boot error. ([`http-server/a-mount-table-expands-at-boot`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-mount-table-expands-at-boot))
- **A mount's key set is `prefix`, `host`, `scan`, `entry` and `origin`; `mode`, limits and capabilities belong to the `[[app]]` block** — A `[[server.mount]]` carries no `mode`, no limits and no capabilities. ([`http-server/a-mount-carries-no-policy`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-mount-carries-no-policy))
- **A `listen` entry beginning with a separator is a Unix socket, Unix-only, with `socket_mode`, and it is the transport a proxy should prefer** — A `[server] listen` entry beginning with a path separator names a Unix-domain socket; because no `host:port` can begin that way the overload is unambiguous, and `socket_mode` applies to those entries only. ([`http-server/a-unix-socket-listener`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-unix-socket-listener))
- **`[mode] ceiling` is `System`-class, bounds a runtime flip and not the startup value, and unset equals the mode the server started in** — `[mode] ceiling` states the most permissive mode any code on the host may select. ([`http-server/the-mode-ceiling-defaults-to-the-startup-mode`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-mode-ceiling-defaults-to-the-startup-mode))
- **A development-mode server binding a non-loopback address prints a banner, writes one `Warn` record naming the address, and serves** *(designed)* — When the server binds a non-loopback address while the mode is `development`, it emits an unmissable startup banner **and** a `Warn` record naming the bound address (`errors/log-level`), then serves. ([`http-server/a-development-server-on-a-public-interface-warns-and-serves`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-development-server-on-a-public-interface-warns-and-serves))
- **A default that is unsafe inbound or unbounded outbound is a defect, not a neutral starting point** — A default that is unsafe inbound or unbounded outbound is a defect, not a neutral starting point a deployment is expected to improve on. ([`http-server/an-unsafe-or-unbounded-default-is-a-defect`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-an-unsafe-or-unbounded-default-is-a-defect))
- **Every `[server] listen` entry is bound before any core accepts, each core holds its own handle on every listener, and `[server] workers` bounds the count over the machine's available parallelism** — `nvs serve` binds every entry of `[server] listen` before it accepts anything, and then starts one worker per core, each holding its own handle on every one of those listeners — so a connection is accepted by whichever… ([`http-server/the-accept-fan-out-is-one-worker-per-core`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-accept-fan-out-is-one-worker-per-core))
- **`max_in_flight` is a process-wide valve that answers a fixed `503` with `Retry-After` before an isolate exists** — `[server] max_in_flight` (`10000`) is a process-wide safety valve, not a worker pool. ([`http-server/max-in-flight-refuses-before-allocating`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-max-in-flight-refuses-before-allocating))
- **The effective in-flight ceiling is the smaller of `max_in_flight` and what the memory budget affords, and a clamp is logged once at boot** — `max_in_flight` refuses work before allocating an isolate, which is the right shape. ([`http-server/admission-is-arithmetic-not-a-number`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-admission-is-arithmetic-not-a-number))
- **Four waits bound a connection, all finite with nothing configured and all idle rather than total** — Four waits bound every connection — `header_timeout` (`10s`), `body_idle_timeout` (`30s`), `write_idle_timeout` (`30s`) and `keepalive_timeout` (`75s`) — and all four are finite with nothing configured. ([`http-server/four-idle-waits-all-finite`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-four-idle-waits-all-finite))
- **An `accept` that fails on descriptor exhaustion is retried under a bounded backoff and logged once per window** — An `accept` that fails with `EMFILE`/`ENFILE` returns immediately and will fail again immediately, which turns descriptor exhaustion into a core pinned at full utilisation for as long as the condition lasts — and, becau… ([`http-server/the-accept-loop-backs-off`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-accept-loop-backs-off))
- **A request resolves by longest mount match, prefix strip, static file, path dispatch, then the entry — and production runs only match, strip, entry** — In production — `dispatch = "entry"`, `static = false` — steps 3 and 4 do not run: match, strip, run the entry. ([`http-server/a-request-resolves-in-five-steps`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-request-resolves-in-five-steps))
- **`trusted_proxies` defaults to empty, empty means the forwarded headers are never read, and a trusted walk takes the rightmost untrusted `X-Forwarded-For` entry** — `[server] trusted_proxies` defaults to empty, and **empty means the forwarded headers are not read at all**: `Core\Request::clientIp()` is the socket peer and `X-Forwarded-For` is never parsed. ([`http-server/trusted-proxies-is-empty-and-empty-reads-nothing`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-trusted-proxies-is-empty-and-empty-reads-nothing))
- **`X-Forwarded-For` is the only client-address header read; a trusted peer sending another is warned about, and an untrusted header is ignored, never refused** — `X-Forwarded-For` is the only client-address header read. ([`http-server/x-forwarded-for-is-the-only-address-header`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-x-forwarded-for-is-the-only-address-header))
- **A forwarded token's port is removed, a withheld address answers `null`, and a token that neither names nor withholds one is a `400`** — The token the trusted walk lands on resolves one of three ways. ([`http-server/a-forwarded-token-is-read-withheld-or-refused`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-forwarded-token-is-read-withheld-or-refused))
- **A trusted `X-Forwarded-Proto` sets the effective scheme and HSTS emission and feeds nothing else; no `X-Forwarded-Host` is read** — `X-Forwarded-Proto` from a trusted peer sets the effective scheme, and feeds exactly two things: `Core\Request::scheme()` and HSTS emission. ([`http-server/x-forwarded-proto-sets-the-scheme-and-hsts-only`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-x-forwarded-proto-sets-the-scheme-and-hsts-only))
- **An absent `Host` is a `400`; matching strips the port, folds ASCII case and one trailing dot, refuses non-ASCII, and an unknown host on a host-mounted deployment is a `404`** *(designed)* — An absent `Host` on HTTP/1.1 is a `400`. ([`http-server/host-matching-is-on-the-host-part-only`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-host-matching-is-on-the-host-part-only))
- **A filesystem path is never derived from a URL at request time** — A request may **select** an entry point from a set enumerated before it arrived; it may never **construct** one. ([`http-server/a-path-is-never-derived-from-a-url`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-path-is-never-derived-from-a-url))
- **A trailing slash is never normalised: `/users` and `/users/` are two URIs** — `/users` and `/users/` are different URIs, and whether they name one resource is application knowledge. ([`http-server/a-trailing-slash-is-never-normalised`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-trailing-slash-is-never-normalised))
- **`HEAD` runs as `GET` with the body discarded and `Content-Length` kept; `method()` reports `Get` and `isHead()` tells the truth** — `HEAD` is implemented, and it is conformance rather than convention: RFC 9110 requires a general-purpose server to support it. ([`http-server/head-runs-as-get`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-head-runs-as-get))
- **A CORS preflight is answered from `[http.cors]` before the unit is loaded, and a plain `OPTIONS` is passed through** — A CORS preflight — an `OPTIONS` carrying both `Origin` and `Access-Control-Request-Method` — is answered from `[http.cors]` **before any application code runs and therefore before the compiled unit is loaded**. ## Routing

- **A route is a `#[Route]` compiled into the unit's table, and its three runtime bugs are compile errors** — A route is declared where its handler is: `#[Route(path: "/users/{id}", method: Http\Method::Get, name: "user.show")]` on a method. ([`routing/routes-are-compiled-not-registered`](rules/routing.md#routing-routes-are-compiled-not-registered))
- **`#[Route]` is `{path, method, name?}` on a method, recognized by name and never by shape** — `type Core\Route = {path: string, method: Core\Http\Method, name?: string};` — an ordinary `attributes/inert-metadata` alias, attached the ordinary way, with one difference: the compiler acts on it only when the name **… ([`routing/route-attribute`](rules/routing.md#routing-route-attribute))
- **A path is literal segments and three capture forms, each capture a whole segment naming a parameter** — A path is a literal string beginning at the root, validated while checking, whose segments are literals or captures:… ([`routing/path-grammar`](rules/routing.md#routing-path-grammar))
- **There is no wildcard verb: `method` is required, singular, and one case of a closed enum** — There is no `Method::Any`, no omitted `method` and no multi-valued `method`. ([`routing/no-wildcard-verb`](rules/routing.md#routing-no-wildcard-verb))
- **Precedence is structural — a literal beats a capture beats an optional beats a catch-all — never declaration order** — Where two routes of one verb both match a path, the more literal one wins, segment by segment: a literal beats a `{name}`, which beats a `{name?}`, which beats a `{name...}`. ([`routing/precedence-is-structural`](rules/routing.md#routing-precedence-is-structural))
- **A capture narrows to a closed set with a literal-union or enum-subset type, never with a regex** — A capture's type may be a **union of `string` or `int` literal types**, or a **subset of an enum's cases** (`types/literal-types`), beside the scalar and enum types a capture already converts to. ([`routing/a-capture-narrows-to-a-closed-set`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-capture-narrows-to-a-closed-set))
- **An enum capture is spelled by a written backing value, and by its case name when the value was counted** — An enum capture matches on its case's **written** backing value, and on the **case name** when the value was counted rather than written, in a path segment and in a `#[Query]` value alike. ([`routing/an-enum-capture-is-spelled-by-its-backing-value-or-its-case-name`](rules/routing.md#routing-an-enum-capture-is-spelled-by-its-backing-value-or-its-case-name))
- **`{name?}` captures one trailing segment or none, and its parameter's default is what makes the absent case well-typed** — `{name?}` captures one whole segment or none. ([`routing/a-trailing-segment-may-be-absent`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-trailing-segment-may-be-absent))
- **A `#[Query]` parameter is declared with a capture's type list, and a default is what makes it optional** — `#[Query]` on a parameter of a `#[Route]` method declares that the parameter is bound from the request's query string, by the parameter's own name — the attribute carries nothing that could give it another key. ([`routing/a-query-parameter-is-declared-like-a-capture`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-query-parameter-is-declared-like-a-capture))
- **A query value that fails to convert is a `400`, where a path capture that fails is a `404`** *(designed)* — A `#[Query]` parameter's value converts to its declared type and arrives unqualified, exactly as a path capture does — and fails differently. ([`routing/a-bad-query-value-is-a-400`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-bad-query-value-is-a-400))
- **One method's repeated routes may share a `name` only when they share a `path`; every other duplicate name is a compile error** — `#[Route]` is repeatable (`attributes/repeatable`), and repeating it is how one method serves several verbs. ([`routing/repeated-routes-share-a-name-when-they-share-a-path`](rules/routing.md#routing-repeated-routes-share-a-name-when-they-share-a-path))
- **A shared name is one `url()` target, one `Match::name` for every verb, and one `operationId` per verb** — A route whose repeated attributes share a `name` is one thing everywhere it is observed:… ([`routing/a-shared-name-is-one-endpoint-everywhere`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-shared-name-is-one-endpoint-everywhere))
- **The router stops at matching: a match is a name and typed parameters, and nothing here dispatches** — The server matches a request once, before any application code, and `Core\Request::route()` is that match; `match` asks the same table about a verb and a path the program chose. ([`routing/matching-is-not-dispatching`](rules/routing.md#routing-matching-is-not-dispatching))
- **A match carries a name and typed parameters and nothing invocable, and typed `callable` would not change that** — `Core\Router\Match` carries a declared name and the typed captures the path filled, and nothing invocable: no `->invoke()`, no callable, no class-and-method strings. ([`routing/a-match-is-not-invocable`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-match-is-not-invocable))
- **A request is matched once, before any application code runs, and `Core\Request::route()` is that match** — The server matches the incoming request against the compiled table **once**, before any application code runs, and records the result on the request. ([`routing/matched-once-before-the-handler`](rules/routing.md#routing-matched-once-before-the-handler))
- **The server's match dispatches nothing, and a request the table does not claim is served by the program** — The server computes a name and typed parameters and stops there. ([`routing/the-servers-match-dispatches-nothing`](rules/routing.md#routing-the-servers-match-dispatches-nothing))
- **A missing path and a refused verb are different answers, and `methodsFor` is what tells them apart** — `Core\Router::methodsFor(tainted string $path): array<Http\Method>` tells a missing path from a refused verb. ([`routing/a-refused-verb-is-not-a-missing-path`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-refused-verb-is-not-a-missing-path))
- **`Core\Request::mount()` answers the prefix the door stripped and the tainted host captures, and it is never `null`** — `Core\Request::mount(): Core\Request\Mount` answers the two facts about the door a request came through: `prefix(): string` is what the mount stripped from the path before the program saw it, and `captures(): array<tain… ([`routing/a-request-reads-its-mount`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-request-reads-its-mount))
- **`Core\Router::url` is a launderer whose literal name and `$params` are checked against the compiled table** — `Core\Router::url(string $name, array<string, mixed> $params): string` reverses the table by name, and the compiler resolves the call against the whole program's table after every file has been walked — the route may be… ([`routing/link-name-and-params-are-checked`](rules/routing.md#routing-link-name-and-params-are-checked))
- **A link carries the mount prefix the request arrived under, so one table serves at any mount** — `Core\Router::url` prepends the prefix of the mount the request arrived through, in front of the substituted path. ([`routing/link-carries-the-mount-prefix`](rules/routing.md#routing-link-carries-the-mount-prefix))
- **A `url()` key that is not a capture becomes a percent-encoded query string, and one that is neither a capture nor a declared `#[Query]` parameter does not compile** — A `$params` key handed to `Core\Router::url` or `urlAbsolute` that names no capture becomes a percent-encoded query string, spelled exactly as `Core\Uri::buildQuery` spells it: `url("posts.index", {page: 3, sort: "desc"… ([`routing/a-leftover-link-key-is-a-query-string`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-leftover-link-key-is-a-query-string))
- **`urlAbsolute` prepends a configured origin and never one sniffed from a request header** — `Core\Router::urlAbsolute(string $name, array<string, mixed> $params): string` is `Core\Router::url` with the configured origin in front — the same laundered path, the same query-string rule (`routing/a-leftover-link-ke… ([`routing/an-absolute-link-takes-a-configured-origin`](rules/routing.md#routing-an-absolute-link-takes-a-configured-origin))
- **An origin is declared per mount with `[app] origin` as the fallback, a request cannot set it, and a mount that calls `urlAbsolute` without one is a boot error** — The origin `urlAbsolute` prepends (`routing/an-absolute-link-takes-a-configured-origin`) is declared **per mount**, on the `[[server.mount]]` block, falling back to `[app] origin`. ([`routing/an-origin-is-per-mount-and-checked-at-boot`](rules/routing.md#routing-an-origin-is-per-mount-and-checked-at-boot))
- **The table is built by the program enumeration, and a program with no `#[Route]` builds none and pays nothing** — Finding routes is the question the program enumeration was built for — *what exists that nothing names* — and the route table is that enumeration filtered by `#[Route]`, reused wholesale with its consequences (`programs… ([`routing/table-is-opt-in`](rules/routing.md#routing-table-is-opt-in))
- **The API document is generated from the route table while compiling, so it cannot drift from the code** — The OpenAPI 3.1 document is a rendering of the compiler's own route table. ([`routing/api-document-is-generated-from-the-route-table`](rules/routing.md#routing-api-document-is-generated-from-the-route-table))
- **`nvs build --openapi` writes OpenAPI 3.1 as a build artifact, and two builds of one source are byte-identical** — `nvs build --openapi <file>` runs the program through the same front end `nvs check` uses and writes the OpenAPI 3.1 document, pretty-printed, to standard output. ([`routing/api-document-is-a-deterministic-build-artifact`](rules/routing.md#routing-api-document-is-a-deterministic-build-artifact))
- **`nvs api diff` classifies every change as breaking, additive or cosmetic, and exits non-zero on a breaking one** — `nvs api diff <old.json> <new.json>` compares two generated documents as JSON values rather than as text, prints one line per change worst-first, and exits non-zero if any change is **breaking**. ([`routing/api-diff-fails-a-breaking-change`](rules/routing.md#routing-api-diff-fails-a-breaking-change))
- **A `#[Route]` missing its `path` gets a quick fix that offers a derived one, and nothing derives a path on its own** *(designed)* — Nothing derives a `path` or a `name` from the declaring class. ([`routing/a-quick-fix-writes-a-derived-path`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-quick-fix-writes-a-derived-path))

## Configuration

- **The configuration file is `nvs.toml`, and it is TOML** — The server configuration is a TOML file named `nvs.toml`, read into the directive registry through the `toml` crate and `serde` — at boot, and again on each reload, which parses and validates a whole replacement before… ([`config/the-file-is-nvs-toml-and-it-is-toml`](rules/config.md#config-the-file-is-nvs-toml-and-it-is-toml))
- **A size or a duration is a quoted string carrying its suffix, a count is an integer, and `false` removes a ceiling** — A size or a duration is written as a **quoted string carrying its suffix** — `memory = "128M"`, `cpu_time = "5s"` — never as a bare integer of implied units. ([`config/a-size-or-duration-is-a-quoted-string-with-its-suffix`](rules/config.md#config-a-size-or-duration-is-a-quoted-string-with-its-suffix))
- **A list is a TOML array, a repeated record is an array of tables, and a dotted key is table nesting** — A directive holding several values is a TOML array, and a directive that is a repeated record with more than one field is an array of tables:… ([`config/lists-are-arrays-and-repeated-records-are-arrays-of-tables`](rules/config.md#config-lists-are-arrays-and-repeated-records-are-arrays-of-tables))
- **A duplicate key is an error, and so is an unknown one — per file** — The same key set twice in one file is refused (`E0604`), and so is a key the registry does not know (`E0601`) — both name the file and the line. - **The block roster is closed, and each block's directives are argued by the rule that adds it** — The set of top-level blocks is closed, and the typed tree refuses any other with the unknown-key diagnostic (`config/a-duplicate-key-is-an-error-and-so-is-an-unknown-one`). - **`nvs.toml` is a deployment file, never a project manifest, and it is never found by walking up** — `nvs.toml` is a root-owned deployment file. ([`config/nvs-toml-is-not-a-project-manifest`](rules/config.md#config-nvs-toml-is-not-a-project-manifest))
- **The root of the tree is every `--config` in order, else `./nvs.toml`, else the shipped defaults** — Four steps, first hit wins:… ([`config/the-root-is-config-else-nvs-toml-else-the-shipped-defaults`](rules/config.md#config-the-root-is-config-else-nvs-toml-else-the-shipped-defaults))
- **A host with no configuration file runs on the shipped defaults, which are a complete configuration and not an error** — When no `--config` is given and no `./nvs.toml` exists, the host runs on the **shipped defaults**, and those are a complete and valid configuration rather than a failure to find one: capabilities deny-all, `[mode] defau… ([`config/no-configuration-file-is-a-complete-configuration`](rules/config.md#config-no-configuration-file-is-a-complete-configuration))
- **The resolved root is canonicalized once at boot, announced with every file it reached, and re-read from that stored path on reload** *(designed)* — Whichever step won is **canonicalized to an absolute path once, at boot, and stored**. - **An include cycle is refused with the chain named, and nesting past eight is refused as depth** — An include tree that reaches a file already on the chain is refused with the whole chain named (`E0606`), and nesting deeper than eight files is refused as depth under the same code — not as a cycle, because it may not… ([`config/an-include-cycle-is-refused-and-nesting-is-capped-at-eight`](rules/config.md#config-an-include-cycle-is-refused-and-nesting-is-capped-at-eight))
- **The tree is one ordered stream, a later assignment wins, and every override is recorded with both origins** — The tree flattens to a single sequence: for each `--config` file in order, that file's own keys, then its includes depth-first in list order; then the next `--config` file. - **Every file the configuration reads, and its directory, must be owned by the runtime account or root and writable by nobody else** — must not be group- or world-writable.** Its containing directory must pass the same check, ownership included and not only the mode: an entry can be replaced by whoever can write the directory holding it, whatever the f… ([`config/ownership-is-the-trust-boundary`](rules/config.md#config-ownership-is-the-trust-boundary))

- **A refused `Core\Config::set` returns `false` and leaves the value unchanged; it is never clamped** — A `Core\Config::set` that the changeability class or a ceiling refuses **returns `false` and leaves the value in force untouched**. - **`ini_set` is `Core\Config::set`, and the whole family crosses as strings** — `classes/no-free-functions-or-constants` removes `ini_set`, `ini_get`, `ini_restore` and `ini_get_all` independently of the format; the names go with the file:… ([`config/ini-set-is-core-config-set`](rules/config.md#config-ini-set-is-core-config-set))

- **There is no network-reachable control surface, in either direction of configuration** — There is no TCP listener, in either direction of configuration. ([`config/no-network-control-surface`](rules/config.md#config-no-network-control-surface))
