- **`origin` and `mode` sit on the `[[app]]` block itself, and there is no global `[app]` table** — `origin` — what `Core\Router::urlAbsolute` prepends when the mount states none — and `mode` are keys of the `[[app]]` block itself, read off every block matching the entry file and layered like any other directive, the… ([`config/origin-is-a-block-key-and-there-is-no-app-table`](rules/config.md#config-origin-is-a-block-key-and-there-is-no-app-table))
- **Every matching `[[app]]` block applies, least-specific `root` first, and two blocks on one canonical path are a duplicate** — More than one `[[app]]` can match one entry file, and all of them do. ([`config/every-matching-app-block-applies-least-specific-first`](rules/config.md#config-every-matching-app-block-applies-least-specific-first))
- **An `[[app]]` block may widen a limit or grant a capability up to the global ceiling, and may only lower its own ceiling** — `[app.limits]` sets any value for its application — wider or narrower than the global `[limits]` — up to the global `[limits.hard]` ceiling, and `[app.capabilities]` may **grant** a capability the global `[capabilities]… ([`config/an-app-block-may-widen-bounded-by-the-global-ceiling`](rules/config.md#config-an-app-block-may-widen-bounded-by-the-global-ceiling))
- **A `[[server.mount]]` routes and carries no `mode`; an `[[app]]` block sets policy** — `[[server.mount]]` carries no `mode` key, and one written there is refused as an unknown key (`E0601`). ([`config/a-mount-routes-and-an-app-block-sets-policy`](rules/config.md#config-a-mount-routes-and-an-app-block-sets-policy))
- **Scheduled work is a `[[schedule]]` entry firing a `spawn script`, checked at boot, with no runtime API** — Scheduled work is a `[[schedule]]` array-of-tables in `nvs.toml`, and nothing else: an entry names a `cron` expression and a `script`, and the server fires that file as an ordinary `spawn script` isolate (`security/isol… ([`config/scheduled-work-is-a-config-block`](rules/config.md#config-scheduled-work-is-a-config-block))
- **`cron` is five-field POSIX plus five named shorthands, parsed at boot with the line named** — The accepted dialect is **five-field POSIX cron** — minute, hour, day-of-month, month, day-of-week — plus exactly five named shorthands: `@hourly`, `@daily`, `@weekly`, `@monthly`, `@yearly`. ([`config/cron-is-five-fields-and-nothing-more`](rules/config.md#config-cron-is-five-fields-and-nothing-more))
- **`scope` is mandatory with no default, and `fleet` with no shared store refuses to boot** — Every `[[schedule]]` entry writes `scope`, and there is no default. ([`config/scope-has-no-default`](rules/config.md#config-scope-has-no-default))
- **Every `[[schedule]]` key is `System`, and not even `RuntimeTighten` reaches one** — Nothing in a `[[schedule]]` entry is changeable from inside a request, and there is no `Core\Config::set` path to any of it. ([`config/every-schedule-key-is-system`](rules/config.md#config-every-schedule-key-is-system))
- **An entry's `limits` and `grants` narrow the deployment's, and can never widen them** — An entry's optional `limits` table is a sub-cap on the run's budget, and its optional `grants` table narrows the run's capabilities. ([`config/a-schedule-entry-narrows-only`](rules/config.md#config-a-schedule-entry-narrows-only))
- **A scheduled run is a root isolate that spends a root's budget, and only `nvs serve` fires one** — An isolate spends its parent's budget (`security/isolate-budget-is-the-trees`). ([`config/a-scheduled-run-is-a-root-isolate`](rules/config.md#config-a-scheduled-run-is-a-root-isolate))
- **A `fleet` entry fires once per interval across the deployment under a lease in the shared store — at most once, never exactly once** — A `scope = "fleet"` entry fires once per interval across the deployment, guarded by a **lease** in the shared store keyed on the entry's `name` plus the fire's *scheduled* instant — not the instant it was noticed, so tw… ([`config/a-fleet-entry-fires-at-most-once-under-a-lease`](rules/config.md#config-a-fleet-entry-fires-at-most-once-under-a-lease))
- **`overlap` is `skip` by default, `queue` holds exactly one pending run, and `kill` cancels before it starts** — `overlap` decides what a fire does when the previous run of the **same entry** is still going, and the count it is asked of is that entry's own running fires — never a process-wide tally, or a nightly report could suppr… ([`config/overlap-is-skip-queue-or-kill`](rules/config.md#config-overlap-is-skip-queue-or-kill))
- **A missed fire is never caught up, `timezone` defaults to UTC, and a DST gap or repeat fires exactly once** — Every fire is computed from **now**, never counted from the entry's last fire, and that one choice is the whole implementation of three rules. ([`config/a-missed-fire-is-skipped-and-a-dst-edge-fires-once`](rules/config.md#config-a-missed-fire-is-skipped-and-a-dst-edge-fires-once))
- **A store an operator configured is authorized by the configuring — `cache.shared` is the grant, unscoped, and asks no address** — An endpoint an operator wrote into root-owned configuration is authorized **by that writing**, so the grant over it names the *store* and not a host. ([`config/cache-shared-is-the-grant-over-the-configured-store`](rules/config.md#config-cache-shared-is-the-grant-over-the-configured-store))
- **A Unix socket is admitted in `[cache.shared] url` and `[db.<name>] host`, and refused from any program-supplied endpoint** *(designed)* — `[cache.shared] url` and `[db.<name>] host` may name a Unix domain socket. ([`config/a-unix-socket-is-admitted-only-where-an-operator-wrote-it`](rules/config.md#config-a-unix-socket-is-admitted-only-where-an-operator-wrote-it))
- **A socket is `unix:` where the key is a URL and a bare absolute path where the key is a host** *(designed)* — Two spellings because the two keys are two different things, and each takes the one that reads as itself. ([`config/unix-scheme-in-a-url-and-a-bare-path-in-a-host`](rules/config.md#config-unix-scheme-in-a-url-and-a-bare-path-in-a-host))
- **A Unix spelling on a build with no `AF_UNIX` transport is refused at boot, never read as loopback TCP** *(designed)* — A Unix spelling on a platform this build has no Unix transport for is refused **where the key was written**, at boot, with a note naming the platform and pointing at loopback TCP. ([`config/a-unix-spelling-with-no-af-unix-transport-refuses-at-boot`](rules/config.md#config-a-unix-spelling-with-no-af-unix-transport-refuses-at-boot))
- **A program-supplied socket path needs `net.local`, a path-scoped grant carrying no address policy and governing both ends** — A program that supplies a socket path — connecting to one or binding one — needs `net.local`, a capability **separate** from `net.connect`, asked at `Scope::Path` under `security/path-scope-canonicalise-then-prefix`, wh… ([`config/net-local-is-named-and-not-on-the-roster`](rules/config.md#config-net-local-is-named-and-not-on-the-roster))
- **The extension set is folded into one `env_hash` that both compiled-unit cache keys carry, so an extension change is an ordinary cache miss** — One `env_hash` is carried by **both** compiled-unit caches: the on-disk key is `BLAKE3(content_hash ‖ env_hash)`, and the in-memory key is `UnitKey { path, content_hash, env_hash }`. ([`config/the-extension-set-is-in-every-unit-key`](rules/config.md#config-the-extension-set-is-in-every-unit-key))
- **`opcache.validate` and its rate cap are `System`, and `validate`'s startup default is chosen by the run mode** — `opcache.validate` — `never`, `mtime` or `hash` — and `opcache.revalidate_freq` are `System`-class: a request cannot loosen how often, or whether, the process re-checks source files. ([`config/opcache-revalidation-is-system-class`](rules/config.md#config-opcache-revalidation-is-system-class))
- **The five `opcache.file_cache*` directives are `System`-class, because where compiled code is read from is a code-injection primitive** — The on-disk artifact cache is governed by five directives in `[opcache]`: `file_cache` (bool, default on), `file_cache_dir` (a path, root-owned, defaulting to a fixed location inside the account running the compile), `f… ([`config/opcache-file-cache-directives-are-system`](rules/config.md#config-opcache-file-cache-directives-are-system))
- **The update-check and telemetry endpoints are compiled-in defaults overridable by `NVS_UPDATE_URL` and `NVS_TELEMETRY_URL`** *(designed)* — The update-check URL and the telemetry upload URL have compiled-in defaults, overridable by environment variable: `NVS_UPDATE_URL` and `NVS_TELEMETRY_URL`. ([`config/telemetry-and-update-endpoints-are-configuration`](rules/config.md#config-telemetry-and-update-endpoints-are-configuration))

## Packaging

- **A compiled unit is one immutable file whose address is its content and its environment** — The on-disk artifact cache is a fan-out directory of immutable files, one per compiled unit:… ([`packaging/an-artifact-is-one-immutable-content-addressed-file`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-an-artifact-is-one-immutable-content-addressed-file))
- **An artifact is a self-describing header over one relocatable object, and it carries no class metadata** — Every artifact file is a fixed header followed by its payload:… ([`packaging/an-artifact-is-a-relocatable-object-behind-a-self-describing-header`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-an-artifact-is-a-relocatable-object-behind-a-self-describing-header))
- **A compiled-unit cache entry is read into memory, never mapped** *(designed)* — The compiled-unit cache is **read into memory**, never mapped. ([`packaging/the-artifact-cache-is-read-not-mapped`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-artifact-cache-is-read-not-mapped))
- **A warm hit skips codegen and nothing else, and it must beat the compile it replaces** — A warm hit parses, checks and lowers the same source in full; only the Cranelift walk and the pages it would have produced come off the disk instead. ([`packaging/a-warm-hit-skips-codegen-not-the-front-end`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-warm-hit-skips-codegen-not-the-front-end))
- **An artifact is hashed in full where it lies, then placed, relocated and only then made executable** — A reader `mmap`s the file read-only, never starting from an executable mapping. ([`packaging/an-artifact-is-verified-whole-before-a-page-is-executable`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-an-artifact-is-verified-whole-before-a-page-is-executable))
- **The checksum answers corruption; a cache directory another account can write is refused at startup** — The header checksum defends against **corruption**: truncation, bit rot, an interrupted write that landed at a final path by bypassing the runtime's own writer. ([`packaging/the-checksum-proves-integrity-and-ownership-proves-trust`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-checksum-proves-integrity-and-ownership-proves-trust))
- **A bad cache entry is a miss the script never sees, and only a corrupt one is deleted** — No failure on the cache path reaches a panic, a `FATAL` or a `Throwable`. ([`packaging/a-bad-cache-entry-is-a-miss-never-an-error`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-bad-cache-entry-is-a-miss-never-an-error))
- **A writer publishes by one atomic rename, and a path that already exists wins** — A writer compiles, writes header and payload to `<cache_dir>/<key[0:2]>/.tmp-<random>` in the shard directory the final name lives in, `fsync`s the temp file, and does one `rename` onto `<key[2:]>.nvsc`. ([`packaging/a-writer-publishes-by-one-atomic-rename-and-never-a-lock`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-writer-publishes-by-one-atomic-rename-and-never-a-lock))
- **Eviction rides the cold miss at a configured probability, and a warm hit pays nothing for it** — A content-addressed entry never needs invalidating for correctness, only for growth: the key covers every input to a compile, so changing any of them produces ordinary misses and no invalidation pass exists. ([`packaging/eviction-rides-the-cold-miss-at-a-probability`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-eviction-rides-the-cold-miss-at-a-probability))
- **`nvs cache gc` and `nvs cache clear` are the operator's deterministic alternative to the roll** *(designed)* — An operator wanting deterministic control instead of a probability gets two explicit commands. ([`packaging/nvs-cache-gc-and-clear-are-the-deterministic-escape`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-nvs-cache-gc-and-clear-are-the-deterministic-escape))
- **A unit's cache key covers every autoload path it probed, misses included, and every directory a discovery query listed** *(designed)* — Plain `autoload` (`programs/autoload`) adds no new dependency kind to the artifact cache, with one exception. ([`packaging/autoload-probes-fold-into-the-cache-key`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-autoload-probes-fold-into-the-cache-key))
- **A compiled extension module is cached in the same store, under the same key, header and verify shape** *(designed)* — A compiled extension module is cached in the same store as a compiled unit, not in a second cache of its own. ([`packaging/a-wasm-module-cache-reuses-the-artifact-cache`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-wasm-module-cache-reuses-the-artifact-cache))
- **`nvs build --compile` appends a program to a copy of the `nvs` binary, and rebundling is running it again** — `nvs build --compile entry.nvs -o app[.exe]` produces a portable single-file executable. ([`packaging/nvs-build-compile-appends-the-program-to-a-copy-of-the-host`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-nvs-build-compile-appends-the-program-to-a-copy-of-the-host))
- **A bundle's payload is source, as a flat file list with no archive and no compression** — The embedded payload is the entry file's `.nvs` source plus every file its `require` graph statically resolves to, laid out as a flat list of `(relative_path, length, bytes)` entries, entry first — no archive format and… ([`packaging/a-bundle-carries-source-not-artifacts`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-bundle-carries-source-not-artifacts))
- **Inside a closed-world target every `require` resolves at build time, and one that cannot fails the build** — A closed-world target has no filesystem to fall back on at run time: a bundled executable's payload is exactly what got embedded and nothing more. ([`packaging/a-bundled-require-resolves-at-build-time`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-bundled-require-resolves-at-build-time))
- **A bundle is recognised by a footer the host reads before it parses one argument** — The build command appends, after the host binary's own last section, the flat file list followed by a fixed-size footer:… ([`packaging/a-bundle-is-found-by-its-footer-before-argv-is-read`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-bundle-is-found-by-its-footer-before-argv-is-read))
- **`nvs build --compile` packages what is already resolved on disk and fetches no dependency** — `nvs build --compile` packages what is already resolved and present on disk, and nothing else. ([`packaging/build-compile-packages-what-is-on-disk-and-resolves-nothing`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-build-compile-packages-what-is-on-disk-and-resolves-nothing))
- **A `.nvsx` the program depends on is embedded as one opaque entry of the same flat list** *(designed)* — A Tier 1 extension is one wasm component, portable across every target Novis ships for. ([`packaging/a-nvsx-dependency-embeds-in-the-same-payload`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-nvsx-dependency-embeds-in-the-same-payload))
- **A macOS bundle is ad-hoc signed by the build command; PE and ELF need no step** — Appending bytes after an already-signed Mach-O invalidates its signature. ([`packaging/a-macos-bundle-is-ad-hoc-signed-at-build`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-macos-bundle-is-ad-hoc-signed-at-build))
- **A build records its target, host, profile, compiler, commit and the commit's own date, and never a build date** — `build.rs` records the target, the host, the profile, `rustc --version`, the Cranelift version from `Cargo.lock`, the commit and the commit's own committer date — and no build date. ([`packaging/a-build-records-no-timestamp`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-build-records-no-timestamp))
- **`nvs --help` opens with the README's own title and the version, commit and commit date of the build answering** — `nvs --help` opens with two lines and no third:… ([`packaging/the-banner-states-the-build`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-banner-states-the-build))
- **The third-party notice is generated from the dependency graph, fails closed, and is never written by hand** — Novis is MIT and links some eighty permissive components, every one of which conditions redistribution on reproducing something — MIT and BSD the copyright line and the license text, Apache-2.0 additionally its `NOTICE`… ([`packaging/the-third-party-notice-is-generated-never-written-by-hand`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-third-party-notice-is-generated-never-written-by-hand))
- **The notice and Novis's own license are compiled into the binary from the same tree** — `crates/nvs-cli/src/info.rs` embeds `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt` and `LICENSE` with `include_str!`, so the notice and the binary it describes are produced from one tree in one compile and cannot drift. ([`packaging/the-notice-is-embedded-in-the-binary`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-notice-is-embedded-in-the-binary))
- **No flag on `nvs` is inherited from PHP; `-h` and `-V` are the Unix baseline and `-o` the only short flag Novis declares** — semantics on purpose; the command line is not semantics, and a spelling inherited there buys a PHP developer one familiar keystroke and charges every reader of `--help` for it afterwards. ([`packaging/the-cli-surface-is-novis-own`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-cli-surface-is-novis-own))
- **A doc comment clap renders is written for the person reading `--help`, and cites nothing they cannot open** — Every doc comment clap renders — a subcommand's, a nested subcommand's, an argument's — is text a person reads in `nvs --help`, and it is written for that person and nobody else. ([`packaging/help-text-speaks-to-its-reader`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-help-text-speaks-to-its-reader))
- **`nvs info` is the one call for build, host and licensing facts, and the one spelling of it** — "What is this binary, what is in it, and what may I do with it?" is one question asked by one person at one moment, so it is one call. ([`packaging/nvs-info-is-the-one-call`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-nvs-info-is-the-one-call))
- **A package name is `vendor/name`, lowercase ASCII compared exactly, and `nvs` is reserved for first-party packages** *(designed)* — A package name is **`vendor/name`**: both segments lowercase ASCII with `-` permitted, and compared… ([`packaging/a-package-name-is-vendor-slash-name`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-package-name-is-vendor-slash-name))
- **A package is an immutable source archive whose identity is its BLAKE3 digest** *(designed)* — A package's **identity is the BLAKE3 digest of its archive** — the hash the artifact cache already uses, so the toolchain carries no second one. ([`packaging/a-package-is-its-digest`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-package-is-its-digest))
- **`package.toml` is read by the `nvs` CLI, never by the runtime and never by name resolution** *(designed)* — The rejection of "a manifest file found by walking up from the entry file" (`programs/no-runtime-autoload`) stands, and so does `config/nvs-toml-is-not-a-project-manifest`. ([`packaging/package-toml-is-a-tool-input`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-package-toml-is-a-tool-input))
- **Every file in a fetched package declares a namespace under the prefix its manifest claims, and two packages claiming one prefix is a fetch error naming both** *(designed)* — Authority is looked up by the enclosing namespace alone (`security/authority-is-the-enclosing-namespace`), and keying on a self-declared attribute would be worthless if a package could declare any attribute it liked. ([`packaging/a-package-file-stays-under-its-declared-prefix`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-package-file-stays-under-its-declared-prefix))
- **A fetched package is reached by an ordinary `autoload` line in a committed, generated `vendor/packages.nvs`** *(designed)* — `nvs fetch` materialises the graph under `vendor/` and writes **one generated Novis source file**, `vendor/packages.nvs`, containing nothing but ordinary declarations:… ([`packaging/a-fetched-package-is-an-autoload-line`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-fetched-package-is-an-autoload-line))
- **Nothing in a package runs before your program does** *(designed)* — no point in the fetch, resolve, verify or compile pipeline at which a package's code executes. ([`packaging/nothing-runs-before-the-program`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-nothing-runs-before-the-program))
- **A package ships no `nvs.toml`, and none of its `require` or `autoload` paths reaches outside its own directory** *(designed)* — Two things a package may not do to the tree it lands in. ([`packaging/a-package-cannot-reach-its-host`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-package-cannot-reach-its-host))
- **Resolution selects the highest minimum any package asked for, and nothing upgrades itself** *(designed)* — Every dependency names the **minimum version** it needs. ([`packaging/resolution-takes-the-highest-minimum`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-resolution-takes-the-highest-minimum))
- **`package.lock` records every package's digest, a mismatch is a hard error, and `--locked` fetches nothing the lock does not name** *(designed)* — selected version, source and digest. ([`packaging/the-lockfile-holds-every-digest`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-lockfile-holds-every-digest))
- **A git dependency pins an exact commit, and only the root application may declare one** *(designed)* — Two kinds of source produce a package's digest, and only one of them is transitive. ([`packaging/a-git-dependency-is-root-only`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-git-dependency-is-root-only))
- **The registry publishes an append-only transparency log, and a client verifies inclusion and consistency before using an artifact** *(designed)* — The registry publishes an **append-only transparency log** of `name → version → digest`: a Merkle tree with signed checkpoints. ([`packaging/the-registry-keeps-an-append-only-log`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-registry-keeps-an-append-only-log))
- **`nvs publish` uploads a clean-checkout archive, and the registry never overwrites a published `name@version`** *(designed)* — `nvs publish` uploads a source archive built from a **clean checkout**. ([`packaging/publishing-never-overwrites`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-publishing-never-overwrites))
- **A known-bad version is retracted, never deleted, and `nvs audit` names the minimum bump that clears it** *(designed)* — A publisher marks a version **retracted** with a reason and a fixed-in version. ([`packaging/a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted))
- **A package that breaks its API publishes under a new name carrying `supersedes`** *(designed)* — A package that breaks its API **publishes under a new name** — conventionally the old name with a numeric suffix, `acme/http` → `acme/http2` — carrying `supersedes = "acme/http"` so that `nvs outdated` and `nvs audit` c… ([`packaging/a-breaking-release-is-a-new-name`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-breaking-release-is-a-new-name))
- **Until 0.1.0 ships any dependency updates at any time, and the version contract starts with the commit that tags 0.1.0** — Two regimes, and the tree is in the first. ([`packaging/the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0))
- **A version number describes the enumerated surface, and the Rust crate APIs, the artifact cache, diagnostic prose and MSRV carry no promise** *(designed)* — A version number is meaningless unless the thing it describes is listed. ([`packaging/the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated))
- **One `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` for the whole workspace, and below 1.0 the breaking slot moves left** — `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, **one number for the whole workspace**, and the number `nvs --version` prints… ([`packaging/below-1-0-the-breaking-slot-moves-left`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-below-1-0-the-breaking-slot-moves-left))
- **A change a dependency forced ships as a patch, a minor or a major by who can see it, never by how big the diff was** *(designed)* — One question classifies a change a dependency forced: **who can see it?** Not how big the diff was, not how many crates moved. ([`packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot))
- **A dependency break that a program author could see goes down a seven-step ladder, and shipping it is the last step** *(designed)* — A dependency change that would land in the last rows of `packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot` does not go there directly. ([`packaging/a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded))
- **A forced user-facing break survives one minor release as a warning naming its replacement, and is removed in the next major** *(designed)* — Where a deprecation cycle is possible — meaning the old and new behaviour can coexist for one release — the old spelling survives one **minor** release emitting a **compiler warning that names its replacement**, and is… ([`packaging/a-forced-break-is-announced-before-it-lands`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-forced-break-is-announced-before-it-lands))
- **A dependency move never fixes a guard test by editing its threshold, and it regenerates the attribution file in the same commit** — The dependency sweep re-runs a battery whose full order and conditional legs are the sweep procedure's to state. ([`packaging/a-dependency-move-proves-two-things`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-dependency-move-proves-two-things))
- **Each dependency bump is its own commit, classified in its message** — Each dependency — or one coherent group that genuinely must move together, such as the `cranelift-*` crates — gets **its own commit**, with its classification from `packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot` in… ([`packaging/one-bump-one-commit`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-one-bump-one-commit))
- **Being current has a schedule, a stale dependency is a defect, and a human fires every pass — never an agent, cron or CI** — Being current is a standing obligation, so it has a schedule. ([`packaging/the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human))
- **A third-party extension is a sandboxed WebAssembly component, never a shared library loaded with `dlopen`** *(designed)* — Third-party code is added to a running Novis as a **WebAssembly component** — a `.nvsx` file — and never as a native shared library. ([`packaging/an-extension-is-a-sandboxed-wasm-component`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-an-extension-is-a-sandboxed-wasm-component))
- **Library and extension code sits at one of three tiers: built-in, sandboxed component, or statically linked native** *(designed)* — Library and extension code lives at one of three tiers, and each exists because it is the right answer for a different class of code:… ([`packaging/three-tiers`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-three-tiers))
- **A `.nvsx` is a single WebAssembly component whose manifest is an `nvs.manifest` custom section** *(designed)* — A `.nvsx` is **one file**: a WebAssembly component implementing the versioned world `nvs:ext@1.0.0`, with an `nvs.manifest` custom section inside it. ([`packaging/an-nvsx-is-one-file-carrying-its-manifest`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-an-nvsx-is-one-file-carrying-its-manifest))
- **An extension package may carry Novis source beside its `.nvsx`, under one namespace, and the component's manifest registers exactly one class** *(designed)* — An extension package may carry **two payloads**: the `.nvsx` wasm component, and Novis source that composes calls into it. ([`packaging/an-extension-package-carries-two-payloads`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-an-extension-package-carries-two-payloads))
- **An extension loads only from an `[[extension]]` entry in the root-owned `nvs.toml`, pinned by its `sha256`** *(designed)* — An extension is loaded from an `[[extension]]` entry in the root-owned `nvs.toml`, and from nowhere else:… ([`packaging/extension-loading-is-root-controlled`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-extension-loading-is-root-controlled))
- **An extension's classes are registered from its manifest at load, and a call into one is type-checked at compile time and emitted as a direct call** *(designed)* — At load the host reads an extension's manifest — its declared classes, their `static` methods and `const` members, and any `nvs.toml` directives it contributes — and registers them into the compiler's symbol table. ([`packaging/extension-calls-are-statically-typed`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-extension-calls-are-statically-typed))
- **A value crosses the guest boundary as a bounds-checked handle, never as a pointer** *(designed)* — Novis values stay in the host heap. ([`packaging/values-cross-as-handles`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-values-cross-as-handles))
- **A guest is instantiated fresh for each request that calls it, so extension state cannot leak between requests** *(designed)* — Each request that calls an extension gets a **pristine instance** of it, created lazily on first use. ([`packaging/a-fresh-instance-per-request`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-fresh-instance-per-request))
- **A guest runs under the request's CPU and memory caps, and a runaway guest traps rather than hanging a core** *(designed)* — Guest execution is tied to the request's own limits. ([`packaging/a-guest-runs-under-the-requests-budget`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-guest-runs-under-the-requests-budget))
- **A guest has no ambient authority: WASI is not granted by default, and every host function it receives is capability-checked** *(designed)* — WASI is **not** granted to a guest by default. ([`packaging/a-guest-has-no-ambient-authority`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-guest-has-no-ambient-authority))
- **An extension call costs a fixed ten-odd nanoseconds over a built-in call, so an extension's API is coarse-grained** *(designed)* — Measured in a release build: a host-to-guest call costs about 11.5 ns, a guest-to-host accessor call about 9 ns, a 1 KiB bulk copy into guest memory about 12 ns, and a fresh pooled instance plus one call about 8 µs. ([`packaging/the-boundary-is-the-cost`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-boundary-is-the-cost))
- **A C dependency is admitted under ordinary audit only if attacker-controlled data never reaches it; otherwise it needs an exceptional verification record or is confined to wasm** — "Pure Rust by default, deviations argued individually" is a standing test rather than a case-by-case argument, so the answer does not depend on who argues it:… ([`packaging/a-c-dependency-answers-two-questions`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-c-dependency-answers-two-questions))
- **PDF is a decode-only format of `nvs/image`, in the second wave, and never a member of `nvs/pdf`** *(designed)* — PDF joins the image component's format roster **decode only**, in the second wave beside SVG, with `Format` gaining a `Pdf` case and no new entry point: the plan/terminal shape and the component's closed set of exports… ([`packaging/pdf-decoding-ships-in-the-image-package`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-pdf-decoding-ships-in-the-image-package))
- **`nvs service` is a namespace, and everything after a mandatory `--` is stored verbatim as the argv the service runs** — A service is this binary, registered with the platform's service manager, running **one stored argv**. ([`packaging/a-service-is-one-stored-argv`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-service-is-one-stored-argv))
- **The service installer fails closed: a closed `serve`/`run` allowlist, no relative path, no argv without `--config`, no install whose output goes nowhere, no password on a command line** — The trailing argv is the sharpest sink in the project (`security/sink-predicate`): the command runs elevated, and what it stores is executed by a privileged account at every boot until somebody removes it. ([`packaging/the-installer-is-a-sink`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-installer-is-a-sink))
- **On Windows the argv is encoded into the SCM's one `ImagePath` string, the binary path is always quoted, and nothing else holds it** *(designed)* — The Windows SCM stores **one string**, and the process gets it back through `CommandLineToArgvW`. ([`packaging/the-argv-lives-in-imagepath`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-argv-lives-in-imagepath))
- **A service's default identity is the per-service virtual account `NT SERVICE\<name>`, and `LocalSystem` is never the default** *(designed)* — The default identity is `NT SERVICE\<name>` — a virtual account the SCM creates and owns, with a per-service SID, no password to rotate or leak, and no interactive logon. ([`packaging/a-service-runs-as-a-virtual-account`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-service-runs-as-a-virtual-account))
- **A stop drains, a `PARAMCHANGE` reloads, and lifecycle records go to the event log beside the configured log destination** — A hosted server answers its service manager with the operations it already has, rather than a shim reporting what it can see from outside:… ([`packaging/a-service-answers-its-manager`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-service-answers-its-manager))
- **On Linux `nvs service unit` prints the systemd unit and touches nothing; writing it is an explicit `--install`** — `nvs service unit <name> -- serve --config …` writes a systemd unit to stdout and touches nothing. ([`packaging/the-unit-is-printed-and-install-is-the-opt-in`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-unit-is-printed-and-install-is-the-opt-in))
- **The generated unit carries the hardening block, `Type=notify`, `MemoryMax` from `[limits]`, and `AmbientCapabilities` only for a privileged port** *(designed)* — The generated unit carries what a hand-written one usually does not:… ([`packaging/the-generated-unit-is-hardened`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-generated-unit-is-hardened))
- **A single-file bundle may not install itself as a service** — `nvs service install` refuses when the running binary is a single-file bundle, with a diagnostic (`E0634`) naming the reason. ([`packaging/a-bundle-may-not-install-itself`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-bundle-may-not-install-itself))
- **There is no `Core\Service`: only an operator installs a service, from the command line, and nothing about it is on the request path** — There is no `Core\Service`, no new grammar, no runtime change and nothing on the request path. ([`packaging/a-service-is-operator-surface`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-service-is-operator-surface))

## Migrating from PHP

- **Every departure from PHP's observable behaviour is listed as a divergence, and each exists only because PHP left a binding untyped** — PHP-compatible observable behaviour is the second priority, so a departure from it is never discovered later: every one is listed, PHP's behaviour beside Novis's. ([`php-migration/every-divergence-is-deliberate-and-listed`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-every-divergence-is-deliberate-and-listed))
- **`->` on a receiver that can hold no object is refused where it is written** — `$i->name` where `$i` is declared `int` is refused where it is written (`E0495`); PHP warns *"Attempt to read property"* and yields `null`. ([`php-migration/a-declared-type-answers-before-the-program-runs`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-a-declared-type-answers-before-the-program-runs))
- **Absent storage never reads as a zero value: an unassigned variable and `[]` in a read position are refused, and an absent key throws** — PHP fills a hole with a zero value and warns. ([`php-migration/absent-storage-is-never-a-zero-value`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-absent-storage-is-never-a-zero-value))
- **An element write through a temporary is refused, because the separated copy has nowhere to be written back** — Copy-on-write separates the array before the element is written, and the separated copy has to land back in whatever held the array. ([`php-migration/an-element-write-needs-storage-to-write-back-into`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-an-element-write-needs-storage-to-write-back-into))
- **A non-`void` body hands back a value at every exit; nothing returns `null` for a declaration it did not make** — In PHP a function declared `: int` whose body reaches its own end returns `null`, whatever it declared. ([`php-migration/a-body-never-falls-off-its-end`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-a-body-never-falls-off-its-end))
- **A `return` never leaves a `finally` block, and neither does a `break` or `continue` whose target lies outside it** *(designed)* — `return` inside `finally` does not compile. ([`php-migration/no-return-leaves-a-finally`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-no-return-leaves-a-finally))
- **A constructor's `return` carries no value; a bare `return;` may still leave early** *(designed)* — `return $value;` inside a `constructor` does not compile: the object under construction is the result, and nothing else can be. ([`php-migration/a-constructor-return-carries-no-value`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-a-constructor-return-carries-no-value))
- **A `readonly` property declares no default; a value known at the declaration is a `const`** *(designed)* — `readonly` with an initializer is refused where it is written. ([`php-migration/a-readonly-property-declares-no-default`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-a-readonly-property-declares-no-default))
- **Partial function application is not adopted; the closure literal already spells it** — `f(?, $x)` and every application-with-holes shape do not parse. ([`php-migration/no-partial-application`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-no-partial-application))
- **`let` and `is` cannot name anything; `var` declares, `as` converts, and `is` is the type test** *(designed)* — Neither `let` nor `is` may name a class, interface, trait, enum, constant, function or parameter. ([`php-migration/let-and-is-are-reserved`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-let-and-is-are-reserved))
- **`instanceof` is refused where it is written, `is` is the one type test, and neither keyword is compared with PHP again** — Novis has one type test, `$x is T`, and `instanceof` is refused where it is written: the diagnostic names the rewrite — *write `$x is Request`; a class reference on the right is `$x is $cls`* — and the converter perform… ([`php-migration/one-type-test`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-one-type-test))
- **What PHP deprecates for removal is refused at compile time, never phased in behind a warning** *(designed)* — Novis compiles, and it has no deprecation channel. ([`php-migration/a-deprecation-is-a-refusal`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-a-deprecation-is-a-refusal))
- **`nvs convert` turns a stateless trait into an interface with defaults and a stateful one into a delegate, and names what it cannot decide** *(designed)* — Every PHP trait shape maps to one of five outcomes. ([`php-migration/a-trait-converts-to-an-interface-or-a-delegate`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-a-trait-converts-to-an-interface-or-a-delegate))
- **`nvs convert` maps every PHP shell-execution call to `Core\Process` and flags each site, because a command string has no argv split** *(designed)* — `exec($cmd)`, `system($cmd)`, `` `cmd` `` and `shell_exec($cmd)` map to `Core\Process::run($path, $argv)` (`core-classes/process-run`). ([`php-migration/a-shell-call-converts-to-process-under-review`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-a-shell-call-converts-to-process-under-review))
- **A session id the store did not issue is rejected, always, with no toggle** *(designed)* — `Core\Session::start()` accepts a presented id only if its own store issued it and it is still live. ([`php-migration/a-session-id-the-store-did-not-issue-is-rejected`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-a-session-id-the-store-did-not-issue-is-rejected))
- **The PHP-name layer is joined once at build time, and a destination spelling the registry cannot place fails the build** *(designed)* — The inventory, the migration table and the `Core` registry are joined once, at build time, into a static sorted table compiled into the language server. ([`php-migration/the-php-name-layer-is-joined-at-build-time`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-the-php-name-layer-is-joined-at-build-time))
- **Every PHP built-in name is a completion candidate, and the migration table is what the item says** *(designed)* — Every function and type name in the PHP inventory — `tools/data/php-builtins.txt`, generated from the same PHP build the differential suite uses as its oracle — is a completion candidate from the day the layer ships. ([`php-migration/every-php-builtin-is-a-completion-candidate`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-every-php-builtin-is-a-completion-candidate))
- **A PHP-name completion item inserts only a `Core` member the registry already holds** *(designed)* — A PHP-name item may insert text only when its destination resolves — a `Core` member that `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs` actually holds, the same table `nvs-types` seeds its signatures from, so *resolves* means her… ([`php-migration/an-item-inserts-only-a-registered-member`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-an-item-inserts-only-a-registered-member))
- **A PHP name completes only where a top-level identifier is legal, and sorts below every Novis symbol** *(designed)* — A PHP-name item appears only where a top-level identifier is legal. ([`php-migration/a-php-name-sorts-below-every-novis-symbol`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-a-php-name-sorts-below-every-novis-symbol))
- **`nvs.completion.phpNames` quiets or removes the PHP-name layer, and never touches `Core` completion** *(designed)* — `nvs.completion.phpNames` takes `all` (the default), `resolved` or `off`. ([`php-migration/completion-php-names-setting`](rules/php-migration.md#php-migration-completion-php-names-setting))
